1"""
2dist_m4ri.py: Python wrapper for the multithreaded dist_m4ri distance calculator.
3
4Provides high-level APIs for computing:
5- Classical code distance: compute_classical_distance(...)
6- Single-sided quantum code distance: compute_quantum_distance(...)
7- CSS quantum code distance: compute_css_distance(...)
8- Detector Error Model (DEM) distance: compute_dem_distance(...)
9- Certified lower bound on the distance of a Stim memory circuit from its code-sized model:
10 compute_model_lower_bound(...)
11
12Supports distance caching, codeword export, and fallback/option for the codedistance library.
13Since dist_m4ri natively handles multithreading (via POSIX threads and dynamic bracketing),
14no Python-level threading or subprocess-per-core logic is necessary.
15"""

41# Debug bitmap (debug=N): bits 1..32768 are passed to the dist_m4ri binary (1: summary, 2: progress, 4: periodic
42# status, 8: thread allocation and timing, 16: code parameters, 32: codeword supports, 64: arguments, 128: matrices,
43# 256: codeword dump, 2048: no size cutoff; see its --morehelp), the higher bits are used by the Python wrapper only.
44PY_DBG_COMMANDS = 1 << 16 # echo the dist_m4ri command lines and their run times
45PY_DBG_CACHE = 1 << 17 # cache messages
46PY_DBG_CIRCUITS = 1 << 18 # Stim circuit to DEM conversion details
47PY_DBG_KEEP_FILES = 1 << 19 # keep (and list) the temporary matrix, codeword, and DEM files
48BIN_DBG_MASK = 0xFFFF # the debug bits passed to the dist_m4ri binary
49VERBOSE_DEBUG = 3 | PY_DBG_COMMANDS | PY_DBG_CACHE # debug bits implied by verbose=True (--verbose)

52def parse_debug_value(val: Union[str, int]) -> int:
53 """
54 Parses a debug bitmap value: a non-negative decimal or hexadecimal (0x...) integer, as in the dist_m4ri binary
55 (no octal: leading zeros are ignored).
56
57 Args:
58 val: The value, e.g., "3" or "0x10004", or an int.
59
60 Returns:
61 The debug bitmap.
62
63 Raises:
64 ValueError: If the value is not a non-negative integer.
65 """
66 msg = f"invalid debug={val!r}: expected a non-negative decimal or hexadecimal (0x...) integer"
67 if isinstance(val, bool):
68 raise ValueError(msg)
69 if isinstance(val, int):
70 value = val
71 else:
72 s = str(val).strip()
73 try:
74 value = int(s[2:], 16) if s.lower().startswith("0x") else int(s, 10)
75 except ValueError:
76 raise ValueError(msg) from None
77 if value < 0:
78 raise ValueError(msg)
79 return value

106# qec_cert (engine='cert' and 'auto'): since version 0.17.2, a single probe per process imports it and loads its native
107# library libqeccert.so (which qec_cert itself loads only inside a certification), see _probe_qec_cert().
108_qec_cert_status: Optional[str] = None # None: not probed yet; "": usable; otherwise why not (one line)
109_qec_cert_missing = False # the probe found no qec_cert package at all (not installed)
110_qec_cert_warned = False # engine='auto' has written its warning on a qec_cert which is not usable
111_QEC_CERT_REMEDY = ("build qec-cert (make) and pip install -e it, or set QEC_CERT_LIB to its libqeccert.so and "
112 "PYTHONPATH to its repository")
113
114
115def _probe_qec_cert() -> str:
116 """
117 Imports qec_cert (its modules io and pipeline) and loads its native library libqeccert.so with qec_cert._lib.load()
118 (since version 0.17.2), once per process: the result is memoized.
119
120 Returns:
121 "" if qec_cert is usable (then _get_qec_cert() returns its modules), otherwise the reason on one line, with
122 the remedy.
123 """
124 global _qec_cert_mod, _qec_cert_status, _qec_cert_missing
125 if _qec_cert_mod is not None:
126 return ""
127 if _qec_cert_status is not None:
128 return _qec_cert_status
129 try:
130 import qec_cert
131 from qec_cert import io as _qec_io, pipeline as _qec_pipeline
132 except Exception as e: # (ImportError, or an error inside its import)
133 _qec_cert_missing = isinstance(e, ModuleNotFoundError) and e.name == "qec_cert"
134 why = "is not installed" if _qec_cert_missing else f"cannot be imported ({type(e).__name__}: {e})"
135 _qec_cert_status = f"qec_cert {why}: {_QEC_CERT_REMEDY}"
136 return _qec_cert_status
137 try:
138 from qec_cert import _lib as _qec_lib
139 except ImportError: # (a version without the loader: the library is loaded by its first certification)
140 _qec_lib = None
141 try:
142 if _qec_lib is not None:
143 _qec_lib.load()
144 except Exception as e: # (qec_cert._lib.LibraryNotFound, an OSError, or a library which cannot be used)
145 _qec_cert_status = (f"qec_cert cannot load its library libqeccert.so ({type(e).__name__}: {e}): "
146 f"{_QEC_CERT_REMEDY}")
147 return _qec_cert_status
148 _qec_cert_mod = (qec_cert, _qec_io, _qec_pipeline)
149 _qec_cert_status = ""
150 return ""
151

172def _qec_cert_lib_found(spec: Any) -> bool:
173 """
174 Whether the library libqeccert.so of the qec_cert package found by importlib.util.find_spec (spec) is where
175 qec_cert looks for it (qec_cert/_lib.py: the file QEC_CERT_LIB, otherwise libqeccert.so next to the package or in
176 build/ of its repository), without importing qec_cert.
177 """
178 env = os.environ.get("QEC_CERT_LIB")
179 if env:
180 return os.path.isfile(env)
181 origin = getattr(spec, "origin", None)
182 if not origin or not os.path.isfile(origin):
183 return False
184 pkg = Path(origin).resolve().parent
185 return (pkg / "libqeccert.so").is_file() or (pkg.parent / "build" / "libqeccert.so").is_file()
186

188def _qec_cert_available() -> bool:
189 """
190 engine='auto': whether qec_cert is usable, without importing it if this can be avoided (the import takes about
191 0.6 s, and Stage A of engine='auto' often answers alone, see _auto_two_stage()): the memoized result of
192 _probe_qec_cert() once it has run; otherwise False if qec_cert cannot be found (importlib.util.find_spec), True if
193 its library libqeccert.so is found where qec_cert looks for it (see _qec_cert_lib_found()), and otherwise the
194 result of the probe, which then runs at once.
195 """
196 if _qec_cert_mod is not None:
197 return True
198 if _qec_cert_status is not None:
199 return _qec_cert_status == ""
200 try:
201 import importlib.util
202 spec = importlib.util.find_spec("qec_cert")
203 except Exception: # (ValueError for a module without __spec__, ...)
204 return False
205 if spec is None:
206 return False
207 if _qec_cert_lib_found(spec):
208 return True
209 return _probe_qec_cert() == ""

212def _auto_qec_cert_unusable_reason(fallback: str = "dist_m4ri with the whole timeout") -> str:
213 """
214 engine='auto' without a usable qec_cert: the reason recorded in _last_run_stats["engine_auto"]. If qec_cert is
215 installed but not usable (see _probe_qec_cert()), a warning is written to stderr, once per process.
216 """
217 global _qec_cert_warned
218 if not _qec_cert_status or _qec_cert_missing:
219 return f"qec_cert is not installed: {fallback}"
220 if not _qec_cert_warned:
221 _qec_cert_warned = True
222 sys.stderr.write(f"# Warning: engine='auto': {_qec_cert_status}; {fallback} (written once)\n")
223 return f"qec_cert is not usable: {fallback}"

230def _is_tropidist_root(path: Union[str, Path]) -> bool:

232 p = Path(path)

236def find_tropidist_root(tropidist_root: Optional[Union[str, Path]] = None) -> Optional[str]:
237 """
238 Locates a `tropidist` repository checkout runnable via `python -m cdist`.
239
240 Checks in order:
241 1. Explicit `tropidist_root` argument, if provided.
242 2. The `TROPIDIST_ROOT` environment variable.
243 3. An importable `cdist` package on `sys.path` (`importlib.util.find_spec("cdist")`), taking its repository root.
244
245 Returns:
246 Absolute path string to the tropidist repository root, or None if not found.
247 """
248 candidates: List[Path] = []
249 if tropidist_root is not None:
250 candidates.append(Path(tropidist_root))
251 else:
252 env_root = os.environ.get("TROPIDIST_ROOT")
253 if env_root:
254 candidates.append(Path(env_root))
255 try:
256 import importlib.util
257 spec = importlib.util.find_spec("cdist")
258 origin = getattr(spec, "origin", None) if spec is not None else None
259 if origin and os.path.isfile(origin):
260 candidates.append(Path(origin).resolve().parent.parent)
261 except Exception:
262 pass
263 for cand in candidates:
264 try:
265 if _is_tropidist_root(cand):
266 return str(cand.resolve())
267 except OSError:
268 continue
269 return None
270

273 """Whether a runnable `tropidist` checkout is configured (`TROPIDIST_ROOT` or `cdist` on `sys.path`)."""
274 return find_tropidist_root(tropidist_root) is not None

341def load_distance_cache(filepath: Optional[Union[str, Path]] = None) -> Dict[str, Any]:
342 """
343 Loads distance cache from a JSON file into memory.
344 Inspects cache version silently; a cache file written by a newer version is ignored with a warning, and it is
345 never overwritten by save_distance_cache(). The records of DEMs with a probability cutoff pmin > 0 (keys
346 'dem:...:pmin=...') of a file written before version 0.17.2 (or without a version) are not loaded, so that they
347 are computed again: engine='cert' ignored pmin before version 0.17.2 (its result for the full DEM was cached under
348 the key of the DEM with the cutoff).
349 """
350 global _distance_cache, _distance_cache_file
351 target_file = str(Path(filepath).resolve()) if filepath is not None else _distance_cache_file
352 if target_file and os.path.isfile(target_file):
353 try:
354 with open(target_file, "r") as f:
355 data = json.load(f)
356 if isinstance(data, dict):
357 cache_ver = data.pop("__version__", None)
358 # If cache is from a future incompatible version, skip loading (and do not overwrite it)
359 if cache_ver is not None and _parse_version(cache_ver) > _parse_version(__version__):
360 _newer_cache_files.add(target_file)
361 sys.stderr.write(
362 f"# Warning: Cache file '{target_file}' has newer version {cache_ver} "
363 f"(current {__version__}); ignoring incompatible cache (the file is not overwritten).\n"
364 )
365 return _distance_cache
366 if cache_ver is None or _parse_version(str(cache_ver)) < _parse_version(_CACHE_PMIN_FIX_VERSION):
367 for k in [k for k in data if k.startswith("dem:") and ":pmin=" in k]:
368 del data[k] # (possibly the result of engine='cert' for the full DEM)
369 # Sanitize any legacy CSS cache entries where dmax was set from dmin when dmax_X == dmax_Z == 0
370 for k, v in data.items():
371 if isinstance(v, dict) and k.startswith("css:"):
372 if v.get("dmax_X", 0) == 0 and v.get("dmax_Z", 0) == 0 and "dmax_X" in v:
373 v["dmax"] = 0
374 _distance_cache.update(data)
375 except Exception as e:
376 sys.stderr.write(f"# Warning: Failed to load distance cache from {target_file}: {e}\n")
377 return _distance_cache
378
379
380def save_distance_cache(filepath: Optional[Union[str, Path]] = None) -> None:
381 """
382 Saves the in-memory distance cache to a JSON file.
383 Silently writes "__version__": __version__ into the file.
384 Uses atomic write via a temporary file to prevent corruption.
385 A cache file written by a newer version (see load_distance_cache()) is not overwritten.
386 """
387 global _distance_cache, _distance_cache_file
388 target_file = str(Path(filepath).resolve()) if filepath is not None else _distance_cache_file
389 if not target_file or target_file in _newer_cache_files:
390 return
391
392 parent_dir = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(target_file)) or "."
393 os.makedirs(parent_dir, exist_ok=True)
394 fd, temp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix=".tmp", prefix="dist_cache_", dir=parent_dir)
395 try:
396 cache_data = dict(_distance_cache)
397 cache_data["__version__"] = __version__
398 with open(fd, "w") as f:
399 json.dump(cache_data, f, indent=2)
400 os.replace(temp_path, target_file)
401 except Exception as e:
402 if os.path.exists(temp_path):
403 try: os.remove(temp_path)
404 except OSError: pass
405 sys.stderr.write(f"# Warning: Failed to save distance cache to {target_file}: {e}\n")
406

408def clear_distance_cache(cache_file: Optional[Union[str, Path]] = None, clear_file: bool = False) -> None:
409 """
410 Clears all cached distance calculations from memory, and optionally deletes the persistent JSON file.
411 """
412 global _distance_cache, _distance_cache_file
413 _distance_cache.clear()
414 target_file = str(Path(cache_file).resolve()) if cache_file is not None else _distance_cache_file
415 if clear_file and target_file and os.path.isfile(target_file):
416 try:
417 os.remove(target_file)
418 _newer_cache_files.discard(target_file)
419 except OSError:
420 pass

441def format_bounds_list(dmin: int, dmax: int, num_rw: int) -> List[int]:
442 """
443 Returns [dmin, dmax, num_rw] according to:
444 - [d, d, 0] if known exactly; also [1, 1, 0] for dmax == 1 (every nonzero codeword has weight >= 1: a codeword of
445 weight 1 gives d = 1; since version 0.17.2, [0, 1, num_rw] before)
446 - [0, 0, 0] for an input without logical codewords (k = 0; the compute_*() functions return it, since version
447 0.17.2, see _k0_result())
448 - [dmin, 0, 0] if there is no upper bound (dmax == 0)
449 - [0, dmax, num_rw] if there is no lower bound (dmin <= 1)
450 - [dmin, dmax, num_rw] otherwise
451 """
452 if dmax == 1:
453 return [1, 1, 0]
454 eff_dmin = dmin if dmin > 1 else 0
455 eff_dmax = dmax if dmax > 0 else 0
456 eff_rw = num_rw if num_rw > 0 else 0
457 if eff_dmin > 0 and eff_dmin == eff_dmax:
458 return [eff_dmin, eff_dmax, 0]
459 elif eff_dmax == 0:
460 return [eff_dmin, 0, 0]
461 elif eff_dmin == 0:
462 return [0, eff_dmax, eff_rw]
463 else:
464 return [eff_dmin, eff_dmax, eff_rw]
465
466
467def format_bounds_str(bounds: List[int]) -> str:
468 """Formats a bounds list [dmin, dmax, num_rw] as a string, stating '(exact)' if bounds coincide."""
469 dmin, dmax, num_rw = bounds[0], bounds[1], bounds[2]
470 if dmin > 0 and dmin == dmax:
471 return f"{dmin} {dmax} {num_rw} (exact)"
472 return f"{dmin} {dmax} {num_rw}"

475def rw_infoset_find_prob(n: int, rank: int, w: int, pairs_l: int = 0) -> float:
476 """
477 Information-set estimate of the probability that a RW step finds a given codeword of weight w.
478
479 Model: uniform random information sets (as in the dist_m4ri binary, rw_infoset_find_prob()). A RW step
480 reduces H (rank r) with a random column order; a codeword is found if exactly one of its w positions is among
481 the k = n - r non-pivot columns: P1(w) = w C(n-w, k-1) / C(n, k). Codewords of weight w > r + 1 are never
482 found (P1 = 0). With the RW pairs (pairs_l > 0, the binary's option pairs), also if exactly two of its positions
483 are non-pivot columns and its other w - 2 positions avoid the l pivot rows of the buckets:
484 P2(w) = C(w, 2) C(n-w, k-2) / C(n, k) * C(r - w + 2, l) / C(r, l), and the probability is P1 + P2.
485
486 This is the isolated-codeword uniform-subset baseline, a diagnostic and not a bound: the information sets of RW
487 do not follow the uniform-subset law for any H of rank 2 <= r <= n - 2, and codewords which differ by the weight-3
488 relations of the columns (T3) or by rows of G are found together (doc/rw_triplet_degeneracies.tex, Cor. 2). With
489 the canonical classes of the binary (rw_opt bit 16, since version 0.17.0), the empirical coverage of the classes
490 of minimum-weight codewords is in _last_run_stats["rw_canon"] (see _parse_stderr_stats() and explain_bounds()).
491
492 Args:
493 n: Block length (number of columns of H).
494 rank: Rank r of H.
495 w: Codeword weight.
496 pairs_l: The number l of pivot rows of the buckets of the RW pairs (0: no pairs).
497
498 Returns:
499 P1(w) + P2(w).
500 """
501 import math
502 k = n - rank
503 if n <= 0 or rank < 0 or k <= 0 or w < 1 or w > n or w - 1 > rank:
504 return 0.0
505
506 def log_binom(a: int, b: int) -> float:
507 return math.lgamma(a + 1) - math.lgamma(b + 1) - math.lgamma(a - b + 1)
508
509 p = math.exp(math.log(w) + log_binom(n - w, k - 1) - log_binom(n, k))
510 if pairs_l > 0 and w >= 2 and k >= 2 and w - 2 + pairs_l <= rank:
511 p += math.exp(log_binom(w, 2) + log_binom(n - w, k - 2) - log_binom(n, k) + log_binom(rank - w + 2, pairs_l)
512 - log_binom(rank, pairs_l))
513 return min(1.0, p)
514
515
516def rw_infoset_estimate(
517 n: int, rank: int, steps: int, d: int, dmin: int = 1, step_time: float = 0.0, target: float = 0.01,
518 steps_total: int = 0, pairs_l: int = 0
519) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
520 """
521 Information-set estimate of the probability that RW missed a codeword lighter than the upper bound d found.
522
523 Among the weights max(dmin, 1) <= w < d (not excluded by CC), the weight hardest to find (the smallest P(w),
524 see rw_infoset_find_prob()) is used: a single codeword of this weight is missed in `steps` RW steps with uniform
525 random permutations with probability (1 - P)^steps. The number of RW steps for the target miss probability is
526 given in total, with the fraction steps / steps_total of uniform steps as in the run (the window steps are not
527 counted: kwin > 0, the hybrid index windows of every other step for n >= 500, and the row slabs of rw_opt 4).
528 Same as print_rw_infoset_estimate() in the binary. Like rw_infoset_find_prob(), this is the isolated-codeword
529 uniform-subset baseline, a diagnostic and not a bound.
530
531 Args:
532 n: Block length (number of columns of H).
533 rank: Rank of H.
534 steps: Number of completed RW steps with uniform random permutations.
535 d: Smallest weight found (the upper bound dmax).
536 dmin: Certified lower bound (smaller weights are excluded).
537 step_time: Wall time per RW step in seconds (0: unknown).
538 target: Target miss probability (default: 0.01).
539 steps_total: Number of all completed RW steps (0: the same as `steps`).
540 pairs_l: The number l of pivot rows of the buckets of the RW pairs (0: no pairs), see rw_infoset_find_prob().
541
542 Returns:
543 Dictionary with the weight `w`, the probability `p_find` = P(w) per step, the miss probability `p_miss`,
544 the total number of RW steps `steps_target` for the target miss probability (None if the codeword cannot be
545 found), and the corresponding wall time `time_target` (None if unknown); or None if there are no weights to
546 check.
547 """
548 import math
549 w_lo, w_hi = max(dmin, 1), d - 1
550 if w_hi < w_lo or n <= 0:
551 return None
552 w_hard, p1 = w_hi, rw_infoset_find_prob(n, rank, w_hi, pairs_l) # the weight hardest to find (smallest P)
553 for w in range(w_lo, w_hi):
554 pw = rw_infoset_find_prob(n, rank, w, pairs_l)
555 if pw < p1:
556 w_hard, p1 = w, pw
557 steps_target: Optional[int]
558 if p1 <= 0.0:
559 p_miss, steps_target = 1.0, None
560 elif p1 >= 1.0:
561 p_miss, steps_target = (0.0 if steps > 0 else 1.0), 1
562 else:
563 lq = math.log1p(-p1)
564 p_miss = math.exp(steps * lq) if steps > 0 else 1.0
565 steps_target = math.ceil(math.log(target) / lq)
566 if steps_target is not None and steps > 0 and steps_total > steps:
567 steps_target = math.ceil(steps_target * steps_total / steps)
568 time_target = steps_target * step_time if (steps_target is not None and step_time > 0.0) else None
569 return {"w": w_hard, "p_find": p1, "p_miss": p_miss, "steps_target": steps_target, "time_target": time_target}
570
571
572def _format_duration(t: float) -> str:
573 """Formats a duration in seconds (s, min, h, or days), as in the dist_m4ri binary."""
574 if t < 120.0:
575 return f"{t:.3g} s"
576 if t < 7200.0:
577 return f"{t / 60.0:.3g} min"
578 if t < 172800.0:
579 return f"{t / 3600.0:.3g} h"
580 return f"{t / 86400.0:.3g} days"
581
582
583def _parse_stderr_stats(stderr: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
584 """
585 Parses codeword and hit statistics from dist_m4ri stderr output (debug & 1), and with debug & 8 the CC rounds:
586 "cc_rounds", a list with an entry for each completed CC round, {"w": weight, "work": the CC thread time in s,
587 "predicted": the predicted work (None if not known), "time": the wall time of the round in s, "threads": the CC
588 threads (at the end of the round in method=3), "nodes": the calls of the CC recursion (None from binaries before
589 0.15.0)}, and "cc_nodes", the total of the nodes of these rounds.
590
591 The RW pipeline of the binary (rw_opt != 0, since version 0.17.0; debug & 1) adds three entries, each only if the
592 binary printed its line:
593 - "rw_triplets" (from '# RW triplets: T3=..., G_rows=..., rw_opt=0x...'): {"T3": the number of weight-3 relations
594 of the columns found by Stage 1, "ms": the time to find them in ms, "G_rows": the rows of G indexed (finG),
595 "rw_opt": the stages active in the run (the resolved bitmask)};
596 - "rw_canon" (from '# RW canonical (w=...): ...', with bit 16): the canonical classes of the codewords of the
597 minimum weight found, {"w": the weight, "classes": the classes C_obs, "raw_cws": the distinct codewords,
598 "M_eff": raw_cws / classes, "unif_inc": the class incidences N_unif of the uniform RW steps (a class counts once
599 per step), "f1", "f2": the classes seen in exactly one and two uniform steps, "p_GT": the Good-Turing unseen
600 mass f1 / N_unif, "C0_Chao2": the Chao2 estimate of the classes not seen; M_eff, p_GT, and C0_Chao2 are None
601 if the binary prints n/a: no codeword of the weight w in a uniform step, since version 0.17.2}, with the notes
602 "canon_full" (True: more than 2^24 classes, the rule of <n> decides), "min_hits_inactive" (the note of the binary
603 when no uniform step found a codeword of the minimum weight: the min_hits stop could not fire), and
604 "canon_decides" (True if the binary says that the canonical classes, not <n>, are the min_hits statistic);
605 - "rw_fkg" (from '# RW FKG score: ...'): the running means of the Harris-FKG score L_FKG(J) of the information
606 sets, {"mean_unif", "steps_unif": over the uniform RW steps, "mean_win", "steps_win": over the window steps,
607 "neg_lnC": the value printed as -lnC (the uniform-subset model, -ln C(n, r))}.
608
609 The codewords found by the step types (from '# RW step types, w=...'): "rw_step_types", {w: {"uniform_cws",
610 "uniform_hits", "window_cws", "window_hits", "slab_cws", "slab_hits" (the row slabs of rw_opt 4; 0 from binaries
611 which do not print them), "both_cws" (found by the uniform and by the other steps), "cws"}}; and with the min_hits
612 statistic <n> (avg_hits), "hits_not_counted": the hits of the row slabs and of the window steps which <n> does not
613 count (with a nonzero resolved rw_opt; absent if none), and "min_hits_inactive" also for the rule of <n> (no
614 codeword of the minimum weight with a counted hit).
615
616 When the binary is invoked with opt-in `json=1` (since version 0.17.4), the `# RESULT {json}` line on stderr is
617 parsed into `"result_json"` (the decoded dict, schema `"dm4ri-result/1"`).
618 """
619 import re
620 stats: Dict[str, Any] = {"extra_weights": [], "rw_converged": False, "hit_warnings": []}
621 if not stderr:
622 return stats
623 hit_warning: Optional[List[str]] = None
624 skip_estimate = False
625 num = r"([-+]?(?:\d+\.?\d*(?:[eE][-+]?\d+)?|\.\d+(?:[eE][-+]?\d+)?|[iI][nN][fF]|[nN][aA][nN])|n/a)" # (%g, %f)
626
627 def fnum(x: str) -> Optional[float]: # (n/a: no data)
628 return None if x == "n/a" else float(x)
629 for line in stderr.splitlines():
630 line_s = line.strip()
631 if line_s.startswith("# RESULT "): # opt-in JSON summary (json=1, since version 0.17.4)
632 try:
633 stats["result_json"] = json.loads(line_s[len("# RESULT "):])
634 except Exception:
635 pass
636 continue
637 if line_s.startswith("# information-set estimate"): # printed by the binary after a hit warning
638 skip_estimate = True
639 elif skip_estimate and line_s.startswith("# "):
640 continue
641 else:
642 skip_estimate = False
643 if skip_estimate:
644 if hit_warning is not None:
645 stats["hit_warnings"].append(" ".join(hit_warning))
646 hit_warning = None
647 continue
648 if hit_warning is not None:
649 if line_s.startswith("# "): # continuation of a hit uniformity warning
650 hit_warning.append(line_s[1:].strip())
651 continue
652 stats["hit_warnings"].append(" ".join(hit_warning))
653 hit_warning = None
654 if line_s.startswith("# Warning: non-uniform RW hit counts"):
655 hit_warning = [line_s[len("# Warning: "):]]
656 continue
657 if line_s.startswith("# Note: drop=") and " not used: " in line_s: # the reduction (drop=FILE) is not exact
658 stats["drop_note"] = line_s.split(" not used: ", 1)[1].replace("; using the full DEM", "")
659 continue
660 if line_s.startswith("# Note: drop=") and "none of the listed detectors is in the DEM" in line_s:
661 stats["drop_none_listed"] = True
662 continue
663 if line_s.startswith("# RW information sets:"):
664 m_rw = re.search(
665 r"n=(\d+), rank\‍(H\‍)=(\d+), steps=(\d+) \‍(uniform permutations: (\d+)\‍), ksub=(\d+), "
666 r"(?:pairs=(\d+), )?([0-9.eE+-]+) s/step per thread, (\d+) RW threads", line_s
667 )
668 if m_rw:
669 stats["rw_n"] = int(m_rw.group(1))
670 stats["rw_rank"] = int(m_rw.group(2))
671 stats["rw_steps"] = int(m_rw.group(3))
672 stats["rw_steps_uniform"] = int(m_rw.group(4))
673 stats["rw_ksub"] = int(m_rw.group(5))
674 stats["rw_pairs_l"] = int(m_rw.group(6)) if m_rw.group(6) else 0
675 stats["rw_step_time"] = float(m_rw.group(7))
676 stats["rw_threads"] = int(m_rw.group(8))
677 continue
678 if line_s.startswith("# RW pairs (p=2"): # the pairs checked, and the codewords found by pairs and singles
679 m_p = re.search(r"([0-9.eE+-]+) pairs checked per step; .*: (\d+) from pairs, (\d+) from single columns",
680 line_s)
681 if m_p:
682 stats["rw_pairs_per_step"] = float(m_p.group(1))
683 stats["rw_hits_pairs"] = int(m_p.group(2))
684 stats["rw_hits_single"] = int(m_p.group(3))
685 continue
686 if line_s.startswith("# RW step types, w="): # the codewords found by the uniform, window, and slab steps
687 m_st = re.search(r"w=(\d+): uniform steps: cws=(\d+), hits=(\d+); window steps: cws=(\d+), hits=(\d+); "
688 r"(?:row slabs: cws=(\d+), hits=(\d+); )?both: cws=(\d+) \‍(of (\d+) cws\‍)", line_s)
689 if m_st:
690 v = [int(x) if x is not None else 0 for x in m_st.groups()] # (no row slabs before the binary said so)
691 stats.setdefault("rw_step_types", {})[v[0]] = {
692 "uniform_cws": v[1], "uniform_hits": v[2], "window_cws": v[3], "window_hits": v[4],
693 "slab_cws": v[5], "slab_hits": v[6], "both_cws": v[7], "cws": v[8]}
694 continue
695 if line_s.startswith("# RW triplets:"): # the RW pipeline (rw_opt != 0): Stage 1, the weight-3 relations T3
696 m_t = re.search(rf"T3=(-?\d+) \‍({num} ms\‍), G_rows=(-?\d+), rw_opt=0x([0-9a-fA-F]+)", line_s)
697 if m_t:
698 g = m_t.groups()
699 stats["rw_triplets"] = {"T3": int(g[0]), "ms": fnum(g[1]) or 0.0, "G_rows": int(g[2]),
700 "rw_opt": int(g[3], 16)}
701 continue
702 if line_s.startswith("# RW canonical (w="): # rw_opt bit 16: the canonical classes of the minimum weight
703 m_c = re.search(rf"\‍(w=(-?\d+)\‍): classes=(-?\d+), raw_cws=(-?\d+), M_eff={num}, unif_inc=(-?\d+), "
704 rf"f1=(-?\d+), f2=(-?\d+), p_GT={num}, C0_Chao2={num}", line_s)
705 if m_c:
706 g = m_c.groups()
707 stats["rw_canon"] = {
708 "w": int(g[0]), "classes": int(g[1]), "raw_cws": int(g[2]), "M_eff": fnum(g[3]),
709 "unif_inc": int(g[4]), "f1": int(g[5]), "f2": int(g[6]), "p_GT": fnum(g[7]),
710 "C0_Chao2": fnum(g[8])}
711 continue
712 if line_s.startswith("# Note: more than") and "canonical classes" in line_s: # (rw_opt 16: tables full)
713 stats["canon_full"] = True
714 continue
715 if line_s.startswith(_K0_NOTE_PREFIX): # (no logical codeword: the result 0 0 0, since version 0.17.2)
716 body = line_s[len(_K0_NOTE_PREFIX):].strip() # ('(<reason>); the result is 0 0 0')
717 stats["k0"] = body[1:body.rfind(")")] if body.startswith("(") and ")" in body else body
718 if line_s.startswith("# Note: the min_hits stop was inactive"): # (rw_opt 16: no uniform-step data)
719 stats["min_hits_inactive"] = line_s[len("# Note: "):]
720 continue
721 if line_s.startswith("# RW FKG score:"): # the running means of the Harris-FKG score of the information sets
722 m_f = re.search(rf"mean_unif={num} \‍(steps=(-?\d+)\‍), mean_win={num} \‍(steps=(-?\d+)\‍), -lnC={num}", line_s)
723 if m_f:
724 g = m_f.groups()
725 stats["rw_fkg"] = {"mean_unif": fnum(g[0]), "steps_unif": int(g[1]), "mean_win": fnum(g[2]),
726 "steps_win": int(g[3]), "neg_lnC": fnum(g[4])}
727 continue
728 if line_s.startswith("# rounds of the DEM:"): # the input summary (debug & 1, a DEM)
729 m_r = re.search(r"D=(\d+) detectors and L=(\d+) columns per round \‍(estimated: score ([0-9.]+)\‍)", line_s)
730 m_n = re.search(r"best score ([0-9.]+)", line_s)
731 if m_r:
732 stats["rounds"] = {"D": int(m_r.group(1)), "L": int(m_r.group(2)), "score": float(m_r.group(3))}
733 elif m_n:
734 stats["rounds"] = {"D": 0, "L": 0, "score": float(m_n.group(1))}
735 continue
736 if line_s.startswith("# CC round w=") and " work: " in line_s: # debug & 8: a completed CC round
737 m_cc = re.match(r"# CC round w=(\d+) work: ([0-9.eE+-]+) thread-s measured, (unknown|([0-9.eE+-]+) "
738 r"thread-s) predicted \‍(([0-9.]+)s(?: on (\d+) threads|, (\d+) CC threads at the end)\‍)"
739 r"(?:, (\d+) nodes)?", line_s)
740 if m_cc:
741 g = m_cc.groups()
742 stats.setdefault("cc_rounds", []).append({
743 "w": int(g[0]), "work": float(g[1]), "predicted": float(g[3]) if g[3] else None,
744 "time": float(g[4]), "threads": int(g[5] or g[6]), "nodes": int(g[7]) if g[7] else None})
745 continue
746 if "RW convergence reached" in line_s: # progress line (debug & 2) or the stop reason (debug & 1)
747 stats["rw_converged"] = True
748 if line_s.startswith("# codewords accumulated: total=0"):
749 stats["total_cws"] = 0
750 elif line_s.startswith("# codewords accumulated:"):
751 m = re.search(
752 r"total=(\d+),\s*min_w=(\d+):\s*cws=(\d+),\s*total_hits=(\d+),\s*"
753 r"hits min=(\d+),\s*max=(\d+),\s*avg=([0-9.]+),\s*stdev=([0-9.]+)",
754 line_s
755 )
756 if m:
757 stats["total_cws"] = int(m.group(1))
758 stats["min_w"] = int(m.group(2))
759 stats["cws"] = int(m.group(3))
760 stats["total_hits"] = int(m.group(4))
761 stats["hits_min"] = int(m.group(5))
762 stats["hits_max"] = int(m.group(6))
763 stats["hits_avg"] = float(m.group(7))
764 stats["hits_stdev"] = float(m.group(8))
765 m_set = re.search(
766 r"<n>=([0-9.]+) over (\d+) cws of w=(\d+)\.\.(\d+) \‍(min_hits=(\d+), cov_cws=(-?\d+)\‍)", line_s
767 )
768 if "not used: the canonical classes decide" in line_s: # (since version 0.17.2 of the binary)
769 stats["canon_decides"] = True
770 m_nc = re.search(r", (\d+) window and slab hits not counted", line_s)
771 if m_nc: # (the hits of the row slabs and of the window steps, not counted for <n>)
772 stats["hits_not_counted"] = int(m_nc.group(1))
773 if m_set:
774 stats["avg_hits"] = float(m_set.group(1))
775 stats["set_cws"] = int(m_set.group(2))
776 stats["set_w_lo"] = int(m_set.group(3))
777 stats["set_w_hi"] = int(m_set.group(4))
778 stats["min_hits"] = int(m_set.group(5))
779 stats["cov_cws"] = int(m_set.group(6))
780 elif line_s.startswith("# codewords w="):
781 m_w = re.search(
782 r"w=(\d+):\s*cws=(\d+),\s*total_hits=(\d+),\s*"
783 r"hits min=(\d+),\s*max=(\d+),\s*avg=([0-9.]+),\s*stdev=([0-9.]+)",
784 line_s
785 )
786 if m_w:
787 stats["extra_weights"].append({
788 "w": int(m_w.group(1)),
789 "cws": int(m_w.group(2)),
790 "total_hits": int(m_w.group(3)),
791 "hits_min": int(m_w.group(4)),
792 "hits_max": int(m_w.group(5)),
793 "hits_avg": float(m_w.group(6)),
794 "hits_stdev": float(m_w.group(7)),
795 })
796 if hit_warning is not None:
797 stats["hit_warnings"].append(" ".join(hit_warning))
798 cc_rounds = stats.get("cc_rounds")
799 if cc_rounds and all(r["nodes"] is not None for r in cc_rounds):
800 stats["cc_nodes"] = sum(r["nodes"] for r in cc_rounds)
801 return stats
802
803
804def _canon_rule_decides(stats: Dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
805 """
806 Whether the min_hits stop of the binary run (stats, see _parse_stderr_stats()) used the canonical classes of
807 rw_opt 16 (the Good-Turing / Chao2 rule on the uniform RW steps) instead of the average hits <n>: if the binary says
808 so (since version 0.17.2), or if it printed the canonical classes with min_hits > 0 (and its tables were not full).
809 """
810 if stats.get("canon_decides"):
811 return True
812 return bool(stats.get("rw_canon")) and stats.get("min_hits", 0) > 0 and not stats.get("canon_full")
813
814
815def _canon_rule_text(stats: Dict[str, Any]) -> str:
816 """
817 The canonical stopping rule of min_hits (rw_opt 16) for explain_bounds(), evaluated on the classes of the run: N
818 step incidences of the C classes in the uniform RW steps, f1 and f2 classes seen in one and two of them; RW stops
819 once N >= max(15, 3 min_hits), N / C >= min_hits, f1 / N <= min(0.02, 3 exp(-min_hits)), and the Chao2 fraction
820 C0 / (C + C0) <= 0.05 with C0 = f1 (f1 - 1) / (2 (f2 + 1)) ('' if this rule did not decide).
821 """
822 import math
823 if not _canon_rule_decides(stats):
824 return ""
825 if stats.get("min_hits_inactive"):
826 return f"Stopping rule (canonical classes, rw_opt 16): {stats['min_hits_inactive']}."
827 canon, mh = stats.get("rw_canon") or {}, stats.get("min_hits", 0)
828 n_u, cls, f1, f2 = canon.get("unif_inc", 0), canon.get("classes", 0), canon.get("f1", 0), canon.get("f2", 0)
829 if mh <= 0 or n_u <= 0 or cls <= 0:
830 return ("Stopping rule (canonical classes, rw_opt 16): inactive, no codeword of the minimum weight was found "
831 "in a uniform RW step.")
832 need, eps = max(15, 3 * mh), min(0.02, 3.0 * math.exp(-mh))
833 c0 = f1 * (f1 - 1) / (2.0 * (f2 + 1))
834 tests = [(n_u >= need, f"N = {n_u} >= max(15, 3 min_hits) = {need}"),
835 (n_u / cls >= mh, f"N/C = {n_u / cls:.2f} >= min_hits = {mh}"),
836 (f1 / n_u <= eps, f"Good-Turing f1/N = {f1 / n_u:.3g} <= min(0.02, 3 exp(-min_hits)) = {eps:.3g}"),
837 (c0 / (cls + c0) <= 0.05, f"Chao2 C0/(C+C0) = {c0 / (cls + c0):.3g} <= 0.05")]
838 held = ", ".join(f"{t} ({'yes' if ok else 'no'})" for ok, t in tests)
839 verdict = "all hold: RW stopped by this rule" if all(ok for ok, _ in tests) else "not all hold"
840 return (f"Stopping rule (canonical classes of weight {canon.get('w')} in the uniform RW steps, rw_opt 16; C = "
841 f"{cls}, f1 = {f1}, f2 = {f2}): {held}; {verdict}.")
842
843
844def _lower_bound_text(dmin: int, stats: Optional[Dict[str, Any]], method: Optional[int] = None) -> str:
845 """
846 For explain_bounds(): a lower bound dmin > 1 and its source as far as the statistics stats of the call show it
847 (since version 0.17.2; before, every lower bound was attributed to CC): qec_cert (engine='cert'), tropidist
848 (engine='tropidist'), a stage of engine='auto', the CC search of a run of the binary (also without statistics with
849 method=2), or a cache record.
850 """
851 st = stats or {}
852 none_below = f"no non-trivial codeword of weight w <= {dmin - 1}"
853 for key, eng_name, opt_name in (("engine_cert", "qec_cert", "cert"),
854 ("engine_tropidist", "tropidist", "tropidist")):
855 rec = st.get(key)
856 if rec is not None:
857 if rec.get("cached"):
858 return f"{none_below} (a cache record; engine='{opt_name}')"
859 if (rec.get("lb", 0) or 0) >= dmin:
860 return f"{none_below}, certified by {eng_name} (engine='{opt_name}')"
861 return f"{none_below} (a cache record or dmin=; {eng_name} itself certified less)"
862 auto = st.get("engine_auto")
863 if auto:
864 b_eng = auto.get("stage_b_engine") or "qec_cert"
865 for key, what in (("stage_c", f"the CC search of the binary after {b_eng} (engine='auto')"),
866 ("stage_b", f"{b_eng} (Stage B of engine='auto')"),
867 ("stage_a", "the CC search of the binary (Stage A of engine='auto')")):
868 b = auto.get(key)
869 if b is not None and (b[0] or 0) >= dmin:
870 cached = key == "stage_a" and auto.get("stage_a_cached")
871 return f"{none_below}, certified by {what}" + (", from the cache" if cached else "")
872 if "hit_warnings" in st or "rw_n" in st or (not st and method == 2): # (a run of the binary: its CC search)
873 return (f"All cluster weights w <= {dmin - 1} were exhaustively analyzed by CC without finding any non-trivial "
874 f"codewords (from a certified lower bound of the cache or dmin=, if given)")
875 return f"{none_below} (a certified lower bound of the cache, of an earlier run, or dmin=)"
876
877
878def explain_bounds(
879 bounds: List[int],
880 method: Optional[int] = None,
881 label: str = "",
882 stats: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
883 dstop: int = 0
884) -> str:
885 """
886 Returns a human-readable explanation of [dmin, dmax, num_rw] following README.md.
887
888 Args:
889 bounds: [dmin, dmax, rw_steps] list.
890 method: Optional solver method (1=RW, 2=CC, 3=Bracketing).
891 label: Optional prefix/label (e.g. "dX", "dZ", "").
892 stats: Optional dictionary of codeword and hit statistics parsed from dist_m4ri.
893 dstop: Stop target of the search (0: none); once dmin >= dstop, the upper bound is not needed, and the
894 estimates of the probability that RW missed a lighter codeword are skipped.
895
896 Returns:
897 Multi-line formatted explanation string.
898 """
899 dmin, dmax, num_rw = bounds[0], bounds[1], bounds[2]
900 lines = []
901 prefix = f"{label} " if label else ""
902 if stats and stats.get("k0") and dmin == 0 and dmax == 0: # (since version 0.17.2)
903 return (f" {prefix}No logical codeword (k = 0): the distance is not defined, and the result is 0 0 0 "
904 f"({stats['k0']}).")
905 stopped = dstop > 0 and dmin >= dstop and not (dmin > 0 and dmin == dmax)
906
907 # Lower bound explanation
908 if dmin > 0 and dmin == dmax:
909 lines.append(f" {prefix}Lower bound (dmin = {dmin}): Exact distance certified (dmin == dmax == {dmin}).")
910 elif dmin > 1:
911 lines.append(f" {prefix}Lower bound (dmin = {dmin}): {_lower_bound_text(dmin, stats, method)}.")
912 else:
913 lines.append(f" {prefix}Lower bound (dmin = {dmin}): No non-trivial lower bound certified (dmin <= 1).")
914
915 # Upper bound explanation
916 if dmax > 0:
917 lines.append(f" {prefix}Upper bound (dmax = {dmax}): Weight of the smallest non-trivial codeword discovered.")
918 else:
919 lines.append(f" {prefix}Upper bound (dmax = {dmax}): No non-trivial codeword discovered yet (dmax = 0).")
920 if stopped:
921 lines.append(f" {prefix}Stop target (dstop = {dstop}): reached, the search ended once dmin >= {dstop} was "
922 f"certified (no codeword of weight < {dstop}); the upper bound is not needed.")
923
924 # RW steps explanation (and why it is zero if num_rw == 0)
925 if num_rw > 0:
926 lines.append(f" {prefix}Random window steps (rw_steps = {num_rw}): {num_rw} completed random "
927 f"information set searches across worker threads.")
928 else:
929 if dmin > 0 and dmin == dmax:
930 lines.append(f" {prefix}Random window steps (rw_steps = 0): Set to 0 because the exact distance "
931 f"d = {dmin} was proven by Connected Cluster search or certified bounds coincided.")
932 elif method == 2:
933 lines.append(f" {prefix}Random window steps (rw_steps = 0): Set to 0 because Method 2 (Connected Cluster) "
934 f"is an exhaustive search that does not perform random information set (RW) sampling.")
935 else:
936 lines.append(f" {prefix}Random window steps (rw_steps = 0): 0 completed random information set steps.")
937
938 if stats and "total_cws" in stats:
939 if stats["total_cws"] > 0:
940 lines.append(
941 f" {prefix}Codewords accumulated: {stats['total_cws']} distinct "
942 f"(w = {stats['min_w']}: {stats['cws']} codewords, {stats['total_hits']} total hits; "
943 f"hits min = {stats['hits_min']}, max = {stats['hits_max']}, "
944 f"avg = {stats['hits_avg']:.2f}, stdev = {stats['hits_stdev']:.2f})."
945 )
946 if stats.get("min_hits", 0) > 0 and "avg_hits" in stats:
947 import math
948 conv_str = "CONVERGED" if stats.get("rw_converged") else "not converged"
949 excl = stats.get("hits_not_counted", 0)
950 excl_str = (f"; the {excl} hits of the row slabs and of the window steps are counted apart, not in "
951 f"<n>" if excl > 0 else "")
952 if _canon_rule_decides(stats): # (rw_opt 16: the canonical classes are the stopping statistic)
953 lines.append(
954 f" {prefix}Hit convergence (min_hits = {stats['min_hits']}): decided by the canonical classes "
955 f"of rw_opt 16 in the uniform RW steps ({conv_str}; see the stopping rule below); the average "
956 f"<n> = {stats['avg_hits']:.2f} hits per codeword ({stats['set_cws']} codewords of weight "
957 f"{stats['set_w_lo']}..{stats['set_w_hi']}, cov_cws = {stats['cov_cws']}) is not used for the "
958 f"stop{excl_str}.")
959 elif stats.get("min_hits_inactive"): # (the rule of <n>: no codeword of the minimum weight counted)
960 lines.append(
961 f" {prefix}Hit convergence (min_hits = {stats['min_hits']}, cov_cws = {stats['cov_cws']}): "
962 f"inactive, no codeword of the minimum weight was found in a uniform RW step (the min_hits "
963 f"stop could not end RW){excl_str} ({conv_str}).")
964 else:
965 lines.append(
966 f" {prefix}Hit convergence (min_hits = {stats['min_hits']}, "
967 f"cov_cws = {stats['cov_cws']}): <n> = {stats['avg_hits']:.2f} average hits per codeword "
968 f"({stats['set_cws']} codewords of weight {stats['set_w_lo']}..{stats['set_w_hi']}), "
969 f"P_fail ~ exp(-<n>) = {math.exp(-stats['avg_hits']):.2g} ({conv_str}){excl_str}."
970 )
971 for ew in stats.get("extra_weights", []):
972 lines.append(
973 f" {prefix}Codewords (w = {ew['w']}): {ew['cws']} codewords, "
974 f"{ew['total_hits']} total hits; hits min = {ew['hits_min']}, "
975 f"max = {ew['hits_max']}, avg = {ew['hits_avg']:.2f}, "
976 f"stdev = {ew['hits_stdev']:.2f}."
977 )
978 n_all, n_unif = stats.get("rw_steps", 0), stats.get("rw_steps_uniform", 0)
979 types = stats.get("rw_step_types", {})
980 # (a run with the row slabs, i.e., rw_opt bit 4 in the resolved mask, has no index windows)
981 slabs = bool((stats.get("rw_triplets") or {}).get("rw_opt", 0) & 0x04) or any(
982 t.get("slab_cws", 0) > 0 or t.get("slab_hits", 0) > 0 for t in types.values())
983 for w, st in sorted(types.items()):
984 other = (f"{st['slab_cws']} in the {n_all - n_unif} row-slab steps ({st['slab_hits']} hits)"
985 if slabs else
986 f"{st['window_cws']} in the {n_all - n_unif} window steps ({st['window_hits']} hits)")
987 lines.append(
988 f" {prefix}Codewords (w = {w}) by RW step type: {st['uniform_cws']} found in the {n_unif} uniform "
989 f"steps ({st['uniform_hits']} hits), {other}, {st['both_cws']} in both (of {st['cws']} codewords)."
990 )
991 if stats.get("rw_pairs_l", 0) > 0 and "rw_pairs_per_step" in stats:
992 lines.append(
993 f" {prefix}RW pairs (p=2, buckets of l = {stats['rw_pairs_l']} pivot rows): "
994 f"{stats['rw_pairs_per_step']:.3g} pairs checked per RW step; codewords recorded with weight up to "
995 f"the upper bound: {stats['rw_hits_pairs']} from pairs, {stats['rw_hits_single']} from single "
996 f"columns."
997 )
998 for hw in stats.get("hit_warnings", []):
999 lines.append(f" {prefix}WARNING: {hw}")
1000 else:
1001 lines.append(f" {prefix}Codewords accumulated: 0 distinct non-trivial codewords found.")
1002 tri = stats.get("rw_triplets") if stats else None
1003 if tri: # the RW pipeline of the binary (rw_opt != 0, since version 0.17.0)
1004 g_str = f"; {tri['G_rows']} rows of G indexed for the shortening" if tri.get("G_rows", 0) > 0 else ""
1005 ms = tri.get("ms", 0.0)
1006 t_str = f"{ms / 1000.0:.3g} s" if ms >= 1000.0 else f"{ms:.3g} ms"
1007 lines.append(f" {prefix}RW pipeline (active stages rw_opt=0x{tri['rw_opt']:x}): {tri['T3']} weight-3 "
1008 f"relations T3 of the columns (found in {t_str}){g_str}.")
1009
1010 # The RW upper bound is not certified: estimated probability that RW missed a lighter codeword
1011 if stats and num_rw > 0 and dmax > max(dmin, 1) and not stopped:
1012 import math
1013 rw_threads = stats.get("rw_threads", 0)
1014 step_wall = stats.get("rw_step_time", 0.0) / rw_threads if rw_threads > 0 else 0.0
1015 avg = stats.get("avg_hits", 0.0)
1016 if stats.get("min_hits", 0) > 0 and avg > 0.0 and not _canon_rule_decides(stats): # (the rule of <n>)
1017 p_hit = math.exp(-avg)
1018 if p_hit > 0.01:
1019 need = math.ceil(num_rw * math.log(100.0) / avg) # the average number of hits grows with the steps
1020 t_str = f", ~{_format_duration((need - num_rw) * step_wall)} more" if step_wall > 0.0 else ""
1021 lines.append(f" {prefix}Hit-based estimate: P_fail ~ exp(-<n>) = {p_hit:.2g}; 1% after about {need} "
1022 f"RW steps in total{t_str}.")
1023 else:
1024 lines.append(f" {prefix}Hit-based estimate: P_fail ~ exp(-<n>) = {p_hit:.2g} (below 1%).")
1025 n_unif = stats.get("rw_steps_uniform", 0)
1026 if stats.get("rw_n", 0) > 0 and stats.get("rw_ksub", 0) == 0 and n_unif > 0:
1027 n_cols, rank = stats["rw_n"], stats["rw_rank"]
1028 pairs_l = stats.get("rw_pairs_l", 0)
1029 est = rw_infoset_estimate(n_cols, rank, n_unif, dmax, dmin=max(dmin, 1), step_time=step_wall,
1030 steps_total=stats.get("rw_steps", n_unif), pairs_l=pairs_l)
1031 if est is not None and est["steps_target"] is None:
1032 lines.append(f" {prefix}Information-set estimate: a codeword of weight {est['w']} cannot be found "
1033 f"by RW (n = {n_cols}, rank(H) = {rank}).")
1034 elif est is not None:
1035 t_str = (f", ~{_format_duration(est['time_target'])}" if est["time_target"] is not None else "")
1036 p_str = f" with pairs, l = {pairs_l}" if pairs_l > 0 else ""
1037 lines.append(
1038 f" {prefix}Information-set estimate (baseline: an isolated codeword, uniform random information "
1039 f"sets{p_str}; n = {n_cols}, rank(H) = {rank}, {n_unif} of {stats.get('rw_steps', n_unif)} RW "
1040 f"steps uniform): a single codeword of weight {est['w']} < {dmax} is found with probability "
1041 f"{est['p_find']:.3g} per RW step and would be missed with probability {est['p_miss']:.2g}; 1% "
1042 f"after about {est['steps_target']} RW steps in total{t_str}."
1043 )
1044 # (with min_hits=0, the binary does not count the hits: each codeword then has a single hit)
1045 if stats.get("min_w") == dmax and "hits_avg" in stats and stats.get("min_hits", 0) > 0:
1046 n_all = stats.get("rw_steps", n_unif)
1047 p1 = rw_infoset_find_prob(n_cols, rank, dmax, pairs_l)
1048 st = stats.get("rw_step_types", {}).get(dmax)
1049 if st is not None and st["uniform_cws"] > 0: # the hits of the uniform steps only
1050 n_ref, obs = n_unif, st["uniform_hits"] / st["uniform_cws"]
1051 note = " over the codewords found in the uniform steps"
1052 else:
1053 n_ref, obs = n_all, stats["hits_avg"]
1054 note = "" if n_unif == n_all else ", including the steps with localized windows"
1055 # (the average over the codewords found, each at least once: the zero-truncated Poisson mean
1056 # mu / (1 - exp(-mu)) of the mu = n p hits of a codeword, as the hit test of the binary uses)
1057 mu = n_ref * p1
1058 exp_hits = mu / -math.expm1(-mu) if mu > 0.0 else 1.0
1059 verdict = ("the uniform model is conservative here" if obs >= exp_hits else
1060 "codewords are found less often than in the uniform model, the information-set "
1061 "estimate may be optimistic")
1062 lines.append(
1063 f" {prefix}Model check: expected hits per codeword of weight {dmax} found in {n_ref} uniform "
1064 f"RW steps (zero-truncated Poisson, mean {mu:.3g} hits): {exp_hits:.3g}, observed average "
1065 f"{obs:.2f}{note} ({verdict})."
1066 )
1067 elif stats.get("rw_n", 0) > 0:
1068 lines.append(f" {prefix}Information-set estimate: not available (ksub > 0 or kwin > 0: no uniform "
1069 f"random information sets).")
1070 canon = stats.get("rw_canon")
1071 if canon and canon.get("classes", 0) > 0 and canon.get("unif_inc", 0) > 0: # (rw_opt bit 16): coverage
1072 m_eff = f"{canon['M_eff']:.2f}" if canon.get("M_eff") is not None else "n/a"
1073 p_gt = f"{canon['p_GT']:.3g}" if canon.get("p_GT") is not None else "n/a"
1074 c0 = f"{canon['C0_Chao2']:.1f}" if canon.get("C0_Chao2") is not None else "n/a"
1075 lines.append(
1076 f" {prefix}Canonical class coverage (w = {canon['w']}; codewords equal up to the weight-3 relations "
1077 f"T3 of the columns or the rows of G form a class): {canon['classes']} classes of {canon['raw_cws']} "
1078 f"distinct codewords (M_eff = {m_eff} codewords per class); {canon['unif_inc']} class "
1079 f"incidences in the uniform RW steps, f1 = {canon['f1']} classes seen in one step, f2 = {canon['f2']} "
1080 f"in two: Good-Turing unseen mass p_GT = {p_gt}, Chao2 estimate of the classes not seen "
1081 f"C0 = {c0} (empirical, not a bound)."
1082 )
1083 rule = _canon_rule_text(stats)
1084 if rule:
1085 lines.append(f" {prefix}{rule}")
1086 fkg = stats.get("rw_fkg")
1087 if fkg and (fkg.get("steps_unif", 0) > 0 or fkg.get("steps_win", 0) > 0) and fkg.get("mean_unif") is not None \
1088 and fkg.get("neg_lnC") is not None:
1089 win_str = (f", {fkg['mean_win']:.2f} over {fkg['steps_win']} window steps"
1090 if fkg.get("steps_win", 0) > 0 and fkg.get("mean_win") is not None else "")
1091 lines.append(
1092 f" {prefix}Harris-FKG concentration score of the information sets J (a lower bound on ln Pr(J), "
1093 f"used as a correlate, not a certificate): mean {fkg['mean_unif']:.2f} nats over {fkg['steps_unif']} "
1094 f"uniform RW steps{win_str}, against -ln C(n, r) = {fkg['neg_lnC']:.2f} for the uniform-subset model "
1095 f"of the baseline estimate."
1096 )
1097
1098 auto = stats.get("engine_auto") if stats else None
1099 if auto: # engine='auto': the two-stage portfolio dist_m4ri -> qec_cert (see _auto_two_stage())
1100 lines.append(f" {prefix}engine='auto': {_format_auto_info(auto)}.")
1101
1102 return "\n".join(lines)

1105def get_cached_distance(
1106 H: Optional[Any] = None,
1107 G: Optional[Any] = None,
1108 L: Optional[Any] = None,
1109 Hx: Optional[Any] = None,
1110 Hz: Optional[Any] = None,
1111 Lx: Optional[Any] = None,
1112 Lz: Optional[Any] = None,
1113 dem: Optional[Any] = None,
1114 circuit: Optional[Any] = None,
1115 pmin: float = 0.0,
1116 cache_file: Optional[Union[str, Path]] = None,
1117 start: Optional[Union[int, str, Sequence[int]]] = None,
1118 simple: Optional[bool] = None,
1119 full: Optional[bool] = None,
1120 basis: Optional[str] = None,
1121 rounds: Optional[int] = None,
1122 p_noise: float = 0.001,
1123 force_noise: bool = False,
1124 start_scan: bool = False
1125) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
1126 """
1127 Retrieves the cached distance entry (including bounds and cumulative rw_steps)
1128 for a given code matrix, CSS code, or DEM.
1129
1130 If the expert CC start-column list `start` is given (see compute_classical_distance), the
1131 separate start-list record (cache key suffix ':start=a,b,c', or ':start=a,b,c:scan' with start_scan=True) is
1132 returned instead of the main record.
1133
1134 For a CSS code (Hx and Hz, optionally Lx / Lz), the entry is assembled from the records of its two sectors,
1135 the quantum codes (H=Hx, G=Hz) -> dZ and (H=Hz, G=Hx) -> dX (shared with compute_quantum_distance()): the fields
1136 dmin_X, dmax_X, rw_steps_X, dX, cws_X (the same for Z), and dist, dmin, dmax, rw_steps of d = min(dX, dZ).
1137
1138 For a Stim circuit (circuit, or dem with a .stim file), the cache key is that of the DEM processed as in
1139 compute_dem_distance(), with the same options rounds, p_noise, and force_noise (simple and full are disabled since
1140 version 0.13.0: ignored with a warning to stderr; basis does not change the DEM).
1141
1142 Returns:
1143 dict with keys {"dist", "dmin", "dmax", "rw_steps", ...} or None if not cached.
1144 """
1145 global _distance_cache, _distance_cache_file
1146 eff_cache_file = str(Path(cache_file).resolve()) if cache_file is not None else _distance_cache_file
1147 if eff_cache_file:
1148 load_distance_cache(eff_cache_file)
1149 sfx = _start_key_suffix(_scan_start_list(_normalize_start_list(start), start_scan))
1150
1151 if H is not None:
1152 entry = _distance_cache.get(_matrix_cache_key(H, G, L, classical=(G is None and L is None)) + sfx)
1153 if entry:
1154 entry = dict(entry)
1155 entry["d_info"] = format_bounds_list(entry.get("dmin", 0), entry.get("dmax", 0), entry.get("rw_steps", 0))
1156 return entry
1157 elif Hx is not None or Hz is not None:
1158 # a CSS code is cached as its two sectors (H=Hx, G=Hz) -> dZ and (H=Hz, G=Hx) -> dX, see compute_css_distance()
1159 if Hx is None or Hz is None:
1160 return None
1161 _migrate_css_records(Hx, Hz, Lx, Lz, eff_cache_file)
1162 codes = _css_sector_codes(Hx, Hz, Lx, Lz)
1163 sec = {s: _distance_cache.get(_matrix_cache_key(*codes[s]) + sfx) for s in ("X", "Z")}
1164 if not sec["X"] and not sec["Z"]:
1165 return None
1166 entry = {}
1167 bounds = {}
1168 for s in ("X", "Z"):
1169 rec = sec[s] or {}
1170 b = (rec.get("dmin", 0) or 0, rec.get("dmax", 0) or 0, rec.get("rw_steps", 0) or 0)
1171 bounds[s] = b
1172 entry[f"dmin_{s}"], entry[f"dmax_{s}"], entry[f"rw_steps_{s}"] = b
1173 entry[f"d{s}"] = format_bounds_list(*b)
1174 entry[f"cws_{s}"] = list(rec.get("cws", []))
1175 dist, d_lo, d_hi, rw = _css_combine(bounds["X"], bounds["Z"])
1176 entry.update({"dist": dist, "dmin": d_lo, "dmax": d_hi, "rw_steps": rw})
1177 return entry
1178 elif dem is not None or circuit is not None:
1179 # the key of compute_dem_distance(): a Stim circuit is processed and converted in the same way
1180 _warn_disabled_simple_full(simple, full)
1181 try:
1182 dem_obj, _, _ = _dem_from_input(dem, circuit, basis=basis, rounds=rounds, p_noise=p_noise,
1183 force_noise=force_noise)
1184 except FileNotFoundError: # (no such DEM or circuit file: nothing cached)
1185 return None
1186 entry = _distance_cache.get(_dem_cache_key(dem_obj, pmin) + sfx)
1187 if entry:
1188 entry = dict(entry)
1189 entry["d_info"] = format_bounds_list(entry.get("dmin", 0), entry.get("dmax", 0), entry.get("rw_steps", 0))
1190 return entry
1191 return None
1192
1193
1194# Backward-compatibility aliases
1195clear_css_distance_cache = clear_distance_cache
1196enable_css_distance_cache = enable_distance_cache
1197disable_css_distance_cache = disable_distance_cache
1198

1200def get_sparse_array_state(A) -> str:
1201 """
1202 Returns a deterministic string representation for JSON-compatible cache keys: for a file, its path and the hash of
1203 its content; for a NumPy array (shape, dtype, data), a scipy sparse matrix (its CSR form), or an object with
1204 tobytes(), the hash of the data; otherwise (e.g., a list of rows, or a stim.DetectorErrorModel), the hash of str(A),
1205 unless str() summarizes it with '...' (e.g., a list of NumPy rows with more than 1000 entries each): then that of
1206 numpy.asarray(A) (since version 0.17.2).
1207 """
1208 if A is None:
1209 return "none"
1210 if isinstance(A, (str, Path)):
1211 path_str = str(Path(A).resolve())
1212 if os.path.isfile(path_str):
1213 try:
1214 with open(path_str, "rb") as f:
1215 content_h = hashlib.sha256(f.read()).hexdigest()
1216 return f"file:{path_str}:{content_h}"
1217 except Exception:
1218 return f"file:{path_str}"
1219 return path_str
1220 if hasattr(A, 'shape') and hasattr(A, 'dtype') and hasattr(A, 'tobytes'):
1221 h = hashlib.sha256(A.tobytes()).hexdigest()
1222 dtype_str = getattr(A.dtype, 'str', str(A.dtype))
1223 return f"ndarray:{A.shape}:{dtype_str}:{h}"
1224 if hasattr(A, 'tocsr'):
1225 csr = A.tocsr()
1226 h = hashlib.sha256(csr.data.tobytes() + csr.indices.tobytes() + csr.indptr.tobytes()).hexdigest()
1227 return f"csr:{csr.shape}:{h}"
1228 if hasattr(A, 'tobytes'):
1229 h = hashlib.sha256(A.tobytes()).hexdigest()
1230 return f"bytes:{h}"
1231 text = str(A)
1232 if "..." in text: # (since version 0.17.2) e.g., a list of NumPy rows with more than 1000 entries, which str()
1233 # summarizes: the key of the array (different matrices had the same key before)
1234 try:
1235 import numpy as np
1236 arr = np.asarray(A)
1237 except Exception:
1238 arr = None
1239 if arr is not None and arr.ndim >= 1 and arr.dtype != object:
1240 return get_sparse_array_state(arr)
1241 h = hashlib.sha256(text.encode('utf-8')).hexdigest() # (the full text: the key of the earlier versions)
1242 return f"str_sha256:{h}"
1243

1245def create_unique_file(directory: Union[str, Path] = "tmp", extension: str = ".tmp") -> str:
1246 """Creates a unique temporary file path and ensures the parent directory exists."""
1247 try:
1248 os.makedirs(directory, exist_ok=True)
1249 fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix=extension, dir=directory)
1250 except OSError:
1251 fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix=extension)
1252 os.close(fd)
1253 return path

1256def _remove_temp_files(files: Sequence[Optional[str]], debug: int = 0) -> None:
1257 """Removes the temporary files `files` (None entries are skipped); with the debug bit PY_DBG_KEEP_FILES, the
1258 files are kept and listed instead."""
1259 for f in files:
1260 if not f or not os.path.exists(f):
1261 continue
1262 if debug & PY_DBG_KEEP_FILES:
1263 print(f"[dist_m4ri] Kept temporary file: {f}")
1264 continue
1265 try:
1266 os.remove(f)
1267 except OSError:
1268 pass

1271def read_sparse_vectors(filepath: str) -> List[List[int]]:
1272 """
1273 Reads a list of sparse vectors from a text file in NZLIST format,
1274 converting from 1-based indexing (in the file) to 0-based indexing (in Python).
1275
1276 Args:
1277 filepath (str): The path to the text file.
1278
1279 Returns:
1280 list of list of int: A list where each element is a 0-based sparse vector.
1281 """
1282 sparse_vectors = []
1283 if not os.path.exists(filepath) or os.path.getsize(filepath) == 0:
1284 return sparse_vectors
1285
1286 with open(filepath, 'r') as f:
1287 first_line = f.readline().strip()
1288 if not first_line:
1289 return sparse_vectors
1290 if first_line != '%% NZLIST':
1291 raise ValueError(f"Invalid file format in {filepath}: Missing '%% NZLIST' header.")
1292
1293 for line_num, line in enumerate(f, start=2):
1294 line = line.strip()
1295 if not line or line.startswith('%'):
1296 continue
1297 try:
1298 parts = list(map(int, line.split()))
1299 except ValueError:
1300 raise ValueError(f"Non-integer data found on line {line_num}: {line}")
1301
1302 stated_length = parts[0]
1303 vector_elements = [x - 1 for x in parts[1:]]
1304 if len(vector_elements) != stated_length:
1305 raise ValueError(
1306 f"Length mismatch on line {line_num}. "
1307 f"Expected {stated_length} elements, but found {len(vector_elements)}."
1308 )
1309 sparse_vectors.append(vector_elements)
1310
1311 return sparse_vectors
1312

1314def find_dist_m4ri_binary(custom_path: Optional[str] = None) -> str:
1315 """Finds the dist_m4ri executable."""
1316 if custom_path:
1317 if os.path.isfile(custom_path) and os.access(custom_path, os.X_OK):
1318 return os.path.abspath(custom_path)
1319 raise FileNotFoundError(
1320 f"Specified executable '{custom_path}' not found or not executable."
1321 )
1322
1323 pkg_dir = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
1324 candidates = [
1325 os.path.join(pkg_dir, "src", "dist_m4ri"),
1326 os.path.join(pkg_dir, "dist_m4ri"),
1327 os.path.join(pkg_dir, "bin", "dist_m4ri"),
1328 os.path.join(pkg_dir, "..", "dist-m4ri", "src", "dist_m4ri"),
1329 os.path.join(os.getcwd(), "src", "dist_m4ri"),
1330 os.path.join(os.getcwd(), "dist_m4ri"),
1331 os.path.join(os.getcwd(), "bin", "dist_m4ri"),
1332 ]
1333
1334 for cand in candidates:
1335 if os.path.isfile(cand) and os.access(cand, os.X_OK):
1336 return os.path.abspath(cand)
1337
1338 which_path = shutil.which("dist_m4ri")
1339 if which_path:
1340 return which_path
1341
1342 raise FileNotFoundError(
1343 "Could not find executable 'dist_m4ri'. Please run 'make -C src' to build it."
1344 )
1345
1346
1347def _parse_version(v_str: str) -> Tuple[int, ...]:
1348 import re
1349 parts = re.findall(r"\d+", v_str)
1350 return tuple(int(p) for p in parts) if parts else (0,)
1351
1352
1353def _binary_version(binary_path: Optional[str] = None) -> Tuple[Optional[str], Optional[str], Optional[str]]:
1354 """
1355 The dist_m4ri binary and its version (from `dist_m4ri --version`).
1356
1357 Returns:
1358 (path, version, error): path is None if the binary is not found; version is None if it is unknown (then
1359 error is the reason, or None if the binary does not support --version).
1360 """
1361 try:
1362 path = find_dist_m4ri_binary(binary_path)
1363 except (RuntimeError, FileNotFoundError):
1364 return None, None, None
1365 try:
1366 proc = subprocess.run([path, "--version"], stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True,
1367 timeout=2.0)
1368 except Exception as e:
1369 return path, None, str(e)
1370 if proc.returncode == 0 and "version" in proc.stdout:
1371 return path, proc.stdout.strip().split()[-1], None
1372 return path, None, None
1373
1374
1375def check_binary_compatibility(binary_path: Optional[str] = None) -> Optional[str]:
1376 """
1377 Checks if the backend dist_m4ri binary exists and is compatible (version >= __version__).
1378 Returns a warning message string if missing or older, or None if compatible (silent).
1379 """
1380 path, bin_ver, error = _binary_version(binary_path)
1381 if path is None:
1382 return "Warning: backend binary 'dist_m4ri' not found (run 'make -C src' to build it)"
1383 if error is not None:
1384 return f"Warning: failed to check binary '{path}': {error}"
1385 if bin_ver is None:
1386 return (
1387 f"Warning: backend binary '{path}' does not support --version "
1388 f"(expected >= {__version__}; run 'make -C src' to rebuild)"
1389 )
1390 if _parse_version(bin_ver) < _parse_version(__version__):
1391 return (
1392 f"Warning: backend binary '{path}' is version {bin_ver} "
1393 f"(expected >= {__version__}; run 'make -C src' to rebuild)"
1394 )
1395 return None # Compatible and up-to-date: silent!
1396
1397
1398def parse_dist_m4ri_output(stdout: str) -> Tuple[int, int, int]:
1399 """
1400 Parses the standard output of dist_m4ri.
1401 Expected format on stdout: "dmin dmax rw_steps", "dmin dmax", or a single integer.
1402
1403 Returns:
1404 tuple (dmin, dmax, rw_steps)
1405 """
1406 lines = stdout.strip().split('\n')
1407 for line in reversed(lines):
1408 line = line.strip()
1409 if not line or line.startswith('#'):
1410 continue
1411 parts = line.split()
1412 if len(parts) >= 3:
1413 try:
1414 return int(parts[0]), int(parts[1]), int(parts[2])
1415 except ValueError:
1416 continue
1417 elif len(parts) == 2:
1418 try:
1419 return int(parts[0]), int(parts[1]), 0
1420 except ValueError:
1421 continue
1422 elif len(parts) == 1:
1423 try:
1424 val = int(parts[0])
1425 return val, val, 0
1426 except ValueError:
1427 continue
1428
1429 raise RuntimeError(f"Could not parse dist_m4ri output: {stdout}")
1430
1431
1432class DistanceResult:
1433 """
1434 Structured result for code distance calculations containing:
1435 - dmin: lower bound on distance
1436 - dmax: upper bound on distance (minimum non-trivial codeword weight found)
1437 - rw_steps: cumulative number of completed random window information sets
1438 - cws: discovered codewords (if requested)
1439 """
1440 def __init__(
1441 self,
1442 dmin: int,
1443 dmax: int,
1444 rw_steps: int = 0,
1445 cws: Optional[List[List[int]]] = None,
1446 cws_X: Optional[List[List[int]]] = None,
1447 cws_Z: Optional[List[List[int]]] = None,
1448 dmin_X: Optional[int] = None,
1449 dmax_X: Optional[int] = None,
1450 rw_steps_X: Optional[int] = None,
1451 dmin_Z: Optional[int] = None,
1452 dmax_Z: Optional[int] = None,
1453 rw_steps_Z: Optional[int] = None,
1454 ):
1455 self.dmin = dmin
1456 self.dmax = dmax
1457 self.rw_steps = rw_steps
1458 self.cws = cws
1459 self.cws_X = cws_X
1460 self.cws_Z = cws_Z
1461 self.dmin_X = dmin_X
1462 self.dmax_X = dmax_X
1463 self.rw_steps_X = rw_steps_X
1464 self.dmin_Z = dmin_Z
1465 self.dmax_Z = dmax_Z
1466 self.rw_steps_Z = rw_steps_Z
1467
1468 @property
1469 def is_exact(self) -> bool:
1470 return self.dmin > 0 and self.dmin == self.dmax
1471
1472 @property
1473 def dist(self) -> int:
1474 return self.dmin if self.is_exact else (self.dmax if self.dmax > 0 else self.dmin)
1475
1476 def __int__(self) -> int:
1477 return self.dist
1478
1479 def __index__(self) -> int:
1480 return self.dist
1481
1482 def __eq__(self, other: Any) -> bool:
1483 if isinstance(other, DistanceResult):
1484 return (self.dmin, self.dmax, self.rw_steps) == (other.dmin, other.dmax, other.rw_steps)
1485 if isinstance(other, (tuple, list)):
1486 return self._fields() == tuple(other)
1487 if isinstance(other, numbers.Integral): # int, bool, and numpy integers
1488 return self.dist == other
1489 return False
1490
1491 def _fields(self) -> tuple:
1492 """The result as a tuple (dmin, dmax, rw_steps[, cws] or [, cws_X, cws_Z])."""
1493 if self.cws_X is not None or self.cws_Z is not None:
1494 return (self.dmin, self.dmax, self.rw_steps, self.cws_X or [], self.cws_Z or [])
1495 if self.cws is not None:
1496 return (self.dmin, self.dmax, self.rw_steps, self.cws)
1497 return (self.dmin, self.dmax, self.rw_steps)
1498
1499 def __iter__(self):
1500 return iter(self._fields())
1501
1502 def __getitem__(self, index: int):
1503 return self._fields()[index]
1504
1505 def __len__(self) -> int: # (not len(tuple(self)): tuple() calls __len__)
1506 return len(self._fields())
1507
1508 def __str__(self) -> str:
1509 if self.is_exact:
1510 return f"{self.dmin} {self.dmax} {self.rw_steps} (exact)"
1511 return f"{self.dmin} {self.dmax} {self.rw_steps}"
1512
1513 def __repr__(self) -> str:
1514 if self.is_exact:
1515 return f"DistanceResult({self.dmin} {self.dmax} {self.rw_steps} (exact))"
1516 return f"DistanceResult(dmin={self.dmin}, dmax={self.dmax}, rw_steps={self.rw_steps})"
1517
1518
1519def check_finc_outc(finC: Optional[str], outC: Optional[str], verbose: bool = False) -> Optional[str]:
1520 """
1521 When finC and outC names are identical, an empty or non-existent file is silently ignored
1522 (with a warning if verbose is True).
1523
1524 Returns:
1525 The effective finC filepath to use (or None if ignored).
1526 """
1527 if not finC:
1528 return None
1529 if outC and (finC == outC or os.path.abspath(finC) == os.path.abspath(outC)):
1530 if not os.path.exists(finC) or os.path.getsize(finC) == 0:
1531 if verbose:
1532 print(f"[dist_m4ri] Warning: finC='{finC}' (identical to outC) is empty or non-existent; "
1533 f"silently ignoring input codewords.")
1534 return None
1535 return finC
1536
1537
1538# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1539# Expert CC options: `start` list of CC start columns, `trust_start`, and the disabled options noscan, cbeg, cend.
1540#
1541# - start=a,b,c: CC clusters are grown only from the listed columns, and they are NOT limited to larger column
1542# indices (unlike cbeg/cend in the dist_m4ri binary). The lower bound dmin (and an exact result) is valid only
1543# if a code symmetry maps every codeword to one whose support contains a listed column (e.g., one column per
1544# block of a quasi-cyclic code); the upper bound dmax is always valid. Results are cached under the separate
1545# key '<key>:start=a,b,c' (sorted, distinct columns). Only dmax and the codewords are merged into the main
1546# record, unless the expert option trust_start is set (then dmin and rw_steps are merged as well, and an
1547# existing exact start-list record is copied to the main record even if no calculation is needed).
1548# - start_scan (since version 0.15.1, with start): a cluster grown from a listed column c only uses the columns > c,
1549# as in the scan of all columns; valid if a code symmetry maps every codeword to one whose smallest column is
1550# listed, e.g., the smallest columns of the orbits of a group of code automorphisms (start=0,l for the two blocks
1551# of a two-block group-algebra code over an abelian group). Cached under '<key>:start=a,b,c:scan'.
1552# - noscan, cbeg, cend: disabled in the Python interface (ignored with a warning to stderr); use the dist_m4ri
1553# binary directly (noscan: CC only at w=wmax; cbeg/cend: start-column range for split multi-run use, where
1554# each column is eventually listed in one of the runs).
1555# - irred (since version 0.14.8): the CLI ignores irred=0 with a warning (see _warn_cli_conflicts()); the binary
1556# always runs with its default irred=1, so that the codewords recorded (and cached) are irreducible.
1557# - steplog, slab_rows, slab_bnd, slab_var, slab_every: the study options of the dist_m4ri binary (steplog=FILE, the
1558# log of the RW steps and of the codewords found in them, and the row slabs of rw_opt 4) are disabled in the Python
1559# interface: the CLI accepts them and ignores them with a warning to stderr (see _STUDY_OPTIONS), since a run of
1560# dist_m4ri.py may run the binary several times (e.g., two CSS sectors, or the stages of engine='auto'), or not at
1561# all (a cached result). Run the dist_m4ri binary directly to use them.
1562# - stamp, json (since version 0.17.4): the opt-in machine-readable output options of the dist_m4ri binary (stamp=1,
1563# json=1|FILE) are likewise disabled in the Python CLI (accepted and ignored with a warning to stderr, see
1564# _BIN_OUTPUT_OPTIONS); use the dist_m4ri binary directly, or run_dist_m4ri(stamp=..., json_out=...) in Python.
1565# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1566
1567def _normalize_start_list(start: Any) -> Optional[List[int]]:
1568 """
1569 Normalizes the expert CC start-column specification `start` into a sorted list of distinct
1570 non-negative (0-based) column indices, or None if unset.
1571
1572 Accepts None, an integer, a comma-separated string (e.g., "0,48"), or a sequence of integers.
1573 A single negative value (e.g., -1, the default of the dist_m4ri binary) means unset (all columns).
1574
1575 Raises:
1576 ValueError: on malformed input or on negative entries in a list of several columns.
1577 """
1578 import operator
1579 if start is None:
1580 return None
1581 err_msg = f"invalid start={start!r}: expected a comma-separated list of column indices, e.g., start=0,48"
1582 vals: List[int] = []
1583 if isinstance(start, str):
1584 s = start.strip()
1585 if not s:
1586 return None
1587 try:
1588 vals = [int(tok) for tok in s.split(",")]
1589 except ValueError:
1590 raise ValueError(err_msg) from None
1591 else:
1592 try:
1593 items = list(start)
1594 except TypeError:
1595 items = [start]
1596 for v in items:
1597 if isinstance(v, (bool, str, bytes)):
1598 raise ValueError(err_msg)
1599 try:
1600 vals.append(operator.index(v))
1601 except TypeError:
1602 raise ValueError(err_msg) from None
1603 if not vals:
1604 return None
1605 if len(vals) == 1 and vals[0] < 0:
1606 return None
1607 if any(v < 0 for v in vals):
1608 raise ValueError(f"invalid start={start!r}: column indices must be non-negative")
1609 return sorted(set(vals))
1610
1611
1612class _StartList(list):
1613 """A normalized CC start list (sorted distinct columns, see _normalize_start_list()) with the expert flag `scan`
1614 (start_scan=1 of the binary: a cluster grown from a listed column c only uses the columns > c), which selects
1615 its own cache key (see _start_key_suffix())."""
1616 scan: bool = False
1617
1618
1619def _scan_start_list(start_list: Optional[List[int]], start_scan: bool) -> Optional[List[int]]:
1620 """The start list with the flag `scan` set if start_scan (None or the list itself otherwise)."""
1621 if not start_list or not start_scan:
1622 return start_list
1623 out = _StartList(start_list)
1624 out.scan = True
1625 return out
1626
1627
1628def _start_key_suffix(start_list: Optional[List[int]]) -> str:
1629 """Returns the cache key suffix ':start=a,b,c' for a normalized start list ('' if unset), with ':scan' for
1630 start_scan."""
1631 if not start_list:
1632 return ""
1633 return ":start=" + ",".join(str(c) for c in start_list) + (":scan" if getattr(start_list, "scan", False) else "")

1636def _format_start_list(start_list: List[int], max_show: int = 8) -> str:
1637 """Formats a start list for messages, showing at most `max_show` entries (as the dist_m4ri binary)."""
1638 shown = ",".join(str(c) for c in start_list[:max_show])
1639 return shown + (",..." if len(start_list) > max_show else "")

1645def set_silent(silent: bool = True) -> None:

1647 Turns off (silent=True) or on again (silent=False) the warnings written to stderr for the inputs which are
1648 ignored (the CLI option --silent). The warnings for disabled options and on the validity of a result (e.g., for

1665
1666# The note on an input without logical codewords (k = 0), whose result is 0 0 0 since version 0.17.2 (with every
1667# engine and solver): the binary writes it at any debug level, and the wrapper on the paths without the binary
1668_K0_NOTE_PREFIX = "# Note: k=0: no logical codeword" # (not the note 'k=0 is not checked' of the binary)

1671def _note_k0(reason: str) -> None:

1673 The one stderr line for an input without logical codewords (k = 0), written by the wrapper on the paths without
1674 the binary (qec_cert, codedistance), unless set_silent() is on (the binary writes its own, which run_dist_m4ri()
1675 forwards on the same terms, see _binary_stderr_forwarded()).
1676 """
1677 if _report_ignored:

1681def _k0_found(reason: str, css: bool = False) -> None:

1683 k = 0 found by the wrapper on a path without the binary (solver='codedistance'): the note (see _note_k0()) and the
1684 statistics of the call for explain_bounds(): _last_run_stats, and _last_css_stats for a CSS code.
1685 """
1686 global _last_run_stats, _last_css_stats
1687 _note_k0(reason)
1688 _last_run_stats = {"k0": reason}
1689 if css:
1690 _last_css_stats = {"X": {"k0": reason}, "Z": {"k0": reason}}

1693def _k0_result(cache_keys: Sequence[Optional[str]] = (), eff_cache_file: Optional[str] = None) -> Dict[str, Any]:
1694 """
1695 The result for an input without logical codewords (k = 0): the bounds [0, 0, 0] (since version 0.17.2; the
1696 binary printed a vacuous lower bound above n before), which are not cached: the records of cache_keys (e.g., such
1697 a lower bound of an earlier version) are removed, so that every later call gives the same result.
1698 """
1699 dropped = False
1700 for key in cache_keys:
1701 if _use_distance_cache and key is not None and key in _distance_cache:
1702 del _distance_cache[key]
1703 dropped = True
1704 if dropped and eff_cache_file:
1705 save_distance_cache(eff_cache_file)
1706 return {"dist": 0, "dmin": 0, "dmax": 0, "rw_steps": 0, "d_info": [0, 0, 0], "cws": [], "cached": False,
1707 "k0": True}
