3610 dmin: int = 0,
3611 dmax: int = 0,
3612 dstop: int = 0,
3613 wmax: int = 0,
3614 label: str = "code",
3615 debug: int = 0,
3616 verbose: bool = False,
3617 run_tropidist: Optional[Callable[..., Dict[str, Any]]] = None,
3618) -> Dict[str, Any]:
3619 """
3620 engine='auto' (since version 0.17.0): the two-stage portfolio for a quantum code, a sector of a CSS code, or a
3621 DEM, for a distance-only method=3 call (see _auto_cert_eligible()).
3622
3623 Stage A runs the dist_m4ri binary (method=3) with the time budget tau_1 (see _auto_stage_a_budget()); a cache
3624 record with the exact distance (or dmin >= dstop) answers the request as usual, without a run. The result of
3625 Stage A is returned at once, without importing qec_cert or spawning tropidist, if it is exact, if dmin >= dstop >
3626 0, if CC has reached wmax > 0, if at most _AUTO_STAGE_B_MIN_TIME s of the timeout are left, or with timeout=0 (no
3627 limit: the binary runs until the bounds meet). Otherwise, Stage B runs qec_cert (see _cert_code_distance()), or
3628 tropidist if qec_cert is unavailable and tropidist is configured (see _tropidist_available()), with the remaining
3629 time, from the bounds of Stage A: wmin = max(1, dmin_A) and wmax = dmax_A - 1 (dmax_A: the weight of a codeword
3630 found and verified by the binary), passed explicitly, so that this also holds with the cache disabled; when a
3631 narrow bracket is already known (0 < dmax_A - max(1, dmin_A) < _AUTO_STAGE_B_UB_GAP, see _auto_stage_b_use_ub()),
3632 qec_cert skips its randomized upper-bound stage (use_ub=False). The assumption lb_assumed_wmin <= dmin_A of
3633 qec_cert is discharged by the lower bound dmin_A certified by the CC of Stage A (certified_dmin, see
3634 _cert_wmin_discharged()); a lower bound of qec_cert which is conditional for any other reason is not used. With
3635 wmin > 1, qec_cert keeps the stabilizer dominance of its search on (search_opts={"force_dom": 1}, since version
3636 0.17.4, see _cert_search_kw()). Since version 0.17.5, Stage A runs the binary with json=1 if it has this option
3637 (see _binary_has_json()) and Stage B uses qec_cert, and a qec_cert with the handoff parameters gets
3638 dmax_init=dmax_A and the codeword of weight dmax_A found in this run (its JSON summary as from_dm4ri, or the
3639 codeword as ub_witness; not from a cache record, see _auto_stage_a_witness() and _cert_handoff_kw()), which it
3640 verifies itself, still from wmin = max(1, dmin_A). If Stage B ends early with an open bracket, the binary runs
3641 with the time left. The result is never weaker than that of Stage A.
3642
3643 If neither qec_cert nor tropidist is available, the binary runs once with the whole timeout (as with engine=None,
3644 without json=1); if qec_cert is installed but not usable (e.g., its library libqeccert.so is missing, see
3645 _qec_cert_available()), a warning is written to stderr once per process. If Stage B fails, a warning is written
3646 to stderr, and the binary continues with the time left. The stages are recorded in _last_run_stats["engine_auto"]
3647 (see explain_bounds()).
3648
3649 Args:
3650 run_native: (timeout, dmin, dmax, json_out=False) -> the result of _cached_code_distance() for the binary
3651 (json_out: the binary writes its JSON summary, if it has this option, in Stage A).
3652 run_cert: (dmin, dmax, certified_dmin, time_limit, dm4ri_json=None) -> the result of _cert_code_distance()
3653 for qec_cert (dm4ri_json: the JSON summary of Stage A with its codeword of weight dmax, see
3654 _auto_stage_a_witness(); None if there is none).
3655 timeout: The timeout of the call in seconds (0: no limit; None: 60 s).
3656 dmin / dmax: The caller's bounds (dmax: a known upper bound; 0 for a CSS sector).
3657 dstop / wmax: The stop target and the CC weight limit of the call.
3658 label: The kind of distance, for the messages.
3659 debug / verbose: With verbose or the debug bit PY_DBG_COMMANDS, the stages are reported.
3660 run_tropidist: Optional (dmin, dmax, certified_dmin, time_limit) -> the result of _tropidist_code_distance()
3661 when qec_cert is unavailable and tropidist is configured.
3662
3663 Returns:
3664 The result dict, as returned by _cached_code_distance().
3665 """
3666 global _last_run_stats
3667 say = verbose or bool(debug & PY_DBG_COMMANDS)
3668 t_all = _auto_timeout(timeout)
3669 stage_b_engine = "qec_cert"
3670 if not _qec_cert_available():
3671 if run_tropidist is not None and _tropidist_available():
3672 _auto_qec_cert_unusable_reason(fallback="falling back to tropidist for Stage B")
3673 stage_b_engine = "tropidist"
3674 else:
3675 reason = _auto_qec_cert_unusable_reason()
3676 res = run_native(timeout, dmin, dmax)
3677 _last_run_stats["engine_auto"] = {"stage": "native", "stage_a": None, "stage_b": None, "reason": reason}
3678 return res
3679 tau_1 = _auto_stage_a_budget(timeout)
3680 if say:
3681 t_str = f"timeout={tau_1:g} s" if tau_1 > 0 else "no time limit"
3682 print(f"[dist_m4ri] engine='auto': Stage A, dist_m4ri (method=3, {t_str}) for the {label} distance")
3683 t0 = time.monotonic()
3684 res_a = run_native(timeout if tau_1 == t_all else tau_1, dmin, dmax, json_out=stage_b_engine == "qec_cert")
3685 rj_a = _last_run_stats.get("result_json") # (of this run only: _cached_code_distance() resets the statistics)
3686 t_a = time.monotonic() - t0
3687 a_rw = res_a.get("rw_steps", 0) or 0
3688 info: Dict[str, Any] = {
3689 "stage": "A", "timeout": t_all, "tau_1": tau_1, "stage_a": [res_a["dmin"], res_a["dmax"], a_rw],
3690 "stage_a_time": t_a, "stage_a_cached": bool(res_a.get("cached")), "stage_b": None, "reason": ""}
3691 if stage_b_engine != "qec_cert":
3692 info["stage_b_engine"] = stage_b_engine
3693 reason = _auto_done_reason(res_a, "Stage A", dstop, wmax, t_all, t_all - t_a)
3694 if reason:
3695 info["reason"] = reason
3696 _last_run_stats["engine_auto"] = info
3697 if say:
3698 print(f"[dist_m4ri] engine='auto': Stage A bounds [{res_a['dmin']}, {res_a['dmax']}] in {t_a:.3g} s; "
3699 f"{reason}: no {stage_b_engine} run")
3700 return res_a
3701 s_dmin, s_dmax = _auto_seed_bounds(dmin, dmax, res_a)
3702 wit_a = _auto_stage_a_witness(res_a, rj_a, s_dmax) if stage_b_engine == "qec_cert" else None
3703 if say:
3704 print(f"[dist_m4ri] engine='auto': Stage A bounds [{res_a['dmin']}, {res_a['dmax']}] in {t_a:.3g} s; "
3705 f"Stage B, {stage_b_engine} with the remaining {t_all - t_a:.3g} s")
3706 t_b0 = time.monotonic()
3707 try:
3708 if stage_b_engine == "qec_cert":
3709 _get_qec_cert() # (the import, before the time limit of qec_cert is set)
3710 t_lim = max(t_all - (time.monotonic() - t0), 0.1) # (never 0.0: no limit in qec_cert)
3711 info["stage_b_time_limit"] = t_lim
3712 res_b = run_cert(s_dmin, s_dmax, res_a["dmin"], t_lim, dm4ri_json=wit_a)
3713 else:
3714 t_lim = max(t_all - (time.monotonic() - t0), 0.1)
3715 info["stage_b_time_limit"] = t_lim
3716 assert run_tropidist is not None
3717 res_b = run_tropidist(s_dmin, s_dmax, res_a["dmin"], t_lim)
3718 except Exception as e: # (ImportError of a broken installation, or an error in Stage B)
3719 if stage_b_engine == "qec_cert" and isinstance(e, ImportError):
3720 _auto_qec_cert_unusable_reason()
3721 info["reason"] = "qec_cert is not usable"
3722 else:
3723 sys.stderr.write(f"# Warning: engine='auto': {stage_b_engine} failed ({type(e).__name__}: {e}); using the "
3724 f"dist_m4ri bounds [{res_a['dmin']}, {res_a['dmax']}]\n")
3725 info["reason"] = f"{stage_b_engine} failed"
3726 return _auto_native_tail(run_native, res_a, info, t0=t0, t_all=t_all, dmin=dmin, dmax=dmax, prev_rw=a_rw,
3727 say=say)
3728 t_b = time.monotonic() - t_b0
3729 res_b = _auto_add_rw(dict(res_b, cached=False), a_rw)
3730 info.update(stage="B", stage_b=[res_b["dmin"], res_b["dmax"]], stage_b_time=t_b)
3731 if say:
3732 print(f"[dist_m4ri] engine='auto': Stage B ({stage_b_engine}) bounds [{res_b['dmin']}, {res_b['dmax']}] in "
3733 f"{t_b:.3g} s")
3734 reason = _auto_done_reason(res_b, "Stage B", dstop, wmax, t_all, t_all - (time.monotonic() - t0))
3735 if reason:
3736 info["reason"] = reason
3737 _last_run_stats["engine_auto"] = info
3738 return res_b
3739 info["reason"] = f"{stage_b_engine} ended early with an open bracket"
3740 return _auto_native_tail(run_native, res_b, info, t0=t0, t_all=t_all, dmin=dmin, dmax=dmax, prev_rw=a_rw,
3741 say=say)
3742
3743
3744def _auto_cert_first(
3745 run_native: Callable[[float, int, int], Dict[str, Any]],
3746 run_cert: Callable[[int, int, int, float], Dict[str, Any]],
3747 *,
3748 timeout: Optional[float],
3749 dmin: int = 0,
3750 dmax: int = 0,
3751 dstop: int = 0,
3752 wmax: int = 0,
3753 num_errors: int = 0,
3754 debug: int = 0,
3755 verbose: bool = False,
3756) -> Dict[str, Any]:
3757 """
3758 engine='auto' for a DEM with more than _AUTO_DEM_FAST_PATH_ERRORS raw error mechanisms and a timeout of at least
3759 _AUTO_DEM_FAST_PATH_MIN_TIMEOUT s (or none): qec_cert first, with the whole timeout (counted from its import, see
3760 _cert_time_left()), as with engine='cert' (a cache record with the exact distance answers without importing it;
3761 without a run of the binary before it, qec_cert gets no codeword of the binary, see _cert_handoff_kw()).
3762 If qec_cert is not installed (or not usable, with a warning once per process, see _qec_cert_available()), the
3763 binary runs with the whole timeout; if qec_cert fails (a warning) or ends early with an open bracket, the binary
3764 runs with the time left (with timeout=0 also without a limit; since version 0.17.2), see _auto_two_stage() for the
3765 arguments.
3766 """
3767 global _last_run_stats
3768 say = verbose or bool(debug & PY_DBG_COMMANDS)
3769 t_all = _auto_timeout(timeout)
3770 info: Dict[str, Any] = {"path": "qec_cert first", "num_errors": num_errors, "stage": "B", "timeout": t_all,
3771 "stage_a": None, "stage_b": None, "reason": ""}
3772 if not _qec_cert_available():
3773 info.update(stage="native", reason=_auto_qec_cert_unusable_reason())
3774 res = run_native(timeout, dmin, dmax)
3775 _last_run_stats["engine_auto"] = info
3776 return res
3777 if say:
3778 print(f"[dist_m4ri] engine='auto': {num_errors} raw DEM error mechanisms (more than "
3779 f"{_AUTO_DEM_FAST_PATH_ERRORS}): qec_cert first")
3780 t0 = time.monotonic()
3781 try: # (run_cert() imports qec_cert only if no cache record answers, and counts its time limit from then on)
3782 info["stage_b_time_limit"] = t_all
3783 res = run_cert(dmin, dmax, 0, t_all)
3784 except Exception as e:
3785 if isinstance(e, ImportError): # (found, but not usable, see _probe_qec_cert(): a warning once per process)
3786 _auto_qec_cert_unusable_reason()
3787 info.update(stage="native", reason="qec_cert is not usable")
3788 else:
3789 sys.stderr.write(f"# Warning: engine='auto': qec_cert failed ({type(e).__name__}: {e}); using dist_m4ri\n")
3790 info.update(stage="native", reason="qec_cert failed")
3791 rem = t_all - (time.monotonic() - t0)
3792 res = run_native(max(rem, _AUTO_STAGE_B_MIN_TIME) if t_all > 0 else 0.0, dmin, dmax)
3793 _last_run_stats["engine_auto"] = info
3794 return res
3795 _last_run_stats = {"k0": "certified by qec_cert"} if res.get("k0") else {} # (no run of the binary)
3796 info.update(stage_b=[res["dmin"], res["dmax"]], stage_b_time=time.monotonic() - t0)
3797 reason = _auto_done_reason(res, "qec_cert", dstop, wmax, t_all, t_all - (time.monotonic() - t0), binary=False)
3798 if reason:
3799 info["reason"] = reason
3800 _last_run_stats["engine_auto"] = info
3801 return res
3802 info["reason"] = "qec_cert ended early with an open bracket"
3803 return _auto_native_tail(run_native, res, info, t0=t0, t_all=t_all, dmin=dmin, dmax=dmax, prev_rw=0, say=say)
3804
3805
3806def _merge_start_into_plain(
3807 plain_key: str,
3808 src: Dict[str, Any],
3809 trust: bool = False,
3810 rw_delta: Optional[Dict[str, int]] = None
3811) -> bool:
3812 """
3813 Merges the start-list cache record `src` (key plain_key + ':start=...') into the main record `plain_key`.
3814
3815 The upper bound dmax (minimum of the positive values) and the codewords (union) are always valid and
3816 are always merged. Only with `trust` (expert option trust_start) the lower bound dmin is merged as well
3817 (maximum, capped at dmax), and rw_steps are either incremented by the steps of the run, `rw_delta`
3818 (after a calculation), or set to the maximum of the two records (copy of a cached record, rw_delta=None).
3819 (A CSS code is cached as the records of its two sectors, see _matrix_cache_key().)
3820
3821 Args:
3822 plain_key: Main cache key.
3823 src: Start-list cache record.
3824 trust: Accept the start-list lower bound as valid.
3825 rw_delta: RW steps of the run, {'': steps}.
3826
3827 Returns:
3828 True if the main record was created or modified.
3829 """
3830 global _distance_cache
3831 prev = _distance_cache.get(plain_key)
3832 new: Dict[str, Any] = dict(prev) if prev else {}
3833 s_dmin = src.get("dmin", 0) or 0
3834 s_dmax = src.get("dmax", 0) or 0
3835 p_dmin = new.get("dmin", 0) or 0
3836 p_dmax = new.get("dmax", 0) or 0
3837 p_rw = new.get("rw_steps", 0) or 0
3838 dmax = min(p_dmax, s_dmax) if (p_dmax > 0 and s_dmax > 0) else (p_dmax if p_dmax > 0 else s_dmax)
3839 dmin, rw = p_dmin, p_rw
3840 if trust:
3841 dmin = max(p_dmin, s_dmin)
3842 if rw_delta is not None:
3843 rw = p_rw + (rw_delta.get("", 0) or 0)
3844 else:
3845 rw = max(p_rw, src.get("rw_steps", 0) or 0)
3846 if dmax > 0 and dmin > dmax:
3847 dmin = dmax
3848 s_cws = src.get("cws", []) or []
3849 if not prev and not (trust or s_dmax > 0 or s_cws):
3850 return False
3851 new["cws"] = _union_cws(new.get("cws", []), s_cws)
3852 new["dist"] = _dist_from_bounds(dmin, dmax)
3853 new["dmin"], new["dmax"], new["rw_steps"] = dmin, dmax, rw
3854 new["d_info"] = format_bounds_list(dmin, dmax, rw)
3855 _distance_cache[plain_key] = new
3856 return True
3857
3858
3859def _resolve_start_cache(
3860 plain_key: str,
3861 start_list: Optional[List[int]],
3862 is_hit: Callable[[Dict[str, Any]], bool],
3863 trust_start: bool,
3864 merge_copy: Callable[[Dict[str, Any]], bool],
3865 eff_cache_file: Optional[str],
3866 verbose: bool = False
3867) -> Tuple[str, Optional[Dict[str, Any]], Optional[Dict[str, Any]]]:
3868 """
3869 Resolves the cache record of a run with an optional expert CC start list.
3870
3871 Without a start list, or if the main record already holds the requested exact result, the main record
3872 is used. Otherwise the separate start-list record (key plain_key + ':start=a,b,c') is used; with
3873 trust_start, an existing exact start-list record is copied to the main record (via `merge_copy`), and
3874 the cache file is saved, even though no calculation is needed.
3875
3876 Returns:
3877 (code_key, cached_entry, plain_entry): the key and the existing record (or None) for the results of
3878 this run, and the main record (or None) used to seed the bounds of a start-list run.
3879 """
3880 plain_entry = _distance_cache.get(plain_key)
3881 if not start_list:
3882 return plain_key, plain_entry, None
3883 if plain_entry is not None and is_hit(plain_entry):
3884 if verbose:
3885 print(f"[dist_m4ri] Start list not needed: the main record '{plain_key}' has the exact distance")
3886 return plain_key, plain_entry, None
3887 code_key = plain_key + _start_key_suffix(start_list)
3888 cached_entry = _distance_cache.get(code_key)
3889 if trust_start and cached_entry is not None and is_hit(cached_entry):
3890 if merge_copy(cached_entry) and eff_cache_file:
3891 save_distance_cache(eff_cache_file)
3892 if verbose:
3893 print(f"[dist_m4ri] trust_start: copied the exact start-list record to the main record '{plain_key}'")
3894 return code_key, cached_entry, plain_entry
3895
3896
3897def run_dist_m4ri(
3898 dist_m4ri_path: Optional[str] = None,
3899 method: int = 3,
3900 finH: Optional[str] = None,
3901 finG: Optional[str] = None,
3902 finL: Optional[str] = None,
3903 fin: Optional[str] = None,
3904 finC: Optional[str] = None,
3905 fdem: Optional[str] = None,
3906 dmin: int = 0,
3907 dmax: int = 0,
3908 wmax: int = 0,
3909 wmin: int = 1,
3910 dexp: int = 0,
3911 dest: int = 0,
3912 dstop: int = 0,
3913 steps: Optional[int] = None,
3914 threads: Optional[int] = None,
3915 timeout: float = 60.0,
3916 smax: Optional[int] = None,
3917 start: Optional[Union[int, str, Sequence[int]]] = None,
3918 cbeg: Optional[int] = None,
3919 cend: Optional[int] = None,
3920 css: Optional[int] = None,
3921 noscan: int = 0,
3922 classical: int = -1,
3923 dW: int = -1,
3924 maxC: int = 0,
3925 pmin: float = 0.0,
3926 merge: bool = True,
3927 drop: Optional[str] = None,
3928 outD: Optional[str] = None,
3929 sort_rows: Optional[bool] = None,
3930 cc_prune: Optional[int] = None,
3931 outC: Optional[str] = None,
3932 seed: int = 0,
3933 debug: int = 0,
3934 nothrottle: bool = False,
3935 chunk_size: int = 0,
3936 ksub: int = 0,
3937 kwin: int = 0,
3938 win_mode: int = 0,
3939 win_hyb: int = 0,
3940 pairs: int = -1,
3941 min_hits: Optional[int] = None,
3942 cov_cws: int = 100,
3943 refresh: Optional[int] = None,
3944 verbose: bool = False,
3945 stop_event: Optional[threading.Event] = None,
3946 warn_start: bool = True,
3947 warn_ksub: bool = True,
3948 start_scan: bool = False,
3949 ortho: bool = True,
3950 warn_ortho: bool = True,
3951 rw_opt: Optional[int] = None,
3952 dem_rounds: int = 0,
3953 stamp: bool = False,
3954 json_out: Optional[Union[bool, int, str, Path]] = None
3955) -> Tuple[int, int, int]:
3956 """
3957 Low-level invocation of the multithreaded dist_m4ri binary.
3958
3959 DEM input:
3960 merge: If True (default), the binary merges the equal columns of the DEM fdem (error mechanisms with the
3961 same detectors and observables). Exact: dropping two equal columns of a codeword gives a lighter one,
3962 so the distance does not change. Column indices (finC, outC, start) are those of the DEM; the codewords
3963 found use the first one of each set of equal columns. merge=False passes merge=0 (all columns are
3964 kept, e.g., to enumerate the codewords with each of them). Ignored without fdem.
3965 drop: The detectors of the DEM fdem to drop if this is verified to be exact, passed as drop=...: None (the
3966 binary's default, drop=auto: a search for the largest such set in the DEM), "auto" or "1" (the same), "0"
3967 (keep all detectors), or a file with the detectors to drop (0-based; otherwise, the binary uses the full DEM
3968 and prints a note, see _parse_stderr_stats()). Ignored without fdem.
3969 outD: File to which the binary writes the detectors dropped from the DEM fdem (0-based; only the comment line
3970 '# N of M detectors dropped ...' if none, see read_drop_file()). Ignored without fdem.
3971 dem_rounds: The rounds T of the DEM fdem, if known, passed as dem_rounds=N if positive (0, the default:
3972 unknown): 1, a single round of syndrome measurements and the final readout, adds the row slabs of rw_opt
3973 4 to the automatic rw_opt (see rw_opt; compute_dem_distance() passes the rounds of a Stim circuit, see
3974 circuit_measurement_rounds()); 2 or more: no automatic row slabs; with 0, the binary's automatic rw_opt has
3975 them for a DEM without round structure and with at most 640 detectors. Ignored without fdem.
3976
3977 Orthogonality check:
3978 ortho: If True (default), the binary checks that the rows of H and G (finG, or fin without finL) are
3979 orthogonal (H G^T = 0) and stops with an error otherwise. False (expert option, since version 0.15.2)
3980 passes ortho=0: the check is skipped, e.g., to screen many codes which are orthogonal by construction; the
3981 result is then valid only if H G^T = 0. No effect without G. The cache key does not depend on it.
3982 warn_ortho: If True (default), issue the warning for ortho=False to stderr (see _warn_ortho()).
3983
3984 Row order:
3985 sort_rows: Passed as sort_rows=1 (True) or sort_rows=0 (False); None (default): the binary's default, i.e.,
3986 1 for matrices and 0 for a DEM. With sort_rows=1, the binary sorts the rows of H by increasing weight
3987 (stable). With cc_prune=0, this reduces the CC work for matrices with very different row weights (e.g.,
3988 1.7-4x with the hook columns of an extended CSS distance), while the detectors of a DEM are in time
3989 order, which is better for CC (use sort_rows=False also for matrices exported from a DEM); with the
3990 default cc_prune=1, the order of the rows only breaks ties. The distance and RW do not depend on the
3991 order of the rows; CC enumerates the same codewords, possibly in another order (with cc_prune=0, also with
3992 other hit counts).
3993
3994 CC search:
3995 cc_prune: Passed as cc_prune=N if not None (0, 1, or 2; None, the default: the binary's default 1). The CC
3996 search with smax=0: 0, the walk of the versions before 0.15.0 (a cluster is extended by the columns of the
3997 first unsatisfied row of its syndrome); 1, the branch and bound (the unsatisfied row with the fewest
3998 available columns, the columns of the earlier branches forbidden in the later ones, so that each codeword
3999 is found once, and pruning by lower bounds on the number of columns needed: an unsatisfied row without
4000 available columns, a packing of unsatisfied rows with disjoint sets of available columns); 2, also the
4001 coverage and fractional cover bounds. The same codewords and distances (doc/cc_completeness.tex); with
4002 the expert start list (and start_scan=False), cc_prune=1 and 2 forbid the columns listed before the start
4003 column. The cache key does not depend on it.
4004
4005 RW windows:
4006 kwin / win_mode: A window of kwin columns in every RW step (win_mode=0: a Tanner graph ball, 1: an index
4007 window). kwin=0 (default): the automatic hybrid for n >= 500, an index window of win_hyb columns in every
4008 other step and uniform random permutations in the others; with a nonzero resolved rw_opt (the run plan;
4009 e.g., the default rw_opt=None on a quantum code), only for a DEM or with win_hyb > 0 (matrices: uniform
4010 random permutations in every step, see rw_opt), and with the row slabs of rw_opt 4 (e.g., automatic for a
4011 single round, see dem_rounds), a slab instead. kwin=-1 (any negative value): no windows, uniform random
4012 permutations in every step.
4013 win_hyb: Window size of the hybrid RW steps, passed as win_hyb=N if nonzero; 0 (default): 256 columns for a
4014 DEM, 512 for matrices (at most 3n/4). The windows of 192-256 columns find the minimum-weight codewords of
4015 circuit DEMs 2-10 times faster than 512, and windows of one round of columns are much slower. With
4016 debug & 1 (or verbose=True), the binary prints the rounds of a DEM (estimated from the time translation of
4017 its errors by D detectors, 2 <= D <= m/3, i.e., at least three detector layers: D detectors and L columns
4018 per round, also in _last_run_stats["rounds"]; a single round, a folded schedule, or detectors not in time
4019 order give no round structure, which the automatic row slabs of rw_opt 4 use, see dem_rounds) and the
4020 codewords found by the uniform steps, by the window steps, and by the row slabs (see
4021 _parse_stderr_stats()).
4022
4023 RW pairs:
4024 pairs: The RW pairs of non-pivot columns (p=2, as in Lee-Brickell and Stern), passed as pairs=N if not -1: a
4025 RW step also finds the codewords with two non-pivot columns, checking only the pairs which agree on N
4026 random pivot rows (0: off). -1 (default): auto, about one non-pivot column per bucket, with fewer rows
4027 while a codeword of the weight of the upper bound would be kept with probability below 0.8, but enough
4028 rows to keep the pairs of a step within about the work of its elimination (e.g., at least 6 for large
4029 circuit DEMs while the upper bound is far above the distance). The pairs find the minimum-weight
4030 codewords of circuit DEMs 7-26 times faster (per wall time) and lighter codewords of codes with a large
4031 distance. With debug & 1, the binary prints the pairs checked per step and the codewords found by pairs
4032 and by single columns (also in _last_run_stats). The pairs of disjoint codewords are skipped (their sum
4033 is reducible: the binary records only irreducible codewords, its default irred=1).
4034
4035 RW pipeline:
4036 rw_opt: Expert option (since version 0.17.0): the stages of the RW search of the binary, passed as rw_opt=N if
4037 not None (None, the default: the binary's default -1). -1: automatic, the stages which apply to the input
4038 (the rules D1-D5 of doc/rw_triplet_degeneracies.tex), for quantum inputs (codes, CSS sectors, and DEMs): 1;
4039 16 with min_hits > 0 and kwin <= 0; 8 with at most 64 rows of L if the dense m x n matrix exceeds 512 KiB
4040 and n >= 20 m or m >= 1400; 32 when collecting codewords (outC, maxC); 4 for a DEM with a single round
4041 (dem_rounds=1) or without round structure and with at most 640 detectors (see dem_rounds); 2 only if
4042 listed; none for classical codes, nor for runs of at most 2 steps. 0: all stages off (the RW of version
4043 0.16.1, e.g., for regression and ablation runs). A bitmask 1..63: only the stages listed whose input is
4044 there: 1, the weight-3 relations T3 of the columns (found after merge and drop) with the contraction of the
4045 candidates of a RW step (the single-column candidates up to the weight min(dmax + 8, 64), the pairs up to
4046 min(dmax + 1, 64), + dW when collecting) and the Stern filter of its pairs (loss-free for the distance,
4047 i.e., the minimum weight, with the contraction, hence only while dmax + 8 <= 64, + dW when collecting; when
4048 collecting codewords, only with 32: 32 restores the codewords the filter removes through 2 <-> 2 exchanges,
4049 1 -> 2 splits, and 1 <-> 1 swaps of identical columns, e.g., in finH/finL exported from a DEM without
4050 merging, or with merge=0, since version 0.17.2); 2, the
4051 shortening of the candidates by the rows of G (finG; before the contraction of 1); 4, row-slab windows of a
4052 DEM in time order (kwin=0, not with sort_rows=1): on every other step (the others uniform), the columns
4053 inside the first or the last m/2 detectors, i.e., the two detector layers of a single round, which reach
4054 the codewords confined to one layer (e.g., weight 16 of the double-gross DEM with one round), not those
4055 across the layers (hence never slabs only); 8, the sparse-dual elimination (an m x m inverse instead of
4056 the m x n matrix; at most 64 rows of L); 16, the canonical classes of the minimum-weight codewords found by
4057 the uniform RW steps, which the min_hits stopping rule then counts (Good-Turing and Chao2, see min_hits;
4058 only with min_hits > 0, not with kwin > 0; tables of up to 2^24 classes, about 640 MiB); 32, the codewords
4059 collected (outC, maxC) expanded by the T3 2 <-> 2 exchanges and 1 -> 2 splits, and by the 1 <-> 1 swaps of
4060 the identical columns of H and L, also without T3 (see 1).
4061 Only with full-matrix RW (ksub=0) and steps > 0. When the resolved rw_opt is not 0 (see the run plan), the
4062 automatic hybrid windows (kwin=0) are used only for a DEM (matrices: uniform permutations, unless kwin > 0
4063 or win_hyb > 0); an automatic rw_opt which resolves to 0 (rw_opt=0x0 in the run plan, e.g., for a classical
4064 code) keeps the hybrid windows of rw_opt=0. The distance found is valid with any rw_opt, and the cache key
4065 does not depend on it. With debug & 1 (or verbose=True), the binary prints the stages used, |T3|, the
4066 canonical classes, and the Harris-FKG score of the dense full-matrix steps with pairs (with any stage, not
4067 with 8, not on the slab steps; all in _last_run_stats, see _parse_stderr_stats()).
4068
4069 RW stopping criterion:
4070 min_hits: Passed as min_hits=N if not None and >= 0 (None, the default, or a negative value: the binary's
4071 default 5): RW ends once the average number of hits <n> per codeword reaches N, both for the codewords
4072 of the minimum weight found and for a representative set of cov_cws lowest-weight codewords (the hits of
4073 the uniform RW steps, of CC, and of finC count, over the codewords with such a hit; with a nonzero resolved
4074 rw_opt, not those of the row slabs of rw_opt 4 and of the hybrid index windows, which find the same
4075 codewords over and over, but those of the windows of kwin > 0; with a resolved rw_opt of 0, all hits, as in
4076 version 0.16.1; while no codeword of the minimum weight has a counted hit, the stop is inactive, see
4077 _last_run_stats["hits_not_counted"] and explain_bounds()). With the canonical classes of
4078 rw_opt 16 (automatic for quantum codes and DEMs with kwin <= 0 and N > 0), RW ends instead once the
4079 classes of the minimum weight found by the uniform RW steps (C classes, Q1 and Q2 of them found in exactly
4080 one and two steps, M step incidences in all) give M >= max(15, 3 N), M / C >= N, the Good-Turing unseen
4081 mass Q1 / M <= min(0.02, 3 exp(-N)), and the Chao2 unseen fraction C0 / (C + C0) <= 0.05, where
4082 C0 = Q1 (Q1 - 1) / (2 (Q2 + 1)) (with more than 2^24 classes, the rule of <n>). Only the uniform steps
4083 count: while none of them has found a codeword of the minimum weight (e.g., on deep circuit DEMs, where
4084 the window steps find them), this stop is inactive and RW runs until the steps or the timeout end (the
4085 binary says so, and explain_bounds() names the rule which decided). 0: off; then, unless the codewords
4086 are collected (outC or maxC), RW records only the codewords lighter than the upper bound, so that the
4087 repeated hits are not counted.
4088 cov_cws: Size of the representative set of lowest-weight codewords for min_hits, passed as cov_cws=N if not
4089 100 (the default, as in the binary; 0: only the minimum weight).
4090
4091 Stop target:
4092 dstop: The run (method=2 or 3) ends once CC has certified dmin >= dstop, i.e., that there is no codeword of
4093 weight < dstop, unless a lighter codeword is found (default: 0 = off). Unlike dmax, dstop is not an
4094 upper bound and is not reported as dmax: the result is (dmin, w, rw_steps), where w is the weight of the
4095 lightest codeword found (0: none).
4096
4097 Expert CC options:
4098 start: List of CC start columns (int, comma-separated string "a,b,c", or sequence of ints;
4099 None or a single negative value: all columns), passed as start=a,b,c (sorted, distinct).
4100 CC clusters are grown only from the listed columns, and they are not limited to larger
4101 column indices. WARNING: the returned dmin (and an exact result) is valid only if a code
4102 symmetry maps every minimum-weight codeword to one containing a listed column (e.g., one
4103 column per block of a quasi-cyclic code); dmax is always valid.
4104 start_scan: With start (expert option, since version 0.15.1): passed as start_scan=1, so that a cluster
4105 grown from a listed column c only uses the columns > c, as in the scan of all columns (not with fdem).
4106 WARNING: dmin is then valid only if a code symmetry maps every minimum-weight codeword to one whose
4107 smallest column is listed, e.g., if the listed columns are the smallest columns of the orbits of a
4108 group of code automorphisms, one per orbit (start=[0, l] for the two blocks of a two-block
4109 group-algebra code of length 2l over an abelian group). The later start columns then need much less
4110 work, the least if each orbit is a range of consecutive columns.
4111 warn_start: If True (default), issue the start-list warning to stderr.
4112 noscan / cbeg / cend: Disabled in the Python interface: accepted for backward compatibility,
4113 but ignored with a warning to stderr (use the dist_m4ri binary directly).
4114
4115 Experimental RW options:
4116 ksub: Experimental, should not be used: subspace dimension sampled from ker(H) in RW (0: full-matrix RW).
4117 A RW step reduces the span of ksub rows of a fixed basis of ker(H), so that a few codewords are found
4118 much more often than others (min_hits may end RW early).
4119 refresh: RW steps between the basis refreshes of the experimental ksub RW (passed if not None; None, the
4120 default: the binary's 5000 with ksub > 0; 0: no refresh).
4121 warn_ksub: If True (default), issue the warning for ksub > 0 to stderr (with method=1 or 3).
4122
4123 Debug output:
4124 debug: Debug bitmap; the bits in BIN_DBG_MASK are passed to the binary (its diagnostic output on stderr
4125 is printed), and PY_DBG_COMMANDS echoes the command line and the run time. verbose=True implies
4126 the bits VERBOSE_DEBUG. With debug=0 (and verbose=False), the warnings and notes which the binary writes
4127 with any debug value (e.g., on inputs which are ignored, invalid codewords in finC, or the confinement
4128 profile of smax > 0) are forwarded to stderr (since version 0.17.2; except those which the wrapper writes
4129 itself, see _binary_stderr_forwarded()).
4130
4131 Machine-readable binary output (opt-in, off by default; requires dist_m4ri >= 0.17.4):
4132 stamp: If True, passes stamp=1 so progress lines (debug bit 2) and the stop line (debug bit 1) carry the
4133 elapsed search time ' [t=S.SSSs]'. Default: False (not passed).
4134 json_out: Passes json=1 (when True or 1) or json=FILE (when a non-empty path str/Path) to emit the
4135 single-line JSON summary (schema 'dm4ri-result/1'). With json_out=True, the '# RESULT {...}' line on
4136 stderr is also decoded into _last_run_stats['result_json']. Default: None (off, not passed).
4137
4138 Cancellation:
4139 stop_event: Optional threading.Event; once it is set, the binary is terminated and RuntimeError is raised
4140 (the binary is also terminated on any other exception, e.g., KeyboardInterrupt).
4141
4142 Returns:
4143 tuple (dmin, dmax, rw_steps)
4144
4145 Raises:
4146 ValueError: for an invalid option value (e.g., method other than 1, 2, or 3, cc_prune, rw_opt), for
4147 method=2 without wmax, dmax, dstop, or a time limit (timeout=0; an infinite timeout is no limit as well),
4148 for a NaN timeout, or for a MatrixMarket file finH, finG, or finL without columns (n = 0, since version
4149 0.17.2).
4150 FileNotFoundError: if the dist_m4ri binary is not found (see find_dist_m4ri_binary()).
4151 RuntimeError: if the binary exits with an error (the first line of the message has its error message, the
4152 others its stderr), or if stop_event is set.
4153 """
4154 global _last_run_stats
4155 exec_path = find_dist_m4ri_binary(dist_m4ri_path)
4156
4157 start_list = _normalize_start_list(start)
4158 _warn_disabled_options(noscan, cbeg, cend)
4159 if start_scan and not start_list:
4160 _warn_ignored("start_scan=1 has no effect without a start list")
4161 if start_scan and start_list and fdem:
4162 raise ValueError("start_scan=1 is not available with fdem (the equal columns of a DEM are merged)")
4163 start_list = _scan_start_list(start_list, start_scan)
4164 if start_list and warn_start:
4165 sys.stderr.write(_start_warning_text(start_list))
4166 if warn_ksub:
4167 _warn_experimental_ksub(ksub, method)
4168 has_g = not fdem and bool(finG or (fin and not finL)) # (fin=PREFIX: finG=PREFIX + 'Z.mtx' unless finL)
4169 if warn_ortho:
4170 _warn_ortho(ortho, has_g)
4171
4172 finC = check_finc_outc(finC, outC, verbose=False)
4173
4174 if cc_prune is not None and cc_prune not in (0, 1, 2):
4175 raise ValueError(f"invalid cc_prune={cc_prune!r}: cc_prune should be 0, 1, or 2")
4176 _check_rw_opt(rw_opt)
4177 _check_dem_rounds(dem_rounds)
4178 json_arg: Optional[str] = None
4179 if json_out is not None:
4180 if isinstance(json_out, bool):
4181 json_arg = "1" if json_out else None
4182 elif isinstance(json_out, int):
4183 if json_out not in (0, 1):
4184 raise ValueError(f"invalid json_out={json_out!r}: expected None, bool, 0, 1, or a file path")
4185 json_arg = "1" if json_out == 1 else None
4186 elif isinstance(json_out, Path):
4187 s_json = str(json_out)
4188 json_arg = f"./{s_json}" if s_json in ("0", "1") else s_json
4189 elif isinstance(json_out, str):
4190 if not json_out:
4191 raise ValueError("invalid json_out='': expected None, bool, 0, 1, or a file path")
4192 json_arg = None if json_out == "0" else json_out
4193 else:
4194 raise ValueError(f"invalid json_out={json_out!r}: expected None, bool, 0, 1, or a file path")
4195
4196 if method not in (1, 2, 3) or isinstance(method, bool):
4197 raise ValueError(f"invalid method={method!r}: method should be 1 (RW), 2 (CC), or 3 (both)")
4198 _auto_timeout(timeout) # (ValueError for a NaN timeout)
4199 if method == 2 and wmax <= 0 and dmax <= 0 and dstop <= 0 and _auto_timeout(timeout) <= 0.0:
4200 # (with dmax > 0, the binary ends the CC rounds at the latest once the bounds coincide, and with dW > 0 it
4201 # continues to weight dmax + dW for the codewords: wmax is not set to dmax, which would stop at dmax)
4202 raise ValueError("either parameter wmax>0, dmax>0, dstop>0, or timeout>0 should be specified for CC method=2.")
4203 for name, path in (("finH", finH), ("finG", finG), ("finL", finL)):
4204 if path and not fdem and _matrix_num_cols(path) == 0: # (the binary stops with an M4RI error)
4205 raise ValueError(f"invalid {name}={path}: a matrix without columns (n = 0)")
4206
4207 eff_debug = (debug | VERBOSE_DEBUG) if verbose else debug
4208 bin_debug = eff_debug & BIN_DBG_MASK # the higher bits are used by the Python wrapper only
4209 cmd = [exec_path, f"debug={bin_debug}", f"method={method}"]
4210
4211 if finH: cmd.append(f"finH={finH}")
4212 if finG: cmd.append(f"finG={finG}")
4213 if finL: cmd.append(f"finL={finL}")
4214 if fin: cmd.append(f"fin={fin}")
4215 if has_g and not ortho: cmd.append("ortho=0")
4216 if finC: cmd.append(f"finC={finC}")
4217 if fdem: cmd.append(f"fdem={fdem}")
4218 if dmin > 0: cmd.append(f"dmin={dmin}")
4219 if dmax > 0: cmd.append(f"dmax={dmax}")
4220 if dstop > 0: cmd.append(f"dstop={dstop}")
4221 if wmax > 0: cmd.append(f"wmax={wmax}")
4222 if wmin is not None and wmin != 1: cmd.append(f"wmin={wmin}")
4223 if dexp > 0: cmd.append(f"dexp={dexp}")
4224 elif dest > 0: cmd.append(f"dest={dest}")
4225 if steps is not None and steps >= 0: cmd.append(f"steps={steps}")
4226 if threads is not None and threads > 0: cmd.append(f"threads={threads}")
4227 if timeout is not None and timeout >= 0: cmd.append(f"timeout={0 if math.isinf(timeout) else timeout}")
4228 if smax is not None: cmd.append(f"smax={smax}")
4229 if start_list: cmd.append("start=" + ",".join(str(c) for c in start_list))
4230 if start_list and start_scan: cmd.append("start_scan=1")
4231 if css is not None: cmd.append(f"css={css}")
4232 if classical >= 0: cmd.append(f"classical={classical}")
4233 if dW >= 0: cmd.append(f"dW={dW}")
4234 if maxC > 0: cmd.append(f"maxC={maxC}")
4235 if pmin > 0.0: cmd.append(f"pmin={pmin}")
4236 if fdem and not merge: cmd.append("merge=0")
4237 if fdem and drop: cmd.append(f"drop={drop}")
4238 if fdem and outD: cmd.append(f"outD={outD}")
4239 if sort_rows is not None: cmd.append(f"sort_rows={1 if sort_rows else 0}")
4240 if cc_prune is not None: cmd.append(f"cc_prune={int(cc_prune)}")
4241 if outC: cmd.append(f"outC={outC}")
4242 if seed != 0: cmd.append(f"seed={seed}")
4243 if nothrottle: cmd.append("nothrottle=1")
4244 if chunk_size > 0: cmd.append(f"chunk_size={chunk_size}")
4245 if ksub > 0: cmd.append(f"ksub={ksub}")
4246 if kwin != 0: cmd.append(f"kwin={kwin}") # (kwin < 0: no windows)
4247 if win_mode != 0: cmd.append(f"win_mode={win_mode}")
4248 if win_hyb != 0: cmd.append(f"win_hyb={win_hyb}")
4249 if pairs != -1: cmd.append(f"pairs={pairs}")
4250 if min_hits is not None and min_hits >= 0: cmd.append(f"min_hits={min_hits}")
4251 if cov_cws != 100: cmd.append(f"cov_cws={cov_cws}")
4252 if refresh is not None: cmd.append(f"refresh={refresh}")
4253 if rw_opt is not None: cmd.append(f"rw_opt={int(rw_opt)}")
4254 if fdem and dem_rounds: cmd.append(f"dem_rounds={int(dem_rounds)}")
4255 if stamp: cmd.append("stamp=1")
4256 if json_arg is not None: cmd.append(f"json={json_arg}")
4257
4258 if eff_debug & PY_DBG_COMMANDS:
4259 print(f"[dist_m4ri] Running: {' '.join(cmd)}")
4260
4261 t_start = time.time()
4262 proc = subprocess.Popen(cmd, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True)
4263 try:
4264 if stop_event is None:
4265 stdout, stderr = proc.communicate()
4266 else:
4267 while True: # communicate() with a timeout keeps draining the pipes (no deadlock on a full pipe)
4268 try:
4269 stdout, stderr = proc.communicate(timeout=0.05)
4270 break
4271 except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
4272 if stop_event.is_set():
4273 raise RuntimeError("dist_m4ri execution cancelled by stop_event")
4274 except BaseException: # cancelled, KeyboardInterrupt, ...: do not leave the child process running
4275 try:
4276 proc.terminate()
4277 proc.communicate(timeout=1.0)
4278 except Exception:
4279 try:
4280 proc.kill()
4281 proc.wait()
4282 except Exception:
4283 pass
4284 raise
4285
4286 if eff_debug & PY_DBG_COMMANDS:
4287 print(f"[dist_m4ri] Finished in {time.time() - t_start:.3f} s (exit code {proc.returncode})")
4288
4289 if proc.returncode != 0:
4290 err_text = _strip_ansi(stderr or "")
4291 msg = _binary_error_line(err_text)
4292 raise RuntimeError(f"dist_m4ri failed with exit code {proc.returncode}{': ' + msg if msg else ''}\n{err_text}")
4293
4294 _last_run_stats = _parse_stderr_stats(stderr)
4295 if (verbose or bin_debug > 0) and stderr:
4296 print(stderr.rstrip())
4297 elif stderr: # (debug=0: the warnings and notes of the binary, see _binary_stderr_forwarded())
4298 fwd = _binary_stderr_forwarded(stderr)
4299 if fwd:
4300 sys.stderr.write(fwd)
4301
4302 return parse_dist_m4ri_output(stdout)
4303
4304
4305# The warnings of the binary which the wrapper writes itself (see _start_warning_text(), _ksub_warning_text(), and
4306# _warn_ortho()), its notes on drop=FILE (reported by compute_dem_distance()), and '# RESULT ' (decoded into
4307# _last_run_stats['result_json'] by _parse_stderr_stats()): not forwarded at debug=0
4308_BIN_STDERR_OWN = ("# WARNING: start=", "# WARNING: ksub=", "# WARNING: ortho=0", "# Note: drop=", "# RESULT ")
4309
4310
4311def _binary_stderr_forwarded(stderr: str) -> str:
4312 """
4313 The lines of the stderr of a run of the binary with debug=0 which run_dist_m4ri() forwards to sys.stderr (since
4314 version 0.17.2; the binary writes them with any debug value): its warnings on the validity of the inputs and of
4315 the result, its notes, and the confinement profile of smax > 0, except the warnings which the wrapper writes itself
4316 (start, ksub, ortho=0, with their continuation lines '# ...'), the notes on drop=FILE (in _last_run_stats, see
4317 _parse_stderr_stats(); compute_dem_distance() reports them in its own words), and '# RESULT ' (in _last_run_stats
4318 as 'result_json').
4319 """
4320 out: List[str] = []
4321 skip = False
4322 for line in stderr.splitlines():
4323 if skip and line.startswith("# "):
4324 continue
4325 skip = line.startswith(_BIN_STDERR_OWN) or (line.startswith(_K0_NOTE_PREFIX) and not _report_ignored)
4326 if not skip and line.strip():
4327 out.append(line + "\n")
4328 return "".join(out)
4329
4330
4331def _strip_ansi(text: str) -> str:
4332 """The text without the ANSI escape sequences of colors and styles (the ERROR() macro of the binary uses them)."""
4333 import re
4334 return re.sub(r"\x1b\‍[[0-9;]*[A-Za-z]", "", text)
4335
4336
4337def _binary_error_line(stderr: str) -> str:
4338 """The error message of a failed run of the binary on one line (from its stderr; '' if there is none)."""
4339 lines = [s.strip() for s in _strip_ansi(stderr or "").splitlines()]
4340 for k, s in enumerate(lines):
4341 if "*** ERROR" in s: # (the ERROR() macro of the binary: the message is on the next line)
4342 return next((t for t in lines[k + 1:] if t), s)
4343 return next((s for s in lines if s and not s.startswith("#")), "")
4344
4345
4346_MTX_PY_MAX_NNZ = 1 << 16 # temporary MatrixMarket files with up to this many entries are formatted in Python
4347
4348
4349def _gf2_entries(matrix: Any) -> Tuple[int, int, Any, Any]:
4350 """
4351 The shape (m, n) and the nonzero entries (0-based row and column index arrays, in row-major order) of a binary
4352 matrix given as a numpy array (or an array-like, e.g., a list of lists) or a scipy sparse matrix (or array): an
4353 entry is nonzero iff its value is odd (floats are truncated to integers, and the duplicate entries of a sparse
4354 matrix are summed first), as the dist_m4ri binary reads the integer entries of a MatrixMarket file.
4355 """
4356 import numpy as np
4357
4358 def odd(v: Any) -> Any: # the mask of the odd entries
4359 if v.dtype == np.bool_:
4360 return v
4361 if not np.issubdtype(v.dtype, np.integer):
4362 v = v.astype(np.int64)
4363 v = v & 1
4364 return v.view(np.bool_) if v.itemsize == 1 else v != 0
4365
4366 if hasattr(matrix, "tocsr"): # a scipy sparse matrix or array
4367 csr = matrix.tocsr()
4368 if not csr.has_canonical_format: # duplicates summed and columns sorted (not in the caller's matrix)
4369 csr = csr.copy() if csr is matrix else csr
4370 csr.sum_duplicates()
4371 m, n = csr.shape
4372 keep = odd(csr.data)
4373 rows = np.repeat(np.arange(m, dtype=np.int64), np.diff(csr.indptr))[keep]
4374 return m, n, rows, csr.indices[keep]
4375 A = np.asarray(matrix)
4376 if A.ndim != 2:
4377 raise ValueError(f"a matrix should have two dimensions, got the shape {A.shape}")
4378 m, n = A.shape
4379 if m == 0 or n == 0:
4380 empty = np.zeros(0, dtype=np.int64)
4381 return m, n, empty, empty
4382 rows, cols = np.divmod(np.flatnonzero(odd(A)), n) # (flatnonzero of a bool array is fast, unlike nonzero)
4383 return m, n, rows, cols
4384
4385
4386def _write_mtx_gf2(path: str, matrix: Any) -> None:
4387 """
4388 Writes a binary matrix (numpy array, array-like, or scipy sparse matrix; see _gf2_entries()) to the file `path` in
4389 the MatrixMarket coordinate pattern format (the 1-based indices of the nonzero entries, in row-major order), which
4390 the dist_m4ri binary reads. With up to _MTX_PY_MAX_NNZ nonzero entries, the file is formatted in Python (e.g.,
4391 about 1 ms for 6000 entries); larger matrices are written by scipy.io.mmwrite, which is faster per entry, but has a
4392 fixed cost of about 10 ms per call on a 128-core machine (the thread pool of its parallel writer).
4393 """
4394 import numpy as np
4395 m, n, rows, cols = _gf2_entries(matrix)
4396 nnz = len(rows)
4397 if nnz > _MTX_PY_MAX_NNZ:
4398 from scipy.io import mmwrite
4399 from scipy.sparse import coo_matrix
4400 mmwrite(path, coo_matrix((np.ones(nnz, dtype=np.int8), (rows, cols)), shape=(m, n)), field="pattern",
4401 symmetry="general")
4402 return
4403 rc = np.empty(2 * nnz, dtype=np.int64) # the interleaved 1-based row and column indices
4404 rc[0::2], rc[1::2] = rows, cols
4405 rc += 1
4406 with open(path, "w") as f:
4407 f.write(f"%%MatrixMarket matrix coordinate pattern general\n{m} {n} {nnz}\n")
4408 f.write(("%d %d\n" * nnz) % tuple(rc.tolist()))
4409
4410
4411def _matrix_to_file(matrix, extension: str = ".mtx", temp_dir: str = "tmp") -> str:
4412 """
4413 The MatrixMarket file of a matrix for the dist_m4ri binary: a file path is returned as is; a numpy array (or an
4414 array-like) or a scipy sparse matrix is written to a new temporary file in temp_dir with _write_mtx_gf2() (its
4415 nonzero entries over GF(2), i.e., those with an odd value; before version 0.15.2, scipy.io.mmwrite wrote the int8
4416 entries, which took 10-13 ms per matrix with up to 1000 columns on a 128-core machine).
4417 """
4418 if isinstance(matrix, (str, Path)):
4419 return str(matrix)
4420 path = create_unique_file(directory=temp_dir, extension=extension)
4421 _write_mtx_gf2(path, matrix)
4422 return path
4423
4424
4425def _matrix_num_cols(matrix: Any) -> int:
4426 """
4427 The number of columns of a matrix: a numpy array (or an array-like), a scipy sparse matrix, or a MatrixMarket file
4428 (from its size line); -1 if unknown (e.g., for a file in another format, or a one-dimensional array).
4429 """
4430 if isinstance(matrix, (str, Path)):
4431 try:
4432 with open(str(matrix)) as f:
4433 if not f.readline().startswith("%%MatrixMarket"):
4434 return -1
4435 for line in f:
4436 parts = line.split()
4437 if parts and not parts[0].startswith("%"):
4438 return int(parts[1]) if len(parts) >= 2 else -1
4439 except (OSError, ValueError, UnicodeDecodeError):
4440 return -1
4441 return -1
4442 shape = getattr(matrix, "shape", None)
4443 if shape is None:
4444 import numpy as np
4445 try:
4446 shape = np.asarray(matrix).shape
4447 except Exception: # (not an array-like)
4448 return -1
4449 return int(shape[1]) if len(shape) == 2 else -1
4450
4451
4452def _check_has_columns(kind: str, *matrices: Any) -> None:
4453 """
4454 ValueError for a matrix without columns (n = 0, see _matrix_num_cols()) among the inputs of a code: since version
4455 0.17.2, with every engine (the binary stopped with an M4RI error).
4456 """
4457 if any(M is not None and _matrix_num_cols(M) == 0 for M in matrices):
4458 raise ValueError(f"invalid {kind} input: a matrix without columns (n = 0)")

4461def has_noise(circuit: Any) -> bool:
4462 """
4463 Checks if a Stim circuit (stim.Circuit or a .stim file) has noise: a noise channel (e.g., DEPOLARIZE1, X_ERROR,
4464 PAULI_CHANNEL_2, E, or HERALDED_ERASE), or a measurement with a flip probability (e.g., M(0.001) or MPP(0.01)),
4465 i.e., if strip_noise() changes it.
4466 """
4467 try:
4468 stim = _get_stim()
4469 except ImportError:
4470 return False
4471 if isinstance(circuit, (str, Path)):
4472 circuit = stim.Circuit.from_file(str(circuit))
4473 if not isinstance(circuit, stim.Circuit):
4474 return False
4475 return circuit.without_noise() != circuit
4476
4477
4478def strip_noise(circuit: Any) -> Any:
4479 """
4480 Removes all noise from a Stim circuit (stim.Circuit or a .stim file), see stim.Circuit.without_noise(): the noise
4481 channels (e.g., DEPOLARIZE1, X_ERROR, PAULI_CHANNEL_2, E) are removed, the measurements lose their flip
4482 probabilities (M(0.001) becomes M), and heralded noise (e.g., HERALDED_ERASE) is replaced by MPAD, so that the
4483 measurement record does not change. E.g., add_noise(strip_noise(circuit), p) (or add_noise(circuit, p,
4484 force=True); CLI: --force-noise) gives circuits with the same noise model.
4485
4486 Returns:
4487 The noiseless stim.Circuit.
4488 """
4489 stim = _get_stim()
4490 if isinstance(circuit, (str, Path)):
4491 circuit = stim.Circuit.from_file(str(circuit))
4492 return circuit.without_noise()
4493
4494
4495def _add_noise_recursive(
4496 circuit: Any, p: float, num_qubits: int, active_qubits: Set[int]
4497) -> Any:
4498 """Recursively adds uniform circuit-level noise to a Stim circuit (see add_noise())."""
4499 stim = _get_stim()
4500 p1 = 0.1 * p # one-qubit depolarizing noise (after one-qubit gates, on idle qubits)
4501 noisy_circuit = stim.Circuit()
4502 for inst in circuit:
4503 if isinstance(inst, stim.CircuitRepeatBlock):
4504 rep_count = inst.repeat_count
4505 if rep_count <= 0:
4506 continue
4507 body = inst.body_copy()
4508 entry_active = set(active_qubits)
4509 first_body = _add_noise_recursive(
4510 body, p, num_qubits, active_qubits
4511 )
4512 if rep_count == 1 or active_qubits == entry_active:
4513 noisy_circuit.append(
4514 stim.CircuitRepeatBlock(rep_count, first_body)
4515 )
4516 else:
4517 rest_active = set(active_qubits)
4518 rest_body = _add_noise_recursive(
4519 body, p, num_qubits, rest_active
4520 )
4521 active_qubits.clear()
4522 active_qubits.update(rest_active)
4523 if rest_body == first_body:
4524 noisy_circuit.append(
4525 stim.CircuitRepeatBlock(rep_count, first_body)
4526 )
4527 else:
4528 noisy_circuit += first_body
4529 noisy_circuit.append(
4530 stim.CircuitRepeatBlock(rep_count - 1, rest_body)
4531 )
4532 continue
4533 name = inst.name
4534 if name == "TICK":
4535 idle_qubits = set(range(num_qubits)) - active_qubits
4536 if idle_qubits:
4537 noisy_circuit.append("DEPOLARIZE1", sorted(idle_qubits), p1)
4538 noisy_circuit.append(inst)
4539 active_qubits.clear()
4540 continue
4541 gd = stim.gate_data(name)
4542 noise_channel = gd.is_noisy_gate and (not gd.produces_measurements or 0 not in gd.num_parens_arguments_range)
4543 if name == "MPAD" or noise_channel or not (gd.is_unitary or gd.is_reset or gd.produces_measurements):
4544 # annotations (DETECTOR, OBSERVABLE_INCLUDE, QUBIT_COORDS, SHIFT_COORDS), MPAD (its targets are bits, not
4545 # qubits), and the noise channels of a noisy circuit (also HERALDED_ERASE): no noise, not an operation
4546 noisy_circuit.append(inst)
4547 continue
4548 targets = inst.targets_copy()
4549 # qubit_value is None for measurement records (rec[-k]), sweep bits (sweep[k]), and combiners (*)
4550 qubits = [t.qubit_value for t in targets if t.qubit_value is not None]
4551 active_qubits.update(qubits)
4552 flip = "Z_ERROR" if name.endswith("X") else "X_ERROR" # (RX, MX, MRX: X basis; Z or Y basis otherwise)
4553 if gd.produces_measurements and gd.is_single_qubit_gate: # M, MX, MY, MR, MRX, MRY
4554 if qubits:
4555 noisy_circuit.append(flip, qubits, p)
4556 noisy_circuit.append(inst)
4557 if gd.is_reset and qubits:
4558 noisy_circuit.append(flip, qubits, p)
4559 elif gd.is_reset and not gd.produces_measurements: # R, RX, RY
4560 noisy_circuit.append(inst)
4561 if qubits:
4562 noisy_circuit.append(flip, qubits, p)
4563 elif gd.is_unitary and gd.is_single_qubit_gate: # I, X, H, H_XY, S, SQRT_X, C_XYZ, ...
4564 noisy_circuit.append(inst)
4565 if qubits:
4566 noisy_circuit.append("DEPOLARIZE1", qubits, p1)
4567 elif gd.is_unitary and gd.is_two_qubit_gate: # CX, CZ, XCY, SWAP, ISWAP, SQRT_XX, CXSWAP, II, ...
4568 noisy_circuit.append(inst)
4569 pair_qubits: List[int] = []
4570 ctrl_qubits: List[int] = [] # the qubits of the classically controlled pairs (e.g., CX rec[-1] 5)
4571 for a, b in zip(targets[::2], targets[1::2]):
4572 if a.qubit_value is not None and b.qubit_value is not None:
4573 pair_qubits += [a.qubit_value, b.qubit_value]
4574 else:
4575 ctrl_qubits += [t.qubit_value for t in (a, b) if t.qubit_value is not None]
4576 if pair_qubits:
4577 noisy_circuit.append("DEPOLARIZE2", pair_qubits, p)
4578 if ctrl_qubits:
4579 noisy_circuit.append("DEPOLARIZE1", ctrl_qubits, p1)
4580 else: # multi-qubit measurements (MPP, MXX, MYY, MZZ) and Pauli product gates (SPP, SPP_DAG): no noise
4581 noisy_circuit.append(inst)
4582 return noisy_circuit
4583
4584
4585def add_noise(circuit: Any, p: float = 0.001, force: bool = False) -> Any:
4586 """
4587 Adds uniform circuit-level noise of strength p to a Stim circuit (the gates are classified by stim.gate_data()):
4588 - DEPOLARIZE2(p) after two-qubit gates (CX, CY, CZ, XCX, XCY, XCZ, YCX, YCY, YCZ, SWAP, ISWAP, ISWAP_DAG, SQRT_XX,
4589 SQRT_YY, SQRT_ZZ and their _DAG versions, CXSWAP, SWAPCX, CZSWAP, II); a classically controlled gate (e.g.,
4590 CX rec[-1] 5 or CZ sweep[0] 5) gets DEPOLARIZE1(p/10) on its qubit;
4591 - DEPOLARIZE1(p/10) after one-qubit gates (I, X, Y, Z, H, H_XY, H_YZ, S, S_DAG, SQRT_X, SQRT_Y and their _DAG
4592 versions, C_XYZ, C_ZYX, and the other variants), and on the qubits idle since the previous TICK (at each TICK,
4593 peeling the first iteration of a REPEAT block when its entry and exit active sets differ, and at the end of the
4594 circuit);
4595 - X (Z) flips with probability p after Z-basis or Y-basis (X-basis) resets and before measurements, both before and
4596 after a measurement with reset (MR, MRX, MRY);
4597 - none for the multi-qubit measurements (MPP, MXX, MYY, MZZ) and the Pauli product gates (SPP, SPP_DAG).
4598 The noise of a noisy circuit is kept and the uniform noise is added to it, unless force=True: then it is replaced
4599 (see strip_noise()).
4600
4601 Args:
4602 circuit: stim.Circuit or path to a .stim file.
4603 p: Noise strength (for the distance, only which errors are possible matters); p=0: no noise is added.
4604 force: If True, all noise of the circuit is removed first (with p=0: only that).
4605
4606 Returns:
4607 The noisy stim.Circuit (a copy).
4608 """
4609 stim = _get_stim()
4610 if isinstance(circuit, (str, Path)):
4611 circuit = stim.Circuit.from_file(str(circuit))
4612 if force:
4613 circuit = strip_noise(circuit)
4614 if p <= 0.0:
4615 return circuit.copy()
4616 num_qubits = circuit.num_qubits
4617 active_qubits: Set[int] = set()
4618 noisy_circuit = _add_noise_recursive(circuit, p, num_qubits, active_qubits)
4619 if active_qubits:
4620 final_idle_qubits = set(range(num_qubits)) - active_qubits
4621 if final_idle_qubits:
4622 noisy_circuit.append("DEPOLARIZE1", sorted(final_idle_qubits), 0.1 * p)
4623 return noisy_circuit
4624
4625
4626def remove_empty_detectors(circuit: Any) -> Tuple[Any, int]:
4627 """Removes DETECTOR instructions that have no measurement record targets.
4628
4629 Args:
4630 circuit: A stim.Circuit instance (not a file path).
4631
4632 Returns:
4633 Tuple of (new_circuit, removed_count), where removed_count weights empty
4634 DETECTOR instructions inside REPEAT blocks by their repeat_count
4635 multiplicity.
4636 """
4637 stim = _get_stim()
4638 new_circuit = stim.Circuit()
4639 removed = 0
4640 for inst in circuit:
4641 if isinstance(inst, stim.CircuitRepeatBlock):
4642 body, r = remove_empty_detectors(inst.body_copy())
4643 removed += r * inst.repeat_count
4644 new_circuit.append(stim.CircuitRepeatBlock(inst.repeat_count, body))
4645 elif inst.name == "DETECTOR":
4646 rec_targets = [
4647 t for t in inst.targets_copy()
4648 if t.is_measurement_record_target
4649 ]
4650 if not rec_targets:
4651 removed += 1
4652 else:
4653 new_circuit.append(inst)
4654 else:
4655 new_circuit.append(inst)
4656 return new_circuit, removed
4657
4658
4659def has_repeat_block(circuit: Any) -> bool:
4660 """Checks if a Stim circuit contains at least one REPEAT block."""
4661 stim = _get_stim()
4662 if isinstance(circuit, (str, Path)):
4663 circuit = stim.Circuit.from_file(str(circuit))
4664 if not isinstance(circuit, stim.Circuit):
4665 return False
4666 for inst in circuit:
4667 if isinstance(inst, stim.CircuitRepeatBlock):
4668 return True
4669 return False
