6128def _dem_pmin_cut(dem: Any, pmin: float) -> Any:
6129 """
6130 The DEM (a stim.DetectorErrorModel, a .dem file, or the text of a DEM) without its error mechanisms of probability
6131 < pmin, as the dist_m4ri binary reads it with pmin=...: a flattened stim.DetectorErrorModel (the other instructions
6132 kept). Used for engine='cert' with pmin > 0 (since version 0.17.2; qec_cert has no such cutoff).
6133 """
6134 stim = _get_stim()
6135 if isinstance(dem, (str, Path)) and os.path.isfile(str(dem)):
6136 dem = stim.DetectorErrorModel.from_file(str(dem))
6137 elif not isinstance(dem, stim.DetectorErrorModel):
6138 dem = stim.DetectorErrorModel(str(dem))
6139 out = stim.DetectorErrorModel()
6140 for inst in dem.flattened():
6141 if inst.type == "error" and inst.args_copy()[0] < pmin:
6142 continue
6143 out.append(inst)
6144 return out
6145
6146
6147def _dem_instruction_parts(line: str) -> Tuple[str, str, str]:
6148 """
6149 The parts (name, args, rest) of a line of a DEM, e.g., ('error', '0.01', 'D0 D1 L0') for 'error[tag](0.01) D0 D1
6150 L0 # comment': the name of the instruction (without its tag in brackets, which stim writes since version 1.15 and
6151 which may contain spaces, '#', and backslash escapes), the text in the parentheses ('' if none), and the targets,
6152 without the comment; ('}', '', '') for the end of a repeat block, and ('', '', '') for a blank or comment line.
6153 """
6154 s = line.strip()
6155 if not s or s[0] == '#':
6156 return "", "", ""
6157 if s[0] == '}':
6158 return "}", "", ""
6159 i = 0
6160 while i < len(s) and (s[i].isalnum() or s[i] == '_'):
6161 i += 1
6162 name, j = s[:i], i
6163 if j < len(s) and s[j] == '[': # the tag: up to the first ']' which is not escaped
6164 j += 1
6165 while j < len(s) and s[j] != ']':
6166 j += 2 if s[j] == '\\' else 1
6167 j = min(j + 1, len(s))
6168 rest = s[j:].split('#', 1)[0].strip()
6169 if rest.startswith('('):
6170 k = rest.find(')')
6171 return (name, rest[1:].strip(), "") if k < 0 else (name, rest[1:k].strip(), rest[k + 1:].strip())
6172 return name, "", rest
6173
6174
6175def _dem_error_columns(dem: Any, pmin: float = 0.0, with_prob: bool = False) -> List[Tuple[Any, ...]]:
6176 """
6177 The columns of a DEM (a stim.DetectorErrorModel, or a .dem file) as read by the dist_m4ri binary: the detector and
6178 observable sets of its error mechanisms, in their order in the flattened DEM (repeat blocks unrolled, with
6179 shift_detectors), after the probability cutoff pmin (an error with probability < pmin is skipped). The components
6180 of a decomposed error (separated by '^') are summed mod 2, so that a target listed twice cancels. With
6181 with_prob=True, each column also has the probability of the error, as written: (detectors, observables, p).
6182 """
6183 if isinstance(dem, str) and ("\n" in dem or "(" in dem) and not os.path.isfile(dem):
6184 lines = dem.splitlines()
6185 elif isinstance(dem, (str, Path)):
6186 with open(str(dem)) as f:
6187 lines = f.read().splitlines()
6188 else:
6189 lines = str(dem.flattened() if hasattr(dem, 'flattened') else dem).splitlines()
6190 cols: List[Tuple[Any, ...]] = []
6191
6192 def block(i: int, shift: int) -> Tuple[int, int]:
6193 # runs the instructions from line i up to the closing brace (or the end): (next line, detector shift)
6194 while i < len(lines):
6195 name, args, rest = _dem_instruction_parts(lines[i])
6196 i += 1
6197 if not name:
6198 continue
6199 if name == '}':
6200 return i, shift
6201 if name == 'repeat':
6202 count = int(rest.split()[0])
6203 body, end = i, i
6204 for _ in range(count):
6205 end, shift = block(body, shift)
6206 if count <= 0: # skip the body
6207 depth = 1
6208 while end < len(lines) and depth > 0:
6209 nm = _dem_instruction_parts(lines[end])[0]
6210 end += 1
6211 depth += (nm == 'repeat') - (nm == '}')
6212 i = end
6213 elif name == 'shift_detectors':
6214 shift += int(rest.split()[-1])
6215 elif name == 'error':
6216 p_text = args
6217 if float(p_text) < pmin:
6218 continue
6219 dets: Set[int] = set()
6220 obs: Set[int] = set()
6221 for tok in rest.split():
6222 if tok[0] == 'D':
6223 dets ^= {int(tok[1:]) + shift}
6224 elif tok[0] == 'L':
6225 obs ^= {int(tok[1:])}
6226 col = (frozenset(dets), frozenset(obs))
6227 cols.append(col + (p_text,) if with_prob else col)
6228 return i, shift
6229
6230 block(0, 0)
6231 return cols
6232
6233
6234def _dem_k0(dem: Any, pmin: float = 0.0) -> bool:
6235 """
6236 Whether a DEM (a stim.DetectorErrorModel, a .dem file, or DEM text) has no logical codeword (k = 0) after the
6237 probability cutoff pmin, checked on the reduced (merged equal columns, zero columns dropped) matrices (H, L),
6238 which have the same k as the raw DEM. Uses qec_cert's C DEM parser when available and pmin <= 0.
6239 """
6240 import numpy as np
6241 import scipy.sparse as sp
6242 if pmin <= 0.0 and _qec_cert_available():
6243 try:
6244 _get_qec_cert()
6245 from qec_cert import prep as _qc_prep
6246 if hasattr(dem, "flattened"):
6247 raw_bytes = str(dem.flattened()).encode("utf-8")
6248 elif isinstance(dem, (str, Path)) and os.path.isfile(str(dem)):
6249 with open(str(dem), "rb") as f:
6250 raw_bytes = f.read()
6251 else:
6252 raw_bytes = str(dem).encode("utf-8")
6253 if b"repeat" in raw_bytes:
6254 raise ValueError("unflattened repeat block")
6255 parsed = _qc_prep.parse_dem_text(raw_bytes, merge_parallel=True, strip_zero=True)
6256 num_det = int(parsed["num_detectors"])
6257 num_obs = int(parsed["num_observables"])
6258 indptr = parsed["col_indptr"]
6259 indices = parsed["col_indices"]
6260 col_obs = parsed["col_obs"]
6261 n_cols = len(indptr) - 1
6262 if num_obs == 0 or n_cols == 0 or not np.any(col_obs):
6263 return True
6264 if np.any((np.diff(indptr) == 0) & (col_obs != 0)):
6265 return False
6266 H = sp.csc_matrix((np.ones(len(indices), dtype=np.uint8), indices, indptr), shape=(num_det, n_cols)).tocsr()
6267 obs_r, obs_c = [], []
6268 for b in range(num_obs):
6269 cs = np.flatnonzero((col_obs >> b) & 1)
6270 if cs.size:
6271 obs_r.extend([b] * int(cs.size))
6272 obs_c.extend(cs.tolist())
6273 L = sp.csr_matrix((np.ones(len(obs_r), dtype=np.uint8), (obs_r, obs_c)), shape=(num_obs, n_cols))
6274 return _k0_of_matrices(H, L=L)
6275 except Exception:
6276 pass
6277 cols = _dem_error_columns(dem, pmin=pmin)
6278 seen: Set[Tuple[frozenset, frozenset]] = set()
6279 h_r: List[int] = []
6280 h_c: List[int] = []
6281 l_r: List[int] = []
6282 l_c: List[int] = []
6283 max_d = max_o = -1
6284 out_c = 0
6285 for dets, obs in cols:
6286 if not dets and not obs:
6287 continue
6288 if not dets and obs:
6289 return False
6290 key = (dets, obs)
6291 if key in seen:
6292 continue
6293 seen.add(key)
6294 for d in dets:
6295 if d > max_d:
6296 max_d = d
6297 h_r.append(d)
6298 h_c.append(out_c)
6299 for o in obs:
6300 if o > max_o:
6301 max_o = o
6302 l_r.append(o)
6303 l_c.append(out_c)
6304 out_c += 1
6305 if not l_r or out_c == 0:
6306 return True
6307 H = sp.csr_matrix((np.ones(len(h_r), dtype=np.uint8), (h_r, h_c)), shape=(max_d + 1, out_c))
6308 L = sp.csr_matrix((np.ones(len(l_r), dtype=np.uint8), (l_r, l_c)), shape=(max_o + 1, out_c))
6309 return _k0_of_matrices(H, L=L)
6310
6311
6312def _drop_mode(drop: Any) -> str:
6313 """
6314 The drop option of compute_dem_distance(): "auto" (for None, True, 1, "1", or "auto"), "0" (False, 0, or "0"),
6315 "css", or the name of an existing file (ValueError otherwise).
6316 """
6317 if drop is None or drop is True:
6318 return "auto"
6319 if drop is False:
6320 return "0"
6321 if isinstance(drop, numbers.Integral):
6322 if drop in (0, 1):
6323 return "auto" if drop == 1 else "0"
6324 raise ValueError(f"invalid drop={drop}: use 0, 1, 'auto', 'css', or a file with the detectors to drop")
6325 s = str(drop).strip()
6326 if s.lower() in ("1", "auto"):
6327 return "auto"
6328 if s == "0":
6329 return "0"
6330 if s.lower() == "css":
6331 return "css"
6332 if not os.path.isfile(s):
6333 raise ValueError(f"drop={s}: no such file (use 0, 1, auto, css, or a file with the detectors to drop)")
6334 return s
6335
6336
6337def _reduced_out_prefix(spec: Union[bool, str, Path], src: str, out_dir: Optional[Union[str, Path]] = None) -> str:
6338 """
6339 The prefix PREFIX of the files PREFIX_red.dem and PREFIX_red.json of compute_dem_distance(out_reduced=spec) for the
6340 input src (a file name, or e.g. 'stim.Circuit'): for True (also '', '1', 'true', 'yes', 'auto'), the basename of
6341 the input file (without a suffix _full or _simp; 'dem' for an object); a bare name goes to out_dir (default: the
6342 directory of the input file, as for --out-dem), and a path is used as given.
6343 """
6344 src_path = Path(src) if os.path.exists(src) else None
6345 eff_dir = Path(out_dir) if out_dir is not None else (src_path.parent if src_path is not None else Path("."))
6346 if spec is True or (isinstance(spec, str) and spec.strip().lower() in ("", "1", "true", "yes", "auto")):
6347 stem = src_path.stem if src_path is not None else "dem"
6348 if stem.endswith(("_full", "_simp")):
6349 stem = stem[:-5]
6350 return str(eff_dir / stem)
6351 spec_s = str(spec)
6352 return str(eff_dir / spec_s) if (not os.path.isabs(spec_s) and os.path.dirname(spec_s) == "") else spec_s
6353
6354
6355def read_drop_file(path: Union[str, Path]) -> Tuple[List[int], Optional[int]]:
6356 """
6357 Reads a drop file: the 0-based detector indices (k for Dk) separated by white space or commas, where lines starting
6358 with '#' or '%' are comments, e.g., the detectors dropped from a DEM written by the binary (outD=FILE).
6359
6360 Returns:
6361 (detectors, num_detectors): the sorted distinct detectors, and the number of detectors of the DEM from the
6362 comment line '# N of M detectors dropped ...' written by the binary (None if there is none).
6363
6364 Raises:
6365 ValueError: for an entry which is not a non-negative integer (as the binary; since version 0.17.2).
6366 """
6367 import re
6368 dets: Set[int] = set()
6369 num: Optional[int] = None
6370 with open(str(path)) as f:
6371 for lineno, line in enumerate(f, start=1):
6372 s = line.strip()
6373 if s.startswith('#') or s.startswith('%'):
6374 mm = re.match(r"#\s*\d+ of (\d+) detectors dropped", s)
6375 if mm and num is None:
6376 num = int(mm.group(1))
6377 continue
6378 for tok in s.replace(',', ' ').split():
6379 try:
6380 v = int(tok)
6381 except ValueError:
6382 v = -1
6383 if v < 0: # (as the binary: an error since version 0.17.2)
6384 raise ValueError(f"drop file '{path}', line {lineno}: invalid entry '{tok}' (expected 0-based "
6385 f"detector indices)")
6386 dets.add(v)
6387 return sorted(dets), num
6388
6389
6390def write_reduced_dem(
6391 dem: Any,
6392 dropped: Sequence[int],
6393 prefix: Union[str, Path],
6394 pmin: float = 0.0,
6395 num_detectors: Optional[int] = None,
6396 meta: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None
6397) -> Tuple[str, str]:
6398 """
6399 Writes the DEM (a stim.DetectorErrorModel or a .dem file) without the detectors `dropped` (0-based, e.g., those
6400 dropped by the binary, see compute_dem_distance(outD=..., out_reduced=...); an index of no detector of the DEM is
6401 ignored, as by the binary, and a negative one is a ValueError, since version 0.17.2) to PREFIX_red.dem: the
6402 errors which touch none of them (after the cutoff pmin, in the order of the flattened DEM; a decomposed error as
6403 the sum of its components), with the other detectors numbered consecutively, and the observables unchanged. The
6404 maps go to PREFIX_red.json: "detectors" (the original index of each detector of the reduced DEM, i.e., the
6405 complement of "dropped"), "errors" (the original index of each error of the reduced DEM, 0-based in the order of
6406 the flattened DEM after the cutoff pmin, as the columns of the codewords in outC), "dropped", "num_detectors",
6407 "num_errors", "pmin", and the entries of meta. If dropping the detectors is exact (as verified by the binary),
6408 the reduced DEM has the same distance, and its codewords map to codewords of the DEM with "errors".
6409
6410 Returns:
6411 (dem_path, json_path): the files written.
6412 """
6413 cols = _dem_error_columns(dem, pmin, with_prob=True)
6414 if any(int(r) < 0 for r in dropped):
6415 raise ValueError("write_reduced_dem: negative detector index in dropped")
6416 m = 1 + max((d for S, _, _ in cols for d in S), default=-1)
6417 if num_detectors is not None:
6418 m = max(m, int(num_detectors))
6419 else:
6420 m = max(m, _dem_num_detectors(dem))
6421 drop_set = set(int(r) for r in dropped if int(r) < m) # (a larger index is ignored, as by the binary)
6422 k = 1 + max((o for _, O, _ in cols for o in O), default=-1)
6423 kept = [r for r in range(m) if r not in drop_set]
6424 new_index = {r: i for i, r in enumerate(kept)}
6425 dem_path, json_path = f"{prefix}_red.dem", f"{prefix}_red.json"
6426 errors: List[int] = []
6427 lines = [f"# reduced DEM: {len(drop_set)} of {m} detectors dropped (dist_m4ri.py {__version__}); the maps to the "
6428 f"original DEM are in {os.path.basename(json_path)}"]
6429 max_det = max_obs = -1
6430 for j, (S, O, p) in enumerate(cols):
6431 if S & drop_set:
6432 continue
6433 dets = sorted(new_index[d] for d in S)
6434 obs = sorted(O)
6435 if dets:
6436 max_det = max(max_det, dets[-1])
6437 if obs:
6438 max_obs = max(max_obs, obs[-1])
6439 lines.append(f"error({p})" + "".join(f" D{d}" for d in dets) + "".join(f" L{o}" for o in obs))
6440 errors.append(j)
6441 if max_det < len(kept) - 1: # (keeps the number of detectors and observables)
6442 lines.append(f"detector D{len(kept) - 1}")
6443 if max_obs < k - 1:
6444 lines.append(f"logical_observable L{k - 1}")
6445 parent_dir = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(dem_path))
6446 os.makedirs(parent_dir, exist_ok=True)
6447 with open(dem_path, "w") as f:
6448 f.write("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
6449 info: Dict[str, Any] = {"__version__": __version__}
6450 info.update(meta or {})
6451 info.update({"pmin": pmin, "num_detectors": m, "num_errors": len(cols), "dropped": sorted(drop_set),
6452 "detectors": kept, "errors": errors})
6453 with open(json_path, "w") as f:
6454 json.dump(info, f, separators=(",", ":"))
6455 f.write("\n")
6456 return dem_path, json_path
6457
6458
6459_EXPAND_MAX = 1 << 22 # the most codewords of _expand_equal_columns() without maxC (as the expansion of the binary)
6460
6461
6462def _expand_equal_columns(
6463 cws: List[List[int]],
6464 dem: Any,
6465 pmin: float = 0.0,
6466 maxC: int = 0,
6467 verbose: bool = False
6468) -> List[List[int]]:
6469 """
6470 The expanded list of the DEM codewords cws (0-based columns of the DEM, see _dem_error_columns()): every version
6471 over the choices among equal columns (the same detectors and observables), which the binary merges (merge=1).
6472 Each codeword is mapped to the first columns of its sets of equal columns (two equal columns cancel), and every
6473 distinct result c is expanded into the prod_{j in c} |set(j)| codewords with one column from each set (sorted, in
6474 the order of cws). At most maxC codewords are returned (without maxC: at most _EXPAND_MAX = 2^22, as the binary
6475 caps its own expansion, since version 0.17.2), with a warning to stderr if some are dropped.
6476 """
6477 if not cws:
6478 return []
6479 cols = _dem_error_columns(dem, pmin)
6480 sets: Dict[Tuple[frozenset, frozenset], List[int]] = {}
6481 for j, c in enumerate(cols):
6482 sets.setdefault(c, []).append(j)
6483 members = [sets[c] for c in cols] # the sorted set of the columns equal to column j (j included)
6484 keys: List[Tuple[int, ...]] = []
6485 seen: Set[Tuple[int, ...]] = set()
6486 for cw in cws:
6487 if any(j < 0 or j >= len(members) for j in cw):
6488 raise ValueError(f"expand: codeword column out of range (the DEM has {len(members)} columns after the "
6489 f"pmin={pmin} cutoff)")
6490 odd: Set[int] = set()
6491 for j in cw:
6492 odd ^= {members[j][0]}
6493 key = tuple(sorted(odd))
6494 if key and key not in seen:
6495 seen.add(key)
6496 keys.append(key)
6497 total = 0
6498 for key in keys:
6499 num = 1
6500 for r in key:
6501 num *= len(members[r])
6502 total += num
6503 cap = maxC if maxC > 0 else _EXPAND_MAX # (without maxC: at most _EXPAND_MAX codewords, since version 0.17.2)
6504 limit = min(total, cap)
6505 out: List[List[int]] = []
6506 for key in keys:
6507 if len(out) >= limit:
6508 break
6509 for choice in itertools.product(*(members[r] for r in key)):
6510 out.append(sorted(choice))
6511 if len(out) >= limit:
6512 break
6513 if limit < total:
6514 what = f"maxC={maxC}" if maxC > 0 else f"{_EXPAND_MAX} (without maxC)"
6515 sys.stderr.write(f"# Warning: expand: the expanded list has {total} codewords ({len(keys)} up to equal "
6516 f"columns); only the first {what} are written (the list is incomplete)\n")
6517 elif verbose:
6518 print(f"[dist_m4ri] expand: {len(keys)} codewords up to equal columns -> {total} codewords")
6519 return out
6520
6521
6522def _css_sector_codes(Hx: Any, Hz: Any, Lx: Optional[Any], Lz: Optional[Any]) -> Dict[str, Tuple[Any, Any, Any]]:
6523 """The quantum codes (H, G, L) of the two sectors of a CSS code: Z -> (Hx, Hz or Lx), X -> (Hz, Hx or Lz)."""
6524 return {
6525 "Z": (Hx, Hz if Lx is None else None, Lx),
6526 "X": (Hz, Hx if Lz is None else None, Lz),
6527 }
6528
6529
6530def _css_combine(
6531 x: Tuple[int, int, int], z: Tuple[int, int, int], dmax: int = 0
6532) -> Tuple[int, int, int, int]:
6533 """
6534 Bounds of the CSS distance d = min(dX, dZ) from the sector bounds x, z = (dmin, dmax, rw_steps), and an upper
6535 bound `dmax` on d supplied by the user (0: none).
6536
6537 Returns:
6538 (dist, dmin, dmax, rw_steps): dist is the smaller sector distance (see _dist_from_bounds(); the larger one if
6539 a sector distance is 0), at most the user's dmax; dmin = min(dmin_X, dmin_Z); dmax is the smallest of the
6540 positive upper bounds (0: none).
6541 """
6542 d_lo = min(x[0], z[0])
6543 uppers = [v for v in (x[1], z[1], dmax) if v > 0]
6544 d_hi = min(uppers) if uppers else 0
6545 if d_hi > 0 and d_lo > d_hi:
6546 d_lo = d_hi
6547 dist_x, dist_z = _dist_from_bounds(x[0], x[1]), _dist_from_bounds(z[0], z[1])
6548 dist = min(dist_x, dist_z) if (dist_x > 0 and dist_z > 0) else max(dist_x, dist_z)
6549 if dmax > 0 and dist > dmax:
6550 dist = dmax
6551 if d_lo > 0 and d_lo == d_hi:
6552 dist = d_lo
6553 return dist, d_lo, d_hi, x[2] + z[2]
6554
6555
6556def _sector_record(dmin: int, dmax: int, rw_steps: int, cws: List[List[int]]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
6557 """A cache record of a classical or quantum code (or of a CSS sector) with the bounds [dmin, dmax]."""
6558 if (dmax > 0 and dmin > dmax) or dmax == 1: # (a codeword of weight 1: d = 1, exact)
6559 dmin = dmax
6560 return {
6561 "dist": _dist_from_bounds(dmin, dmax),
6562 "dmin": dmin,
6563 "dmax": dmax,
6564 "rw_steps": rw_steps,
6565 "d_info": format_bounds_list(dmin, dmax, rw_steps),
6566 "cws": cws,
6567 }
6568
6569
6570def _migrate_css_records(
6571 Hx: Any, Hz: Any, Lx: Optional[Any] = None, Lz: Optional[Any] = None, eff_cache_file: Optional[str] = None
6572) -> bool:
6573 """
6574 Converts the CSS cache records written before version 0.12.0 (key 'css:X=<Hx>:Z=<Hz>[:Lx=<Lx>:Lz=<Lz>]', also
6575 with a ':start=...' suffix) into the records of the two sectors (see _matrix_cache_key()), and removes them.
6576
6577 The lower bounds dmin_X and dmin_Z are kept. An upper bound dmax_X or dmax_Z is kept only if a stored codeword
6578 confirms it, or if it is smaller than the upper bound of the other sector: earlier versions passed an upper bound
6579 dmax given to compute_css_distance() (a bound on min(dX, dZ)) to both sectors, where it was reported back as the
6580 upper bound of the sector, which is not valid for the sector with the larger distance. Otherwise, the weight of
6581 the lightest stored codeword (if any) is used.
6582
6583 Returns:
6584 True if a record was converted (the cache file, if any, is then saved).
6585 """
6586 global _distance_cache
6587 old = f"css:X={get_sparse_array_state(Hx)}:Z={get_sparse_array_state(Hz)}"
6588 if Lx is not None or Lz is not None:
6589 old = f"{old}:Lx={get_sparse_array_state(Lx)}:Lz={get_sparse_array_state(Lz)}"
6590 old_keys = [k for k in list(_distance_cache) if k == old or k.startswith(old + ":start=")]
6591 if not old_keys:
6592 return False
6593 codes = _css_sector_codes(Hx, Hz, Lx, Lz)
6594 base = {s: _matrix_cache_key(*codes[s]) for s in ("X", "Z")}
6595 for key in old_keys:
6596 rec = _distance_cache.pop(key)
6597 if not isinstance(rec, dict):
6598 continue
6599 sfx = key[len(old):]
6600 for s, other in (("X", "Z"), ("Z", "X")):
6601 dmin = int(rec.get(f"dmin_{s}", rec.get("dmin", 0)) or 0)
6602 dmax = int(rec.get(f"dmax_{s}", 0) or 0)
6603 other_dmax = int(rec.get(f"dmax_{other}", 0) or 0)
6604 cws = [list(cw) for cw in (rec.get(f"cws_{s}") or [])]
6605 w_cw = min((len(cw) for cw in cws), default=0)
6606 if dmax > 0 and w_cw != dmax and not (dmax < other_dmax):
6607 dmax = 0 # possibly the upper bound on min(dX, dZ) reported back by the binary
6608 if w_cw > 0:
6609 dmax = min(dmax, w_cw) if dmax > 0 else w_cw
6610 rw = int(rec.get(f"rw_steps_{s}", 0) or 0)
6611 skey = base[s] + sfx
6612 prev = _distance_cache.get(skey)
6613 if prev:
6614 p_dmax = prev.get("dmax", 0) or 0
6615 dmax = min(p_dmax, dmax) if (p_dmax > 0 and dmax > 0) else max(p_dmax, dmax)
6616 dmin = max(prev.get("dmin", 0) or 0, dmin)
6617 rw = max(prev.get("rw_steps", 0) or 0, rw)
6618 cws = _union_cws(prev.get("cws", []), cws)
6619 _distance_cache[skey] = _sector_record(dmin, dmax, rw, cws)
6620 if eff_cache_file:
6621 save_distance_cache(eff_cache_file)
6622 return True
6623
6624
6625def _cached_code_distance(
6626 H: Any,
6627 G: Optional[Any],
6628 L: Optional[Any],
6629 classical: bool,
6630 kind: str,
6631 dist_m4ri: Optional[str],
6632 method: int,
6633 threads: Optional[int],
6634 timeout: float,
6635 num_steps: Optional[int],
6636 d_exp: int,
6637 dmin: int,
6638 dmax: int,
6639 dstop: int,
6640 wmin: int,
6641 wmax: int,
6642 smax: Optional[int],
6643 start_list: Optional[List[int]],
6644 dW: int,
6645 maxC: int,
6646 finC: Optional[str],
6647 outC: Optional[str],
6648 need_cws: bool,
6649 eff_cache_file: Optional[str],
6650 seed: int,
6651 debug: int,
6652 verbose: bool,
6653 nothrottle: bool,
6654 chunk_size: int,
6655 ksub: int,
6656 kwin: int,
6657 win_mode: int,
6658 min_hits: Optional[int],
6659 cov_cws: int,
6660 refresh: Optional[int],
6661 trust_start: bool,
6662 fdem: Optional[Any] = None,
6663 pmin: float = 0.0,
6664 merge: bool = True,
6665 key_fn: Optional[Callable[[], str]] = None,
6666 cws_out_fn: Optional[Callable[[List[List[int]]], List[List[int]]]] = None,
6667 fdrop: Optional[Union[str, Path, List[int]]] = None,
6668 outD: Optional[str] = None,
6669 sort_rows: Optional[bool] = None,
6670 win_hyb: int = 0,
6671 pairs: int = -1,
6672 cc_prune: Optional[int] = None,
6673 ortho: bool = True,
6674 rw_opt: Optional[int] = None,
6675 dem_rounds: int = 0,
6676 json_out: bool = False
6677) -> Dict[str, Any]:
6678 """
6679 Distance of a classical code (H), of a quantum code (H with G or L), or of a DEM (fdem: a stim DEM object or a .dem
6680 file, with the probability cutoff pmin, merge, the detectors to drop fdrop ("auto", "0", a file, or a list), the
6681 file outD for the detectors dropped, and its rounds dem_rounds: see run_dist_m4ri()) with the dist_m4ri binary,
6682 using the distance cache shared by compute_classical_distance(), compute_quantum_distance(), the two sectors of
6683 compute_css_distance(), and compute_dem_distance() (the warnings for the expert options are issued by the callers).
6684 The row order sort_rows and the CC search cc_prune (see run_dist_m4ri()) do not change the result, nor the cache
6685 key; nor do the RW window size win_hyb, the RW pairs (pairs), the RW stages rw_opt, the rounds dem_rounds, and the
6686 expert option ortho (False: the binary does not check H G^T = 0) change the cache key. With json_out (Stage A of
6687 engine='auto', since version 0.17.5), a binary which has the option json= (see _binary_has_json()) writes its JSON
6688 summary (json=1, decoded into _last_run_stats['result_json'] of this run, see _auto_stage_a_witness()).
6689
6690 A cache record (key: key_fn() if given, otherwise see _matrix_cache_key()) answers the request if it holds the
6691 exact distance, or with the stop target dstop > 0 a lower bound dmin >= dstop (and the codewords, if needed).
6692 Otherwise, the binary is run, starting from the cached bounds, and the merged bounds are stored. The returned
6693 codewords (those of the run merged with the cached ones, or the cached ones) are written to outC; with finC
6694 identical to outC, the codewords already in the file are kept. If given, cws_out_fn transforms the codewords
6695 returned and written to outC (e.g., the expansion over equal DEM columns, see _expand_equal_columns()); the cache
6696 keeps the codewords as found.
6697
6698 Returns:
6699 dict with the distance "dist" (see _dist_from_bounds()), the bounds "dmin", "dmax", "rw_steps", "d_info"
6700 (see format_bounds_list()), the codewords "cws" (empty unless need_cws), and "cached" (True if no binary run).
6701 """
6702 global _distance_cache, _last_run_stats
6703 _last_run_stats = {} # the statistics of the binary run (none if the result is cached)
6704 if fdem is None:
6705 _check_has_columns(kind, H, G, L)
6706 same_file = bool(finC and outC) and os.path.abspath(str(finC)) == os.path.abspath(str(outC))
6707 finC = check_finc_outc(finC, outC, verbose=verbose)
6708
6709 def write_out(cws_res: List[List[int]]) -> List[List[int]]:
6710 # the codewords returned (transformed by cws_out_fn) and written to outC; with finC identical to outC, the
6711 # codewords already in the file are kept
6712 if cws_out_fn is not None and cws_res:
6713 cws_res = cws_out_fn(cws_res)
6714 if outC and cws_res:
6715 out = cws_res
6716 if same_file and os.path.isfile(outC):
6717 out = _union_cws(read_sparse_vectors(outC), cws_res)
6718 _write_nzlist_file(outC, out)
6719 return cws_res
6720
6721 code_key = cached_entry = plain_key = plain_entry = None
6722 hit: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None # the result of a cache hit
6723 eff_dmin, eff_dmax = dmin, dmax
6724 if _use_distance_cache:
6725 if eff_cache_file:
6726 load_distance_cache(eff_cache_file)
6727 try:
6728 plain_key = key_fn() if key_fn is not None else _matrix_cache_key(H, G, L, classical)
6729 code_key, cached_entry, plain_entry = _resolve_start_cache(
6730 plain_key, start_list, lambda e: _single_entry_is_exact(e, need_cws, dstop), trust_start,
6731 lambda e: _merge_start_into_plain(plain_key, e, True), eff_cache_file, verbose
6732 )
6733 eff_dmin, eff_dmax = _seed_bounds_from_entry(eff_dmin, eff_dmax, plain_entry)
6734 if cached_entry is not None:
6735 c_dmin, c_dmax = cached_entry.get("dmin", 0) or 0, cached_entry.get("dmax", 0) or 0
6736 if _single_entry_is_exact(cached_entry, need_cws, dstop):
6737 c_rw = cached_entry.get("rw_steps", 0) or 0
6738 d_info = format_bounds_list(c_dmin, c_dmax, c_rw)
6739 found = "exact distance" if (c_dmin > 0 and c_dmin == c_dmax) else f"dmin={c_dmin} >= dstop={dstop}"
6740 if verbose:
6741 print(f"[dist_m4ri] Cache retrieval: SUCCESS (found cached {found} for '{code_key}')")
6742 print(f"[dist_m4ri] Cached result: dist={_dist_from_bounds(c_dmin, c_dmax)}, "
6743 f"bounds={format_bounds_str(d_info)}")
6744 elif debug & PY_DBG_CACHE:
6745 print(f"[dist_m4ri] Cache hit for {kind} distance ({found} known)!")
6746 cws_res = [list(cw) for cw in cached_entry.get("cws", [])] if need_cws else []
6747 hit = {"dist": _dist_from_bounds(c_dmin, c_dmax), "dmin": c_dmin, "dmax": c_dmax,
6748 "rw_steps": c_rw, "d_info": d_info, "cws": cws_res, "cached": True}
6749 else:
6750 if verbose:
6751 print(f"[dist_m4ri] Cache retrieval: PARTIAL (cached bounds: dmin={c_dmin}, dmax={c_dmax}, "
6752 f"rw_steps={cached_entry.get('rw_steps', 0)}; continuing search)")
6753 eff_dmin, eff_dmax = _seed_bounds_from_entry(eff_dmin, eff_dmax, cached_entry)
6754 elif verbose:
6755 print(f"[dist_m4ri] Cache retrieval: MISS (no entry for '{code_key}')")
6756 except Exception:
6757 code_key = cached_entry = plain_key = plain_entry = hit = None
6758 elif verbose:
6759 print("[dist_m4ri] Cache retrieval: DISABLED (cache is turned off)")
6760 if hit is not None:
6761 hit["cws"] = write_out(hit["cws"])
6762 return hit
6763
6764 if wmax > 0 and eff_dmin > max(wmax, dmin): # a cached lower bound beyond wmax (the binary needs dmin <= wmax)
6765 src = cached_entry or plain_entry
6766 if not (method & 1) and src is not None: # CC only: all weights up to wmax have been analyzed already
6767 c_dmin, c_dmax, c_rw = src.get("dmin", 0) or 0, src.get("dmax", 0) or 0, src.get("rw_steps", 0) or 0
6768 if verbose:
6769 print(f"[dist_m4ri] Cached lower bound dmin={c_dmin} > wmax={wmax}: no CC round needed")
6770 cws_res = write_out([list(cw) for cw in src.get("cws", [])] if need_cws else [])
6771 return {"dist": _dist_from_bounds(c_dmin, c_dmax), "dmin": c_dmin, "dmax": c_dmax, "rw_steps": c_rw,
6772 "d_info": format_bounds_list(c_dmin, c_dmax, c_rw), "cws": cws_res, "cached": True}
6773 eff_dmin = max(wmax, dmin)
6774
6775 temp_files: List[str] = []
6776 try:
6777 def input_file(M: Any, ext: str) -> Optional[str]:
6778 if M is None:
6779 return None
6780 if isinstance(M, (str, Path)) and os.path.exists(str(M)):
6781 return str(M)
6782 path = _matrix_to_file(M, extension=ext)
6783 temp_files.append(path)
6784 return path
6785
6786 file_dem = None
6787 if fdem is not None: # a DEM: the file, or the object written to a temporary file
6788 if isinstance(fdem, (str, Path)) and os.path.exists(str(fdem)):
6789 file_dem = str(fdem)
6790 else:
6791 file_dem = create_unique_file(extension=".dem")
6792 temp_files.append(file_dem)
6793 _write_dem_file(fdem, file_dem)
6794 file_H, file_G, file_L = input_file(H, "_H.mtx"), input_file(G, "_G.mtx"), input_file(L, "_L.mtx")
6795 file_drop = None
6796 if fdem is not None and fdrop is not None: # the detectors to drop: the file, or the list written to a file
6797 if isinstance(fdrop, (str, Path)):
6798 file_drop = str(fdrop)
6799 elif len(fdrop) > 0:
6800 file_drop = create_unique_file(extension="_drop.txt")
6801 temp_files.append(file_drop)
6802 with open(file_drop, "w") as f:
6803 f.write(" ".join(str(r) for r in fdrop) + "\n")
6804 outC_file = None
6805 if need_cws:
6806 outC_file = create_unique_file(extension="_cws.nz")
6807 temp_files.append(outC_file)
6808
6809 dmin_res, dmax_res, rw_steps = run_dist_m4ri(
6810 dist_m4ri_path=dist_m4ri,
6811 method=method,
6812 finH=file_H,
6813 finG=file_G,
6814 finL=file_L,
6815 fdem=file_dem,
6816 finC=finC,
6817 classical=-1 if fdem is not None else (1 if classical else 0),
6818 dmin=eff_dmin,
6819 dmax=eff_dmax,
6820 dstop=dstop,
6821 wmin=wmin,
6822 wmax=wmax,
6823 smax=smax,
6824 start=start_list,
6825 start_scan=bool(getattr(start_list, "scan", False)),
6826 warn_start=False,
6827 warn_ksub=False,
6828 ortho=ortho,
6829 warn_ortho=False,
6830 dexp=d_exp,
6831 steps=num_steps,
6832 threads=threads,
6833 timeout=timeout,
6834 pmin=pmin,
6835 merge=merge,
6836 drop=file_drop,
6837 outD=outD if fdem is not None else None,
6838 sort_rows=sort_rows,
6839 cc_prune=cc_prune,
6840 dW=dW,
6841 maxC=maxC,
6842 outC=outC_file,
6843 seed=seed,
6844 debug=debug,
6845 nothrottle=nothrottle,
6846 chunk_size=chunk_size,
6847 ksub=ksub,
6848 kwin=kwin,
6849 win_mode=win_mode,
6850 win_hyb=win_hyb,
6851 pairs=pairs,
6852 min_hits=min_hits,
6853 cov_cws=cov_cws,
6854 refresh=refresh,
6855 verbose=verbose,
6856 rw_opt=rw_opt,
6857 dem_rounds=dem_rounds if fdem is not None else 0,
6858 json_out=True if (json_out and _binary_has_json(dist_m4ri)) else None
6859 )
6860
6861 if _last_run_stats.get("k0"): # (no logical codeword: [0, 0, 0], not cached, see _k0_result())
6862 return _k0_result((code_key, plain_key), eff_cache_file)
6863
6864 cws: List[List[int]] = []
6865 if need_cws and outC_file and os.path.exists(outC_file):
6866 cws = read_sparse_vectors(outC_file)
6867 cws.sort(key=len)
6868
6869 if _use_distance_cache and code_key is not None:
6870 prev = cached_entry or {}
6871 p_dmax = prev.get("dmax", 0) or 0
6872 best_dmax = min(p_dmax, dmax_res) if (p_dmax > 0 and dmax_res > 0) else max(p_dmax, dmax_res)
6873 best_dmin = max(prev.get("dmin", 0) or 0, dmin_res)
6874 total_rw = (prev.get("rw_steps", 0) or 0) + rw_steps
6875 record = _sector_record(best_dmin, best_dmax, total_rw, _union_cws(prev.get("cws", []), cws))
6876 if "dmin_model" in prev: # (a bound from the code-sized model, see compute_model_lower_bound())
6877 record["dmin_model"] = prev["dmin_model"]
6878 _distance_cache[code_key] = record
6879 if plain_key is not None and code_key != plain_key:
6880 # start-list run: merge the valid part (or all, with trust_start) into the main record
6881 _merge_start_into_plain(plain_key, record, trust_start, {"": rw_steps})
6882 if eff_cache_file:
6883 save_distance_cache(eff_cache_file)
6884 res = {"dist": record["dist"], "dmin": record["dmin"], "dmax": record["dmax"], "rw_steps": total_rw,
6885 "d_info": record["d_info"], "cws": record["cws"] if need_cws else [], "cached": False}
6886 else:
6887 res = {"dist": _dist_from_bounds(dmin_res, dmax_res), "dmin": dmin_res, "dmax": dmax_res,
6888 "rw_steps": rw_steps, "d_info": format_bounds_list(dmin_res, dmax_res, rw_steps), "cws": cws,
6889 "cached": False}
6890 res["cws"] = write_out(res["cws"])
6891 return res
6892 finally:
6893 _remove_temp_files(temp_files, debug)
6894
6895
6896def compute_classical_distance(
6897 H: Any,
6898 dist_m4ri: Optional[str] = None,
6899 method: int = 3,
6900 threads: Optional[int] = None,
6901 timeout: float = 60.0,
6902 num_steps: Optional[int] = None,
6903 d_exp: int = 0,
6904 d_min: int = 0,
6905 d_max: int = 0,
6906 dmin: int = 0,
6907 dmax: int = 0,
6908 dstop: int = 0,
6909 wmin: int = 1,
6910 wmax: int = 0,
6911 smax: Optional[int] = None,
6912 start: Optional[Union[int, str, Sequence[int]]] = None,
6913 cbeg: Optional[int] = None,
6914 cend: Optional[int] = None,
6915 noscan: int = 0,
6916 dW: int = -1,
6917 maxC: int = 0,
6918 finC: Optional[str] = None,
6919 outC: Optional[str] = None,
6920 do_cws: bool = False,
6921 return_info: bool = False,
6922 cache_file: Optional[Union[str, Path]] = None,
6923 solver: str = "dist_m4ri",
6924 codedistance_method: str = "QDistEvol",
6925 codedistance_params: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
6926 seed: int = 0,
6927 debug: int = 0,
6928 verbose: bool = False,
6929 nothrottle: bool = False,
6930 chunk_size: int = 0,
6931 ksub: int = 0,
6932 kwin: int = 0,
6933 win_mode: int = 0,
6934 win_hyb: int = 0,
6935 pairs: int = -1,
6936 min_hits: Optional[int] = None,
6937 cov_cws: int = 100,
6938 refresh: Optional[int] = None,
6939 trust_start: bool = False,
6940 start_scan: bool = False,
6941 sort_rows: Optional[bool] = None,
6942 cc_prune: Optional[int] = None,
6943 engine: Optional[str] = None,
6944 rw_opt: Optional[int] = None,
6945 table_gb: Optional[int] = None,
6946 **kwargs
6947) -> Any:
6948 """
6949 Computes the minimum distance of a classical linear code given parity check matrix H.
6950
6951 Args:
6952 H: Parity check matrix (numpy array, scipy sparse matrix, or file path).
6953 dist_m4ri: Path to dist_m4ri executable (optional).
6954 method: Solver method (1=RW, 2=CC, 3=Bracketing default).
6955 threads: Maximum number of worker threads (default: all logical CPUs available; subject to throttling).
6956 timeout: Execution timeout in seconds (default: 60.0; 0 or inf: no limit).
6957 nothrottle: If True, the automatic thread throttling of the binary is disabled (default: False).
6958 chunk_size: Maximum RW batch claimed at once by a thread (default: 0: adaptive, 25-500 steps; in method=3,
6959 at most about 0.5 s of RW steps, and an RW thread leaves its batch between two steps for a CC round).
6960 num_steps: Maximum RW steps.
6961 min_hits: RW stops once the average number of hits per codeword reaches min_hits (with a nonzero resolved
6962 rw_opt, not counting the hits of the row slabs and of the hybrid index windows), both for the codewords of
6963 the minimum weight found and for a representative set of cov_cws lowest-weight codewords; with the
6964 canonical classes of rw_opt 16 (automatic for quantum codes and DEMs with kwin <= 0), once the classes of
6965 the minimum weight found by the uniform RW steps pass the Good-Turing and Chao2 tests instead (none found
6966 by them, e.g., on deep circuit DEMs: RW runs to num_steps or the timeout); see run_dist_m4ri(). Passed if
6967 not None and >= 0 (None, the default: the binary's 5; 0: off, and then the repeated hits are not counted,
6968 unless codewords are collected with do_cws, outC, or maxC).
6969 cov_cws: Size of the representative set of lowest-weight codewords for min_hits (default: 100; 0: only the
6970 minimum weight).
6971 kwin / win_mode: A window of kwin columns in every RW step (alias: win; win_mode=0, the default: a Tanner
6972 graph ball, 1: an index window); kwin=0 (default): the automatic hybrid windows for n >= 500 (with a
6973 nonzero resolved rw_opt, only for a DEM or with win_hyb > 0: matrices then use uniform random permutations;
6974 an automatic rw_opt which resolves to 0, e.g., on classical codes, keeps the hybrid windows), see win_hyb
6975 and run_dist_m4ri(); kwin=-1: no windows (uniform random permutations in every step).
6976 refresh: RW steps between the basis refreshes of the experimental ksub RW (passed if not None; None,
6977 the default: the binary's 5000 with ksub > 0; 0: no refresh).
6978 d_exp: Expected distance estimate.
6979 d_min / dmin: Known lower bound on distance.
6980 d_max / dmax: Known upper bound on distance.
6981 dstop: Stop target for the lower bound (default: 0 = off): the search ends once CC has certified
6982 dmin >= dstop (method=2 or 3), unless a lighter codeword is found. Unlike dmax, dstop is not an upper
6983 bound, and it is not reported as dmax: d_info = [dmin, w, rw_steps] with dmin >= dstop and the weight w
6984 of the lightest codeword found (0: none). A cached lower bound dmin >= dstop answers the request without
6985 a calculation.
6986 wmin: Minimum distance of interest (terminate early if cw of weight <= wmin is found in RW or CC, default: 1).
6987 wmax: Maximum weight to search in CC.
6988 smax: Maximum syndrome weight for CC confinement profile.
6989 start: Expert option: list of CC start columns (int, comma-separated string "a,b,c", or
6990 sequence of ints; None or -1: all columns). CC clusters are grown only from the listed
6991 columns, and they are not limited to larger column indices. WARNING: the lower bound
6992 (and an exact result) is valid only if a code symmetry maps every minimum-weight codeword
6993 to one containing a listed column (e.g., one column per block of a quasi-cyclic code);
6994 the upper bound is always valid. Results are cached under the separate key
6995 '<key>:start=a,b,c'; only dmax and codewords update the main cache record.
6996 trust_start: Expert option: accept the start-list results as valid, i.e., also merge dmin and
6997 rw_steps into the main cache record, and copy an existing exact start-list record to the
6998 main record even if no calculation is needed (default: False).
6999 start_scan: Expert option, with start (default: False): a cluster grown from a listed column c only
7000 uses the columns > c (see run_dist_m4ri()), e.g., start=[0, l] for the two blocks of a two-block
7001 group-algebra code over an abelian group; cached under the key suffix ':start=a,b,c:scan' (not for a
7002 DEM: ignored with a warning).
7003 cbeg / cend / noscan: Disabled in the Python interface: accepted for backward compatibility,
7004 but ignored with a warning to stderr (use the dist_m4ri binary directly).
7005 sort_rows: Row order of H in the binary (see run_dist_m4ri()): True sorts the rows by increasing weight
7006 (faster CC for very different row weights with cc_prune=0), False keeps their order, and None (default)
7007 leaves the binary's default (sorted for matrices; the detectors of a DEM are kept in time order). The
7008 result and the cache key do not depend on it.
7009 cc_prune: The CC search of the binary (see run_dist_m4ri()): 0, the walk of the versions before 0.15.0; 1,
7010 the branch and bound (each codeword found once); 2, also the coverage and fractional cover bounds; None
7011 (default): the binary's default 1. The result and the cache key do not depend on it.
7012 win_hyb: Window size of the automatic hybrid RW steps (kwin=0, n >= 500: a window on every other step, for
7013 matrices only when the resolved rw_opt is 0 or win_hyb > 0; see run_dist_m4ri()); 0 (default): 256 columns
7014 for a DEM, 512 for matrices. The cache key does not depend on it.
7015 pairs: The RW pairs of non-pivot columns (p=2, see run_dist_m4ri()): the number of random pivot rows of
7016 their buckets (0: off; -1, the default: auto). The cache key does not depend on it.
7017 ksub: Experimental, should not be used (a warning is printed to stderr for ksub > 0 with method=1 or 3):
7018 subspace dimension sampled from ker(H) in RW (default: 0, full-matrix RW).
7019 dW: Extra weight window above dmin to collect codewords (only irreducible ones: not the union of a
7020 codeword and a disjoint nonzero vector with zero syndrome; the binary's default irred=1).
7021 maxC: Maximum number of codewords to collect.
7022 finC: Input file with initial codewords.
7023 outC: Output file to save codewords (NZLIST format).
7024 do_cws: Whether to return extracted codewords.
7025 return_info: If True, return (dist, d_info) or (dist, d_info, cws) where d_info is [dmin, dmax, num_rw].
7026 cache_file: Optional JSON file path for persistent distance caching.
7027 solver: "dist_m4ri", "cert", "tropidist", "auto", or "codedistance".
7028 codedistance_method: Method if using codedistance library.
7029 codedistance_params: Extra parameters for codedistance library.
7030 seed: Random seed.
7031 debug: Debug bitmap: the bits in BIN_DBG_MASK for the dist_m4ri binary, and the PY_DBG_* bits.
7032 verbose: Verbose reporting flag.
7033 engine: None or "dist_m4ri" (default): the dist_m4ri binary; "cert": qec_cert (distance only, see
7034 compute_quantum_distance()); "tropidist": external `tropidist` subprocess (`python -m cdist`, located via
7035 `TROPIDIST_ROOT` or `cdist` on `sys.path`; distance only, independently verifies every returned witness);
7036 "auto": the dist_m4ri binary (since version 0.17.0, a classical code is never delegated to qec_cert or
7037 tropidist, whose startup takes longer than most runs of the binary).
7038 rw_opt: Expert option (since version 0.17.0): the stages of the RW search of the binary (None, the default:
7039 the binary's -1, automatic; 0: all off, the RW of version 0.16.1; a bitmask 1..63: only the stages listed,
7040 see run_dist_m4ri()). The distance and the cache key do not depend on it.
7041 table_gb: Optional lookup-table memory budget in GiB for `engine="tropidist"` (0: tropidist default; ignored
7042 with a warning for other engines).
7043
7044 Returns:
7045 dist or (dist, cws) if do_cws is True (or (dist, d_info) / (dist, d_info, cws) if return_info=True). A code
7046 without nonzero codewords (k = 0, e.g., a full-rank H) gives dist 0 and d_info [0, 0, 0] (since version 0.17.2,
7047 with every engine and solver, and one note on stderr unless silent; not cached).
7048
7049 Raises:
7050 TypeError: for an unknown keyword argument (e.g., a misspelled option).
7051 ValueError: for an invalid option value (e.g., start, cc_prune other than 0, 1, or 2, rw_opt outside -1..63,
7052 or negative table_gb), for H without columns (n = 0, since version 0.17.2), for method=2 with timeout <= 0
7053 but without wmax, dmax, or dstop, or for do_cws / outC with solver="codedistance", engine="cert", or
7054 engine="tropidist".
7055 FileNotFoundError: if the dist_m4ri binary is not found (see find_dist_m4ri_binary()).
7056 RuntimeError: if the binary (or tropidist) exits with an error (e.g., for a missing input file).
7057 ImportError: if solver="codedistance", engine="cert", or engine="tropidist" is requested but unavailable.
7058 """
7059 eff_dmin = dmin if dmin > 0 else d_min
7060 eff_dmax = dmax if dmax > 0 else d_max
7061 _check_kwargs(compute_classical_distance, kwargs)
7062 _check_has_columns("classical", H)
7063 _check_rw_opt(rw_opt)

7067 start_list = _prepare_start_option(start, trust_start, noscan, cbeg, cend, solver, start_scan=start_scan,
7068 engine_cert=cert_mode if cert_mode in ("cert", "tropidist") else False)

7070 _warn_table_gb_unused(eff_table_gb, cert_mode, is_codedist=is_codedist)
7071 _warn_experimental_ksub(ksub, method, solver)
7072
7073 if is_codedist:

7075 raise ValueError("Codeword extraction is not supported with codedistance solver; use solver='dist_m4ri'.")
7076 _warn_codedistance_ignored(locals())
7077 codedistance = _get_codedistance()
7078 import numpy as np
7079 params = dict(codedistance_params or {})
7080 if num_steps is not None and "iterCount" not in params:
7081 params["iterCount"] = num_steps
7082
7083 if _k0_of_matrices(H, classical=True): # (since version 0.17.2)
7084 _k0_found("rank H = n")

7087 np.asarray(H, dtype=np.int8) if isinstance(H, (np.ndarray, list)) else None
7088 )

7090 H_mat, None, tB=1, method=codedistance_method, params=params,
7091 seed=seed if seed != 0 else None
7092 )
7093 d = res.get("d", -1)
7094 if return_info:
7095 d_info = format_bounds_list(d, d, 0) if d > 0 else [0, 0, 0]
7096 return d, d_info
7097 return d
7098
7099 eff_cache_file = str(Path(cache_file).resolve()) if cache_file is not None else _distance_cache_file
7100 if _can_delegate_to_tropidist(cert_mode, do_cws=do_cws, outC=outC):
7101 def run_trop_classical(w_lo: int, w_hi: int) -> Tuple[Dict[str, Any], Any, Any]:
7102 import numpy as np
7103 import scipy.sparse as sp
7104 H_csr = _to_binary_csr(H)
7105 if _k0_of_matrices(H_csr, classical=True):
7106 return {"k0": "rank H = n"}, None, None
7107 L_csr = sp.eye(int(H_csr.shape[1]), dtype=np.uint8, format="csr")
7108 rec = _run_tropidist(
7109 H_csr=H_csr, L_csr=L_csr, w_lo=w_lo, w_hi=w_hi, threads=threads, timeout=timeout,
7110 table_gb=eff_table_gb, debug=debug, verbose=verbose,
7111 )
7112 return rec, H_csr, L_csr
7113 res = _tropidist_code_distance(
7114 lambda: _matrix_cache_key(H, None, None, True), run_trop_classical,
7115 label="classical", classical=True, dmin=eff_dmin, dmax=eff_dmax, dstop=dstop, wmax=wmax,
7116 eff_cache_file=eff_cache_file, debug=debug, verbose=verbose,
7117 )
7118 dist, d_info = res["dist"], res["d_info"]
7119 return (dist, d_info) if return_info else dist
7120
7121 if _can_delegate_to_cert(
7122 cert_mode, method=method, do_cws=do_cws, outC=outC, finC=finC, smax=smax, dW=dW, maxC=maxC,
7123 start_list=start_list, classical=True, # (engine='auto': never for a classical code)
7124 ):
7125 _, qec_io, qec_pipeline = _get_qec_cert()
7126 mode_arg = "ub" if method == 1 else "auto"

7128 lambda: _matrix_cache_key(H, None, None, True),
7129 lambda w_lo, w_hi, dmax_c: qec_pipeline.certify( # (no stabilizer dominance: search=False)
7130 qec_io.DistanceProblem(_cert_to_csr(H, qec_io), None, None),
7131 wmax=w_hi, threads=threads or (os.cpu_count() or 8),
7132 seed=seed if seed != 0 else 1,
7133 time_limit=_auto_timeout(timeout),
7134 mode=mode_arg,
7135 **_cert_handoff_kw(qec_pipeline, w_lo, search=False, dmax=dmax_c, debug=debug, verbose=verbose),
7136 ),
7137 label="classical", dmin=eff_dmin, dmax=eff_dmax, dstop=dstop, wmax=wmax,
7138 eff_cache_file=eff_cache_file, debug=debug, verbose=verbose,
7139 )
7140 dist, d_info = res["dist"], res["d_info"]
7141 return (dist, d_info) if return_info else dist
7142
7143 # Solver is native multithreaded dist_m4ri (supports bounds caching and cumulative RW steps)
7144 res = _cached_code_distance(
7145 H, None, None, True, "classical", dist_m4ri=dist_m4ri, method=method, threads=threads, timeout=timeout,
7146 num_steps=num_steps, d_exp=d_exp, dmin=eff_dmin, dmax=eff_dmax, dstop=dstop, wmin=wmin, wmax=wmax,
7147 smax=smax, start_list=start_list, dW=dW, maxC=maxC, finC=finC, outC=outC, need_cws=bool(do_cws or outC),
7148 eff_cache_file=eff_cache_file, seed=seed, debug=debug, verbose=verbose, nothrottle=nothrottle,
7149 chunk_size=chunk_size, ksub=ksub, kwin=kwin if kwin != 0 else int(kwargs.get("win", 0) or 0),
7150 win_mode=win_mode, min_hits=min_hits, cov_cws=cov_cws, refresh=refresh, trust_start=trust_start,
7151 sort_rows=sort_rows, win_hyb=win_hyb, pairs=pairs, cc_prune=cc_prune, rw_opt=rw_opt
7152 )
7153 dist, d_info, cws = res["dist"], res["d_info"], res["cws"]
7154 if return_info:
7155 return (dist, d_info, cws) if do_cws else (dist, d_info)
7156 return (dist, cws) if do_cws else dist

7159def compute_quantum_distance(
7160 H: Any,
7161 G: Optional[Any] = None,
7162 L: Optional[Any] = None,
7163 dist_m4ri: Optional[str] = None,
7164 method: int = 3,
7165 threads: Optional[int] = None,
7166 timeout: float = 60.0,
7167 num_steps: Optional[int] = None,
7168 d_exp: int = 0,
7169 d_min: int = 0,
7170 d_max: int = 0,
7171 dmin: int = 0,
7172 dmax: int = 0,
7173 dstop: int = 0,
7174 wmin: int = 1,
7175 wmax: int = 0,
7176 smax: Optional[int] = None,
7177 start: Optional[Union[int, str, Sequence[int]]] = None,
7178 cbeg: Optional[int] = None,
7179 cend: Optional[int] = None,
7180 noscan: int = 0,
7181 dW: int = -1,
7182 maxC: int = 0,
7183 finC: Optional[str] = None,
7184 outC: Optional[str] = None,
7185 do_cws: bool = False,
7186 return_info: bool = False,
7187 cache_file: Optional[Union[str, Path]] = None,
7188 solver: str = "dist_m4ri",
7189 codedistance_method: str = "QDistEvol",
7190 codedistance_params: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
7191 seed: int = 0,
7192 debug: int = 0,
7193 verbose: bool = False,
7194 nothrottle: bool = False,
7195 chunk_size: int = 0,
7196 ksub: int = 0,
7197 kwin: int = 0,
7198 win_mode: int = 0,
7199 win_hyb: int = 0,
7200 pairs: int = -1,
7201 min_hits: Optional[int] = None,
7202 cov_cws: int = 100,
7203 refresh: Optional[int] = None,
7204 trust_start: bool = False,
7205 start_scan: bool = False,
7206 sort_rows: Optional[bool] = None,
7207 cc_prune: Optional[int] = None,
7208 ortho: bool = True,
7209 engine: Optional[str] = None,
7210 rw_opt: Optional[int] = None,
7211 table_gb: Optional[int] = None,
7212 **kwargs
7213) -> Any:
7214 """
7215 Computes the minimum distance of a single-sided quantum code given parity check matrix H
7216 and degeneracy generator G (or logical operator matrix L).
7217
7218 Args:
7219 H: Parity check matrix (numpy array, scipy sparse matrix, or file path).
7220 G: Degeneracy generator matrix (numpy array, scipy sparse matrix, or file path); the binary constructs the
7221 logical operators from H and G. Either G or L is required, not both (ValueError).
7222 L: Logical operator matrix (numpy array, scipy sparse matrix, or file path), instead of G.
7223 ortho: Expert option (default: True; since version 0.15.2): False skips the check of the binary that the rows
7224 of H and G are orthogonal (H G^T = 0; True: an error otherwise), e.g., to screen many codes which are
7225 orthogonal by construction; a warning is printed to stderr, and the result is valid only if H G^T = 0. No
7226 effect without G. The cache key does not depend on it.
7227 dist_m4ri: Path to dist_m4ri executable (optional).
7228 method: Solver method (1=RW, 2=CC, 3=Bracketing default).
7229 threads: Maximum number of worker threads (default: all logical CPUs available; subject to throttling).
7230 timeout: Execution timeout in seconds (default: 60.0; 0 or inf: no limit).
7231 nothrottle: If True, the automatic thread throttling of the binary is disabled (default: False).
7232 chunk_size: Maximum RW batch claimed at once by a thread (default: 0: adaptive, 25-500 steps; in method=3,
7233 at most about 0.5 s of RW steps, and an RW thread leaves its batch between two steps for a CC round).
7234 num_steps: Maximum RW steps.
7235 min_hits: RW stops once the average number of hits per codeword reaches min_hits (with a nonzero resolved
7236 rw_opt, not counting the hits of the row slabs and of the hybrid index windows), both for the codewords of
7237 the minimum weight found and for a representative set of cov_cws lowest-weight codewords; with the
7238 canonical classes of rw_opt 16 (automatic for quantum codes and DEMs with kwin <= 0), once the classes of
7239 the minimum weight found by the uniform RW steps pass the Good-Turing and Chao2 tests instead (none found
7240 by them, e.g., on deep circuit DEMs: RW runs to num_steps or the timeout); see run_dist_m4ri(). Passed if
7241 not None and >= 0 (None, the default: the binary's 5; 0: off, and then the repeated hits are not counted,
7242 unless codewords are collected with do_cws, outC, or maxC).
7243 cov_cws: Size of the representative set of lowest-weight codewords for min_hits (default: 100; 0: only the
7244 minimum weight).
7245 kwin / win_mode: A window of kwin columns in every RW step (alias: win; win_mode=0, the default: a Tanner
7246 graph ball, 1: an index window); kwin=0 (default): the automatic hybrid windows for n >= 500 (with a
7247 nonzero resolved rw_opt, only for a DEM or with win_hyb > 0: matrices then use uniform random permutations;
7248 an automatic rw_opt which resolves to 0, e.g., on classical codes, keeps the hybrid windows), see win_hyb
7249 and run_dist_m4ri(); kwin=-1: no windows (uniform random permutations in every step).
7250 refresh: RW steps between the basis refreshes of the experimental ksub RW (passed if not None; None,
7251 the default: the binary's 5000 with ksub > 0; 0: no refresh).
7252 d_exp: Expected distance estimate.
7253 d_min / dmin: Known lower bound on distance.
7254 d_max / dmax: Known upper bound on distance.
7255 dstop: Stop target for the lower bound (default: 0 = off): the search ends once CC has certified
7256 dmin >= dstop (method=2 or 3), unless a lighter codeword is found. Unlike dmax, dstop is not an upper
7257 bound, and it is not reported as dmax: d_info = [dmin, w, rw_steps] with dmin >= dstop and the weight w
7258 of the lightest codeword found (0: none). A cached lower bound dmin >= dstop answers the request without
7259 a calculation.
7260 wmin: Minimum distance of interest (terminate early if cw of weight <= wmin is found in RW or CC, default: 1).
7261 wmax: Maximum weight to search in CC.
7262 smax: Maximum syndrome weight for CC confinement profile.
7263 start: Expert option: list of CC start columns (int, comma-separated string "a,b,c", or
7264 sequence of ints; None or -1: all columns). CC clusters are grown only from the listed
7265 columns, and they are not limited to larger column indices. WARNING: the lower bound
7266 (and an exact result) is valid only if a code symmetry maps every minimum-weight codeword
7267 to one containing a listed column (e.g., one column per block of a quasi-cyclic code);
7268 the upper bound is always valid. Results are cached under the separate key
7269 '<key>:start=a,b,c'; only dmax and codewords update the main cache record.
7270 trust_start: Expert option: accept the start-list results as valid, i.e., also merge dmin and
7271 rw_steps into the main cache record, and copy an existing exact start-list record to the
7272 main record even if no calculation is needed (default: False).
7273 start_scan: Expert option, with start (default: False): a cluster grown from a listed column c only
7274 uses the columns > c (see run_dist_m4ri()), e.g., start=[0, l] for the two blocks of a two-block
7275 group-algebra code over an abelian group; cached under the key suffix ':start=a,b,c:scan' (not for a
7276 DEM: ignored with a warning).
7277 cbeg / cend / noscan: Disabled in the Python interface: accepted for backward compatibility,
7278 but ignored with a warning to stderr (use the dist_m4ri binary directly).
7279 sort_rows: Row order of H in the binary (see run_dist_m4ri()): True sorts the rows by increasing weight
7280 (faster CC for very different row weights with cc_prune=0), False keeps their order, and None (default)
7281 leaves the binary's default (sorted for matrices; the detectors of a DEM are kept in time order). The
7282 result and the cache key do not depend on it.
7283 cc_prune: The CC search of the binary (see run_dist_m4ri()): 0, the walk of the versions before 0.15.0; 1,
7284 the branch and bound (each codeword found once); 2, also the coverage and fractional cover bounds; None
7285 (default): the binary's default 1. The result and the cache key do not depend on it.
7286 win_hyb: Window size of the automatic hybrid RW steps (kwin=0, n >= 500: a window on every other step, for
7287 matrices only when the resolved rw_opt is 0 or win_hyb > 0; see run_dist_m4ri()); 0 (default): 256 columns
7288 for a DEM, 512 for matrices. The cache key does not depend on it.
7289 pairs: The RW pairs of non-pivot columns (p=2, see run_dist_m4ri()): the number of random pivot rows of
7290 their buckets (0: off; -1, the default: auto). The cache key does not depend on it.
7291 ksub: Experimental, should not be used (a warning is printed to stderr for ksub > 0 with method=1 or 3):
7292 subspace dimension sampled from ker(H) in RW (default: 0, full-matrix RW).
7293 dW: Extra weight window above dmin to collect codewords (only irreducible ones: not the union of a
7294 codeword and a disjoint nonzero vector with zero syndrome; the binary's default irred=1).
7295 maxC: Maximum number of codewords to collect.
7296 finC: Input file with initial codewords.
7297 outC: Output file to save codewords (NZLIST format).
7298 do_cws: Whether to return extracted codewords.
7299 return_info: If True, return (dist, d_info) or (dist, d_info, cws) where d_info is [dmin, dmax, num_rw].
7300 cache_file: Optional JSON file path for persistent distance caching.
7301 solver: "dist_m4ri", "cert", "tropidist", "auto", or "codedistance".
7302 codedistance_method: Method if using codedistance library.
7303 codedistance_params: Extra parameters for codedistance library.
7304 seed: Random seed.
7305 debug: Debug bitmap: the bits in BIN_DBG_MASK for the dist_m4ri binary, and the PY_DBG_* bits.
7306 verbose: Verbose reporting flag.
7307 engine: None or "dist_m4ri" (default): the dist_m4ri binary. "cert": qec_cert (an error for codeword
7308 extraction; finC, smax, dW, maxC, and start are ignored with a warning, since version 0.17.2; a lower bound
7309 of qec_cert is cached only if it is unconditional, and an upper bound only with a verified witness;
7310 ImportError if qec_cert is not usable; a code without logical operators, which qec_cert certifies with the
7311 status 'infeasible', gives [0, 0, 0], as with every engine). It searches the weights from the certified
7312 lower bound of the cache record (not from the caller's dmin, since version 0.17.2: its lower bound would be
7313 conditional on it and
7314 could not be cached; dmin only tightens the returned bounds) up to dmax - 1 (or wmax, or dstop - 1; 40
7315 without any of them, where its stages which do not depend on the weight, e.g., the graphlike or rank-DP
7316 bounds, may still certify a larger distance), see _cert_code_distance(). "tropidist": external `tropidist`
7317 subprocess (`python -m cdist`, located via `TROPIDIST_ROOT` or `cdist` on `sys.path`; constructs `L` from
7318 `(H, G)` over GF(2) when `G` is given, independently verifies every returned witness `H x = 0, L x != 0`,
7319 and uses the same verified-only cache rules; `table_gb` controls its lookup-table memory budget). "auto"
7320 (since version 0.17.0, a two-stage portfolio for a distance-only method=3 call; otherwise the binary, see
7321 _auto_two_stage()): Stage A, the binary for tau_1 = timeout if timeout <= 2 s, else min(max(2, timeout /
7322 10), 10) s; if its bracket is still open and more than 1 s is left, Stage B, qec_cert (or tropidist when
7323 qec_cert is unavailable and tropidist is configured) with the remaining time, from the bounds of Stage A
7324 (wmin = max(1, dmin_A), wmax = dmax_A - 1; qec_cert's randomized upper-bound stage only if dmax_A - max(1,
7325 dmin_A) >= 3 or no codeword is known, since version 0.17.1); if Stage B ends early with an open bracket,
7326 the binary with the time left; the binary only, with the whole timeout, if neither qec_cert nor tropidist
7327 is usable (with a warning once per process if qec_cert is installed without libqeccert.so). A cached exact
7328 result is used without a run (and without importing qec_cert or spawning tropidist). The details are in
7329 _last_run_stats["engine_auto"]. With "cert" and "auto", a floor wmin > 1 (a certified lower bound) is
7330 passed to qec_cert with search_opts={"force_dom": 1}, so that qec_cert keeps the stabilizer dominance of
7331 its search on (since version 0.17.4; also for a DEM; not for a classical code, which has no such dominance,
7332 nor with method=1, whose mode 'ub' runs no search; an older qec_cert without this option is called as
7333 before), see _cert_search_kw(). Since version 0.17.5, a qec_cert with the handoff parameters also gets the
7334 upper bound dmax (of the caller or of the cache record, if above wmin) as dmax_init, and with "auto" the
7335 codeword of weight dmax_A found by the binary in Stage A (which then runs with json=1), as its JSON summary
7336 from_dm4ri (or as ub_witness), which qec_cert verifies; the floor stays wmin (see _cert_handoff_kw()).
7337 rw_opt: Expert option (since version 0.17.0): the stages of the RW search of the binary (None, the default:
7338 the binary's -1, automatic; 0: all off, the RW of version 0.16.1; a bitmask 1..63: only the stages listed,
7339 see run_dist_m4ri()). The distance and the cache key do not depend on it (for codeword collection, see
7340 run_dist_m4ri()).
7341 table_gb: Optional lookup-table memory budget in GiB for `engine="tropidist"` (or `engine="auto"` when
7342 falling back to `tropidist`; 0: tropidist default; ignored with a warning for other engines).
7343
7344 Returns:
7345 dist or (dist, cws) if do_cws is True (or (dist, d_info) / (dist, d_info, cws) if return_info=True). A code
7346 without logical operators (k = 0) gives dist 0 and d_info [0, 0, 0] (since version 0.17.2, with every engine and
7347 solver, and one note on stderr unless silent; not cached).
7348
7349 Raises:
7350 TypeError: for an unknown keyword argument (e.g., a misspelled option).
7351 ValueError: if neither or both of G and L are given (or G is not given, with solver="codedistance"), for a
7352 matrix without columns (n = 0, since version 0.17.2), for an invalid option value (e.g., start, cc_prune
7353 other than 0, 1, or 2, rw_opt outside -1..63, or negative table_gb), for method=2 with timeout <= 0 but
7354 without wmax, dmax, or dstop, or for do_cws / outC with solver="codedistance", engine="cert", or
7355 engine="tropidist".
7356 FileNotFoundError: if the dist_m4ri binary is not found (see find_dist_m4ri_binary()).
7357 RuntimeError: if the binary (or tropidist) exits with an error (e.g., for a missing input file, or with
7358 ortho=True for rows of H and G which are not orthogonal).
7359 ImportError: if solver="codedistance", engine="cert", or engine="tropidist" is requested but unavailable.
7360 """
7361 eff_dmin = dmin if dmin > 0 else d_min
7362 eff_dmax = dmax if dmax > 0 else d_max
7363 _check_kwargs(compute_quantum_distance, kwargs)
7364 _check_has_columns("quantum", H, G, L)
7365 _check_rw_opt(rw_opt)
7366 eff_table_gb = _check_table_gb(table_gb)
7367 cert_mode = _resolve_cert_engine(solver, engine)
7368 is_codedist = solver == "codedistance" or str(engine or "").strip().lower() == "codedistance"
7369 start_list = _prepare_start_option(start, trust_start, noscan, cbeg, cend, solver, start_scan=start_scan,
7370 engine_cert=cert_mode if cert_mode in ("cert", "tropidist") else False)
7371 _warn_cert_ignored(cert_mode, finC=finC, smax=smax, dW=dW, maxC=maxC, method=method)
7372 _warn_table_gb_unused(eff_table_gb, cert_mode, is_codedist=is_codedist)
7373 _warn_experimental_ksub(ksub, method, solver)
7374
7375 if G is None and L is None:
7376 raise ValueError(
7377 "Either G (dual generator matrix) or L (logical operator matrix) "
7378 "must be specified for quantum distance."
7379 )
7380 if G is not None and L is not None:
7381 raise ValueError("Either G or L should be specified for quantum distance, not both.")
7382 _warn_ortho(ortho, G is not None, solver)
7383
7384 if is_codedist:
7385 if do_cws or outC:
7386 raise ValueError("Codeword extraction is not supported with codedistance solver; use solver='dist_m4ri'.")
7387 _warn_codedistance_ignored(locals())
7388 codedistance = _get_codedistance()
7389 import numpy as np
7390 params = dict(codedistance_params or {})
7391 if num_steps is not None and "iterCount" not in params:
7392 params["iterCount"] = num_steps
7393
7394 if G is None and L is not None:
7395 raise ValueError(
7396 "The 'codedistance' solver requires the stabilizer generator matrix G, "
7397 "not the logical operator matrix L. Use solver='dist_m4ri' with L."
7398 )
7399 if _k0_of_matrices(H, G=G): # (since version 0.17.2)
7400 _k0_found("rank H + rank G = n")
7401 return (0, [0, 0, 0]) if return_info else 0
7402 H_mat = H.toarray() if hasattr(H, 'toarray') else (
7403 np.asarray(H, dtype=np.int8) if isinstance(H, (np.ndarray, list)) else None
7404 )
7405 dual_mat = G if G is not None else L
7406 dual_arr = dual_mat.toarray() if hasattr(dual_mat, 'toarray') else (
7407 np.asarray(dual_mat, dtype=np.int8) if isinstance(dual_mat, (np.ndarray, list)) else None
7408 )
7409
7410 res = codedistance.codeDistance(
7411 H_mat, dual_arr, tB=1, method=codedistance_method, params=params,
7412 seed=seed if seed != 0 else None
7413 )
7414 d = res.get("d", -1)
7415 if return_info:
7416 d_info = format_bounds_list(d, d, 0) if d > 0 else [0, 0, 0]
7417 return d, d_info
7418 return d
7419
7420 eff_cache_file = str(Path(cache_file).resolve()) if cache_file is not None else _distance_cache_file
7421

7426 num_steps=num_steps, d_exp=d_exp, dmin=dmin_s, dmax=dmax_s, dstop=dstop, wmin=wmin, wmax=wmax,

7440 t_call = time.monotonic()

7443 _, qec_io, qec_pipeline = _get_qec_cert() # (the import, before its time limit is counted)

7445 verbose=verbose)

7448 _cert_to_csr(H, qec_io), _cert_to_csr(L, qec_io), _cert_to_csr(G, qec_io)
7449 ),
7450 wmax=w_hi, threads=threads or (os.cpu_count() or 8), seed=seed if seed != 0 else 1,

7452 use_ub=_auto_stage_b_use_ub(dmin_s, dmax_s), **h_kw,
7453 )

7455 lambda: _matrix_cache_key(H, G, L, False), certify, label="quantum", dmin=dmin_s, dmax=dmax_s,

7460 def run_fn(w_lo: int, w_hi: int) -> Tuple[Dict[str, Any], Any, Any]:
7461 H_csr, L_csr, k0_reason = _tropidist_prepare_quantum(H, G, L, ortho=ortho)
7462 if k0_reason is not None:

7474 res = _auto_two_stage(run_native, run_cert, timeout=timeout, dmin=eff_dmin, dmax=eff_dmax, dstop=dstop,
7475 wmax=wmax, label="quantum", debug=debug, verbose=verbose, run_tropidist=run_trop)
7476 dist, d_info = res["dist"], res["d_info"]
7477 return (dist, d_info) if return_info else dist

7479 if _can_delegate_to_tropidist(cert_mode, do_cws=do_cws, outC=outC):
7480 def run_trop_quantum(w_lo: int, w_hi: int) -> Tuple[Dict[str, Any], Any, Any]:
7481 H_csr, L_csr, k0_reason = _tropidist_prepare_quantum(H, G, L, ortho=ortho)
7482 if k0_reason is not None:

7487 )

7493 )

7499 start_list=start_list,
7500 ):
7501 _, qec_io, qec_pipeline = _get_qec_cert()
7502 mode_arg = "ub" if method == 1 else "auto"
7503 res = _cert_code_distance(
7504 lambda: _matrix_cache_key(H, G, L, False),
7505 lambda w_lo, w_hi, dmax_c: qec_pipeline.certify(
7506 qec_io.DistanceProblem(
7507 _cert_to_csr(H, qec_io), _cert_to_csr(L, qec_io), _cert_to_csr(G, qec_io)
7508 ),
7509 wmax=w_hi, threads=threads or (os.cpu_count() or 8),
7510 seed=seed if seed != 0 else 1,
7511 time_limit=_auto_timeout(timeout),
7512 mode=mode_arg,
7513 **_cert_handoff_kw(qec_pipeline, w_lo, search=mode_arg != "ub", dmax=dmax_c, debug=debug,
7514 verbose=verbose),
7515 ),
7516 label="quantum", dmin=eff_dmin, dmax=eff_dmax, dstop=dstop, wmax=wmax,
7517 eff_cache_file=eff_cache_file, debug=debug, verbose=verbose,
7518 )
7519 dist, d_info = res["dist"], res["d_info"]
7520 return (dist, d_info) if return_info else dist
7521
7522 res = run_native(timeout, eff_dmin, eff_dmax)
7523 dist, d_info, cws = res["dist"], res["d_info"], res["cws"]
7524 if return_info:
7525 return (dist, d_info, cws) if do_cws else (dist, d_info)
7526 return (dist, cws) if do_cws else dist
