8755
8756def _model_detector_groups(circuit: Any) -> Tuple[List[int], List[bool], int]:
8757 """
8758 The groups of the detectors of a Stim circuit for its code-sized model (see compute_model_lower_bound()): two
8759 detectors are in the same group if they share a measurement record other than a final data measurement. The final
8760 data measurements are the measurements in the final measurement block (after both the last detector which precedes
8761 the last measurement and the last unitary gate) of qubits not measured before it, or all measurements of the final
8762 block if there are none (e.g., if every qubit is measured in each round). In a memory circuit, the groups are the
8763 chains of the detectors of the checks, linked by the measurements of their ancillas in consecutive rounds; the
8764 chain of a check of the measured basis ends with its detector of the final data measurements.
8765
8766 Returns:
8767 (group, final, num_final): the group of each detector (numbered in the order of their first detectors), for
8768 each group whether one of its detectors has a final data measurement, and the number of final data
8769 measurements.
8770 """
8771 stim = _get_stim()
8772 det_recs: List[List[int]] = [] # the measurement records of each detector (absolute indices)
8773 det_pos: List[int] = [] # its position in the flattened circuit
8774 meas_pos: List[int] = [] # the position of the instruction of each measurement record
8775 meas_qubits: List[frozenset] = [] # and its qubits
8776 last_gate_pos = -1 # the position of the last unitary gate (for end-of-circuit DETECTORs)
8777 for pos, inst in enumerate(circuit.flattened()):
8778 if inst.name == "DETECTOR":
8779 n = len(meas_pos)
8780 det_recs.append([n + t.value for t in inst.targets_copy() if t.is_measurement_record_target])
8781 det_pos.append(pos)
8782 else:
8783 gd = stim.gate_data(inst.name)
8784 if gd.produces_measurements:
8785 for grp in inst.target_groups(): # (one record per group, e.g., per Pauli product of MPP)
8786 meas_pos.append(pos)
8787 meas_qubits.append(frozenset() if inst.name == "MPAD" else
8788 frozenset(t.qubit_value for t in grp if t.qubit_value is not None))
8789 elif gd.is_unitary:
8790 last_gate_pos = pos
8791 last_meas = meas_pos[-1] if meas_pos else -1
8792 last_det = max((p for p in det_pos if p < last_meas), default=-1)
8793 cutoff = max(last_det, last_gate_pos)
8794 before: Set[int] = set() # the qubits measured before the final measurement block
8795 for p, qs in zip(meas_pos, meas_qubits):
8796 if p <= cutoff:
8797 before |= qs
8798 final_data = {r for r, (p, qs) in enumerate(zip(meas_pos, meas_qubits)) if p > cutoff and qs and not qs & before}
8799 if not final_data: # (e.g., all qubits are measured in every round): all measurements of the final block
8800 final_data = {r for r, p in enumerate(meas_pos) if p > cutoff}
8801 parent = list(range(len(det_recs)))
8802
8803 def find(a: int) -> int:
8804 while parent[a] != a:
8805 parent[a] = parent[parent[a]]
8806 a = parent[a]
8807 return a
8808
8809 first_det: Dict[int, int] = {} # the first detector of each measurement record (other than final data)
8810 for d, recs in enumerate(det_recs):
8811 for r in recs:
8812 if r not in final_data:
8813 a, b = find(d), find(first_det.setdefault(r, d))
8814 if a != b:
8815 parent[max(a, b)] = min(a, b) # (the root of a group is its first detector)
8816 ids: Dict[int, int] = {}
8817 group = [ids.setdefault(find(d), len(ids)) for d in range(len(det_recs))]
8818 final = [False] * len(ids)
8819 for d, recs in enumerate(det_recs):
8820 if any(r in final_data for r in recs):
8821 final[group[d]] = True
8822 return group, final, len(final_data)
8823
8824
8825def _dem_detector_groups(dem: Any, pmin: float = 0.0) -> Tuple[List[int], List[bool], int, int, int]:
8826 """
8827 Pure-DEM detector chains for compute_model_lower_bound() when no Stim circuit is available (or when the circuit
8828 groups are trivial). Uses detector coordinates (x, y, ..., t) when present in the DEM to group detectors with the
8829 same spatial coordinates across rounds, and falls back to linking consecutive-round detectors via dominant weight-2
8830 observable-free (ancilla measurement) error mechanisms when coordinates are absent.
8831
8832 Returns:
8833 (group, final, num_final, num_detectors, num_observables).
8834 """
8835 if isinstance(dem, (str, Path)):
8836 with open(str(dem)) as f:
8837 lines = f.read().splitlines()
8838 else:
8839 lines = str(dem.flattened() if hasattr(dem, "flattened") else dem).splitlines()
8840
8841 det_coords: Dict[int, Tuple[float, ...]] = {}
8842 max_det = -1
8843 max_obs = -1
8844
8845 parse_dem_line = _dem_instruction_parts # (the name, args, and targets of a line; tags and comments)
8846
8847 def parse_block(i: int, det_shift: int, c_shift: Tuple[float, ...]) -> Tuple[int, int, Tuple[float, ...]]:
8848 nonlocal max_det, max_obs
8849 while i < len(lines):
8850 name, args, rest = parse_dem_line(lines[i])
8851 i += 1
8852 if not name:
8853 continue
8854 if name == "}":
8855 return i, det_shift, c_shift
8856 if name == "repeat":
8857 count = int(rest.split()[0])
8858 body, end = i, i
8859 for _ in range(count):
8860 end, det_shift, c_shift = parse_block(body, det_shift, c_shift)
8861 if count <= 0:
8862 depth = 1
8863 while end < len(lines) and depth > 0:
8864 nm, _, _ = parse_dem_line(lines[end])
8865 end += 1
8866 depth += (nm == "repeat") - (nm == "}")
8867 i = end
8868 elif name == "shift_detectors":
8869 if args:
8870 vals = [float(x) for x in args.split(",") if x.strip()]
8871 n_c = max(len(c_shift), len(vals))
8872 c_shift = tuple(
8873 (c_shift[k] if k < len(c_shift) else 0.0) + (vals[k] if k < len(vals) else 0.0)
8874 for k in range(n_c)
8875 )
8876 if rest:
8877 det_shift += int(rest.rsplit(None, 1)[-1])
8878 elif name == "detector":
8879 coords: Tuple[float, ...] = ()
8880 if args:
8881 vals = [float(x) for x in args.split(",") if x.strip()]
8882 coords = tuple(vals[k] + (c_shift[k] if k < len(c_shift) else 0.0) for k in range(len(vals)))
8883 for tok in rest.split():
8884 if tok.startswith("D"):
8885 d = int(tok[1:]) + det_shift
8886 max_det = max(max_det, d)
8887 if coords:
8888 det_coords[d] = coords
8889 elif name == "logical_observable":
8890 for tok in rest.split():
8891 if tok.startswith("L"):
8892 max_obs = max(max_obs, int(tok[1:]))
8893 elif name == "error":
8894 p_text = args.strip()
8895 if float(p_text) < pmin:
8896 continue
8897 for tok in rest.split():
8898 if tok.startswith("D"):
8899 max_det = max(max_det, int(tok[1:]) + det_shift)
8900 elif tok.startswith("L"):
8901 max_obs = max(max_obs, int(tok[1:]))
8902 return i, det_shift, c_shift
8903
8904 parse_block(0, 0, ())
8905 num_det = int(getattr(dem, "num_detectors", max_det + 1) or (max_det + 1))
8906 num_obs = int(getattr(dem, "num_observables", max_obs + 1) or (max_obs + 1))
8907 if num_det <= 0:
8908 return [], [], 0, 0, max(0, num_obs)
8909
8910 if len(det_coords) == num_det and all(len(c) >= 2 for c in det_coords.values()):
8911 spatial_ids: Dict[Tuple[float, ...], int] = {}
8912 group = [spatial_ids.setdefault(det_coords[d][:-1], len(spatial_ids)) for d in range(num_det)]
8913 if 1 <= len(spatial_ids) < num_det:
8914 max_t = max(c[-1] for c in det_coords.values())
8915 final = [False] * len(spatial_ids)
8916 for d in range(num_det):
8917 if det_coords[d][-1] == max_t:
8918 final[group[d]] = True
8919 if all(final):
8920 counts = [0] * len(spatial_ids)
8921 for g in group:
8922 counts[g] += 1
8923 max_c = max(counts, default=0)
8924 if max_c > 1 and 0 < sum(c == max_c for c in counts) < len(spatial_ids):
8925 final = [c == max_c for c in counts]
8926 return group, final, sum(final), num_det, max(0, num_obs)
8927
8928 cols_prob = _dem_error_columns(dem, pmin, with_prob=True)
8929 pair_prob: Dict[Tuple[int, int], float] = {}
8930 best_inc = [0.0] * num_det
8931 for dets, obs, p_text in cols_prob:
8932 if len(dets) == 2 and not obs:
8933 u, v = sorted(dets)
8934 if 0 <= u < v < num_det:
8935 p = float(p_text)
8936 if p > pair_prob.get((u, v), -1.0):
8937 pair_prob[(u, v)] = p
8938 if p > best_inc[u]:
8939 best_inc[u] = p
8940 if p > best_inc[v]:
8941 best_inc[v] = p
8942
8943 parent = list(range(num_det))
8944
8945 def find(a: int) -> int:
8946 while parent[a] != a:
8947 parent[a] = parent[parent[a]]
8948 a = parent[a]
8949 return a
8950
8951 has_next = [False] * num_det
8952 has_prev = [False] * num_det
8953 cand_edges = [
8954 (p, u, v) for (u, v), p in pair_prob.items()
8955 if p >= 0.5 * max(best_inc[u], best_inc[v])
8956 ]
8957 cand_edges.sort(key=lambda item: (-item[0], item[1], item[2]))
8958 for _, u, v in cand_edges:
8959 if not has_next[u] and not has_prev[v]:
8960 ru, rv = find(u), find(v)
8961 if ru != rv:
8962 parent[max(ru, rv)] = min(ru, rv)
8963 has_next[u] = True
8964 has_prev[v] = True
8965
8966 ids: Dict[int, int] = {}
8967 group = [ids.setdefault(find(d), len(ids)) for d in range(num_det)]
8968 counts = [0] * len(ids)
8969 for g in group:
8970 counts[g] += 1
8971 max_len = max(counts, default=0)
8972 if max_len > 1 and 0 < sum(c == max_len for c in counts) < len(ids):
8973 final = [c == max_len for c in counts]
8974 else:
8975 final = [True] * len(ids)
8976 return group, final, sum(final), num_det, max(0, num_obs)
8977
8978
8979def _model_matrices(
8980 cols: List[Tuple[Any, ...]], group: List[int], use: List[bool], num_observables: int
8981) -> Dict[str, Any]:
8982 """
8983 The matrices of a code-sized model (see compute_model_lower_bound()): one row per group of detectors with use[g]
8984 (the sum of the rows of its detectors), and one column per distinct pair (model column, observables) of the error
8985 mechanisms `cols` (see _dem_error_columns()); the errors with no effect on the rows nor on the observables are
8986 dropped.
8987
8988 Returns:
8989 dict with "H" and "L" (scipy.sparse.csr_matrix), "col_map" (the model column of each error mechanism, -1 if
8990 it is dropped), "groups" (the group of each row), and "trivial" (the error mechanisms which flip an observable
8991 but no row: then the model has a codeword of weight 1).
8992 """
8993 import numpy as np
8994 import scipy.sparse as sp
8995 index: Dict[Tuple[frozenset, frozenset], int] = {}
8996 col_map: List[int] = []
8997 trivial: List[int] = []
8998 for j, (dets, obs) in enumerate(cols):
8999 rows: Set[int] = set()
9000 for d in dets:
9001 if use[group[d]]:
9002 rows ^= {group[d]}
9003 if not rows:
9004 col_map.append(-1)
9005 if obs:
9006 trivial.append(j)
9007 continue
9008 col_map.append(index.setdefault((frozenset(rows), obs), len(index)))
9009 used = sorted({g for rows, _ in index for g in rows})
9010 row_of = {g: i for i, g in enumerate(used)}
9011 hi: List[int] = []
9012 hj: List[int] = []
9013 li: List[int] = []
9014 lj: List[int] = []
9015 for c, (rows, obs) in enumerate(index):
9016 hi.extend(row_of[g] for g in rows)
9017 hj.extend([c] * len(rows))
9018 li.extend(obs)
9019 lj.extend([c] * len(obs))
9020 H = sp.csr_matrix((np.ones(len(hi), dtype=np.int8), (hi, hj)), shape=(len(used), len(index)))
9021 L = sp.csr_matrix((np.ones(len(li), dtype=np.int8), (li, lj)), shape=(num_observables, len(index)))
9022 return {"H": H, "L": L, "col_map": col_map, "groups": used, "trivial": trivial}
9023
9024
9025def compute_model_lower_bound(
9026 circuit: Any = None,
9027 dist_m4ri: Optional[str] = None,
9028 method: int = 3,
9029 threads: Optional[int] = None,
9030 timeout: float = 60.0,
9031 num_steps: Optional[int] = None,
9032 dstop: int = 0,
9033 wmax: int = 0,
9034 minority: bool = False,
9035 pmin: float = 0.0,
9036 rounds: Optional[int] = None,
9037 p_noise: float = 0.001,
9038 force_noise: bool = False,
9039 out_model: Optional[Union[str, Path]] = None,
9040 cache_file: Optional[Union[str, Path]] = None,
9041 seed: int = 0,
9042 debug: int = 0,
9043 verbose: bool = False,
9044 nothrottle: bool = False,
9045 pairs: int = -1,
9046 sort_rows: Optional[bool] = None,
9047 cc_prune: Optional[int] = None,
9048 return_info: bool = False,
9049 dem: Optional[Any] = None,
9050 rw_opt: Optional[int] = None,
9051 **kwargs
9052) -> Any:
9053 """
9054 Certified lower bound on the circuit-level distance of a Stim memory circuit (or standalone DEM) from its
9055 code-sized model.
9056
9057 The model is a row reduction of the DEM (H, L) of the circuit or DEM (processed as in compute_dem_distance(), with
9058 the options rounds, p_noise, force_noise, and pmin): for a circuit, two detectors are linked if they share a
9059 measurement record other than a final data measurement, and each group of linked detectors gives one row, the sum
9060 of the rows of its detectors (see _model_detector_groups()). For a standalone DEM (or if the circuit groups are
9061 trivial), detector chains across rounds are grouped by spatial detector coordinates (x, y, ..., t) when present, or
9062 else by linking consecutive-round detectors via dominant weight-2 observable-free error mechanisms (see
9063 _dem_detector_groups()). In a memory circuit, the groups are the chains of the detectors of the checks over the
9064 rounds: the chain of a check h of the measured basis telescopes to the parity of the final data measurements on its
9065 support, so that the column of an error mechanism is the syndrome of its net data error (a data error or a hook
9066 error), and the chains of the minority-basis checks (with minority=True) add the net change of their values between
9067 their first and last measurements. Equal columns are merged, and the errors with no effect on the rows nor on the
9068 observables (e.g., ancilla measurement errors) are dropped; the model has a few columns per data qubit. Since
9069 every row is a sum of detector rows, every codeword x of the DEM (Hx = 0, Lx != 0) gives a model codeword of weight
9070 at most |x|: the distance of the model, as certified by CC (its dmin), is a lower bound on the distance of the DEM.
9071 It ignores the timing within the rounds, so it is not tight in general (e.g., 5 for the bb_72 circuit of distance
9072 6). Any circuit or DEM gives a valid bound, but a useful one needs this structure; if an error flips an observable
9073 but no row, the bound is 1 (with a note to stderr).
9074
9075 The binary runs on the model with the rows of the measured-basis chains first, and then (with minority=True) on
9076 the model with all rows, starting from that bound (the extra rows can only raise it): RW first (unless method=2 or
9077 num_steps=0), which ends as soon as it finds a model codeword of that weight (then the bound is not raised), and
9078 only otherwise with `method` (CC from dmin). The minority-basis rows are off by default: with depolarizing-type
9079 noise, every net data error which flips the measured-basis observable also occurs without a component of the other
9080 basis, so that a lightest model codeword has a version which the minority-basis rows do not detect (they never
9081 raised the bound of the benchmark circuits or of the surface-code circuits of stim, and cost up to 9 s for the
9082 mitten_270 circuits); they may raise it for other noise models (e.g., biased noise). The certified bound is stored
9083 as dmin in the cache record of the DEM (the same key as compute_dem_distance(); "dmin_model": the bound), so that a
9084 later compute_dem_distance() starts CC from it; the distances of the models are cached under their own keys.
9085
9086 Args:
9087 circuit: Stim memory circuit (stim.Circuit or .stim file), or a DEM (stim.DetectorErrorModel or .dem file)
9088 when `dem` is omitted.
9089 dem: Optional standalone DEM (stim.DetectorErrorModel or .dem file); takes precedence over `circuit` if given.
9090 dist_m4ri: Path to dist_m4ri executable (optional).
9091 method: Solver method for the model (1=RW, 2=CC, 3=Bracketing default); only CC certifies a bound.
9092 threads / timeout / num_steps / seed / nothrottle / pairs: As for compute_dem_distance(), for each run of the
9093 binary (at most three).
9094 sort_rows / cc_prune: The row order and the CC search of the binary (see run_dist_m4ri(); None, the default:
9095 the binary's defaults, i.e., the rows of the model sorted by weight, and the branch and bound), for each
9096 run. The bound and the cache keys do not depend on them.
9097 rw_opt: Expert option (since version 0.17.0): the stages of the RW search of the binary, for each run (None,
9098 the default: the binary's -1, automatic; see run_dist_m4ri()). The bound does not depend on it.
9099 dstop: Stop target (see compute_dem_distance()): the runs end once CC has certified dmin >= dstop.
9100 wmax: Maximum weight of the CC rounds on the model (0: until the bounds meet or the timeout).
9101 minority: If True, the groups without a final data measurement (e.g., the chains of the minority-basis
9102 checks of a CSS circuit) are rows of the model as well (default: False; CLI: --model-minority).
9103 pmin: Probability cutoff for the error mechanisms of the DEM.
9104 rounds / p_noise / force_noise: The processing of the circuit, as in compute_dem_distance().
9105 out_model: If given, the model matrices H and L (the measured-basis rows by default, or all rows with
9106 minority=True) are written to PREFIX_HR.mtx and PREFIX_LR.mtx.
9107 cache_file: Optional JSON file path for persistent distance caching.
9108 debug / verbose: As for compute_dem_distance().
9109 return_info: If True, return (bound, info).
9110
9111 Returns:
9112 The certified lower bound, or (bound, info) with return_info=True, where info has "d_info" (the bounds
9113 [dmin, dmax, rw_steps] of the circuit's DEM from the cache record, with dmin including the bound; [bound, 0, 0]
9114 without the cache), "model_d_info" and "measured_d_info" (the bounds of the model and of its measured-basis
9115 part, [] if not run), the sizes "rows", "cols", "rows_measured", "cols_measured", "groups", "groups_final",
9116 "detectors", "final_data", "dem_cols", "trivial" (the error mechanisms which flip an observable but no row),
9117 the model "H", "L", and "col_map" (the model column of each error mechanism of the DEM, -1 if dropped), and
9118 "files" (the files written with out_model).
9119
9120 Raises:
9121 TypeError: for an unknown keyword argument (e.g., a misspelled option).
9122 ValueError: if neither a Stim circuit (.stim) nor a DEM (.dem) is given, if `rounds` is given without a
9123 circuit or is negative, if `p_noise` is outside [0, 0.5], if `rw_opt` is out of range, or if the circuit
9124 and DEM detector counts disagree.
9125 """
9126 global _distance_cache
9127 _check_kwargs(compute_model_lower_bound, kwargs, aliases=())
9128 _check_rw_opt(rw_opt)
9129 src = dem if dem is not None else circuit
9130 if src is None:
9131 raise ValueError("compute_model_lower_bound: a Stim circuit (.stim) or DEM (.dem) is required")
9132 is_dem_input = dem is not None or (
9133 isinstance(src, (str, Path)) and str(src).endswith(".dem")
9134 ) or (not isinstance(src, (str, Path)) and not hasattr(src, "detector_error_model"))
9135 if isinstance(src, (str, Path)) and not str(src).endswith((".stim", ".dem")):
9136 raise ValueError(f"compute_model_lower_bound: {src} is not a Stim circuit (.stim) or DEM (.dem)")
9137 if not 0.0 <= p_noise <= 0.5:
9138 raise ValueError(f"invalid p_noise={p_noise}: the noise strength must be in [0, 0.5]")
9139 circ_verbose = verbose or bool(debug & PY_DBG_CIRCUITS)
9140 dem_obj, circ, _ = _dem_from_input(
9141 src if is_dem_input else None, None if is_dem_input else src,
9142 rounds=rounds, p_noise=p_noise, circ_verbose=circ_verbose, force_noise=force_noise
9143 )
9144 dem = dem_obj
9145 info: Dict[str, Any] = {"d_info": [0, 0, 0], "model_d_info": [], "measured_d_info": [], "files": []}
9146 if getattr(dem, "num_errors", None) == 0:
9147 sys.stderr.write("# Note: the DEM has no error mechanisms (no noise, e.g., p_noise=0 for a noiseless circuit "
9148 "or with force_noise): no bound computed\n")
9149 return (0, info) if return_info else 0
9150 cols = _dem_error_columns(dem, pmin)
9151 if not cols:
9152 sys.stderr.write("# Note: the DEM has no error mechanisms (no noise, e.g., p_noise=0 for a noiseless circuit "
9153 "or with force_noise): no bound computed\n")
9154 return (0, info) if return_info else 0
9155 if circ is not None:
9156 group, final, num_final = _model_detector_groups(circ)
9157 num_det = int(getattr(dem, "num_detectors", len(group)))
9158 num_obs = int(getattr(dem, "num_observables", 0))
9159 if len(group) != num_det:
9160 raise ValueError(f"compute_model_lower_bound: {len(group)} detectors in the circuit, {num_det} in its DEM")
9161 if len(final) == len(group) and len(group) > 1:
9162 dem_group, dem_final, dem_num_final, _, _ = _dem_detector_groups(dem, pmin)
9163 if len(dem_group) == len(group) and len(dem_final) < len(group):
9164 group, final, num_final = dem_group, dem_final, dem_num_final
9165 else:
9166 group, final, num_final, num_det, num_obs = _dem_detector_groups(dem, pmin)
9167 part = _model_matrices(cols, group, final, num_obs) # the rows of the measured-basis chains
9168 full = _model_matrices(cols, group, [True] * len(final), num_obs) if minority else part
9169 info.update(rows=full["H"].shape[0], cols=full["H"].shape[1], rows_measured=part["H"].shape[0],
9170 cols_measured=part["H"].shape[1], groups=len(final), groups_final=sum(final), detectors=len(group),
9171 final_data=num_final, dem_cols=len(cols), trivial=len(full["trivial"]), H=full["H"], L=full["L"],
9172 col_map=full["col_map"])
9173 if verbose:
9174 print(f"[dist_m4ri] Code-sized model: {info['rows']} x {info['cols']} ({info['rows_measured']} rows of the "
9175 f"chains with final data measurements, {info['rows'] - info['rows_measured']} other), from "
9176 f"{len(cols)} error mechanisms and {len(group)} detectors in {len(final)} groups ({num_final} final data "
9177 f"measurements)")
9178 if out_model:
9179 from scipy.io import mmwrite
9180 for name, M in (("HR", full["H"]), ("LR", full["L"])):
9181 path = f"{out_model}_{name}.mtx"
9182 parent_dir = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path))
9183 os.makedirs(parent_dir, exist_ok=True)
9184 mmwrite(path, M, symmetry="general")
9185 info["files"].append(path)
9186 if verbose:
9187 print(f"[dist_m4ri] Saved the code-sized model to '{info['files'][0]}' and '{info['files'][1]}'")
9188 eff_cache_file = str(Path(cache_file).resolve()) if cache_file is not None else _distance_cache_file
9189
9190 def run(model: Dict[str, Any], dmin: int, run_method: int, wmin: int = 1) -> List[int]:
9191 # the bounds [dmin, dmax, rw_steps] of the model
9192 res = _cached_code_distance(
9193 model["H"], None, model["L"], False, "code-sized model", dist_m4ri=dist_m4ri, method=run_method,
9194 threads=threads, timeout=timeout, num_steps=num_steps, d_exp=0, dmin=dmin, dmax=0, dstop=dstop,
9195 wmin=wmin, wmax=wmax, smax=0, start_list=None, dW=-1, maxC=0, finC=None, outC=None, need_cws=False,
9196 eff_cache_file=eff_cache_file, seed=seed, debug=debug, verbose=verbose, nothrottle=nothrottle,
9197 chunk_size=0, ksub=0, kwin=0, win_mode=0, min_hits=None, cov_cws=100, refresh=None, trust_start=False,
9198 pairs=pairs, sort_rows=sort_rows, cc_prune=cc_prune, rw_opt=rw_opt)
9199 return list(res["d_info"])
9200
9201 if full["trivial"]:
9202 sys.stderr.write(f"# Note: code-sized model: {len(full['trivial'])} error mechanisms flip an observable but no "
9203 f"group of detectors (e.g., the first one, column {full['trivial'][0]} of the DEM), so that "
9204 f"the model has a codeword of weight 1: the bound is 1\n")
9205 bound = 1
9206 else:
9207 bound = 1
9208 if not part["trivial"]:
9209 info["measured_d_info"] = run(part, 0, method)
9210 bound = max(bound, info["measured_d_info"][0])
9211 info["model_d_info"] = info["measured_d_info"]
9212 if full is not part and (dstop <= 0 or bound < dstop) and (wmax <= 0 or bound <= wmax):
9213 # all rows: RW first (a model codeword of weight `bound` ends the search), then CC from the bound
9214 dmin = bound if bound > 1 else 0
9215 if method == 1 or (method != 2 and num_steps != 0):
9216 info["model_d_info"] = run(full, dmin, 1, wmin=bound)
9217 need_cc = method != 1 and not 0 < info["model_d_info"][1] <= bound
9218 else:
9219 need_cc = True
9220 if need_cc:
9221 info["model_d_info"] = run(full, dmin, method)
9222 bound = max(bound, info["model_d_info"][0])
9223 info["d_info"] = [bound, 0, 0]
9224 if _use_distance_cache: # the bound as dmin in the cache record of the DEM
9225 if eff_cache_file:
9226 load_distance_cache(eff_cache_file)
9227 key = _dem_cache_key(dem, pmin)
9228 prev = _distance_cache.get(key) or {}
9229 p_dmin, p_dmax, p_rw = (prev.get("dmin", 0) or 0), (prev.get("dmax", 0) or 0), (prev.get("rw_steps", 0) or 0)
9230 if p_dmax > 0 and bound > p_dmax:
9231 sys.stderr.write(f"# Warning: the code-sized model bound {bound} exceeds the cached upper bound "
9232 f"{p_dmax} of the DEM: not stored\n")
9233 info["d_info"] = format_bounds_list(p_dmin, p_dmax, p_rw)
9234 else:
9235 record = _sector_record(max(p_dmin, bound), p_dmax, p_rw, prev.get("cws", []))
9236 record["dmin_model"] = max(bound, prev.get("dmin_model", 0) or 0)
9237 if record != prev:
9238 _distance_cache[key] = record
9239 if eff_cache_file:
9240 save_distance_cache(eff_cache_file)
9241 info["d_info"] = list(record["d_info"])
9242 if verbose:
9243 print(f"[dist_m4ri] Code-sized model: certified lower bound d >= {bound} on the circuit distance (model bounds "
9244 f"{info['model_d_info']}; measured-basis rows only: {info['measured_d_info']})")
9245 return (bound, info) if return_info else bound
9246
9247
9248def _write_nzlist_file(filepath: str, cws: List[List[int]]) -> None:
9249 """Writes codewords to a text file in NZLIST format (1-based indices).
9250 Skips creating the file if cws is empty.
9251 """
9252 if not cws:
9253 return
9254 with open(filepath, "w") as f:
9255 f.write("%% NZLIST\n")
9256 f.write(f"% {len(cws)} codewords\n")
9257 for cw in cws:
9258 f.write(f"{len(cw)} " + " ".join(str(idx + 1) for idx in cw) + "\n")
9259
9260
9261_CLI_FALSE = ("0", "false", "no", "off", "none") # the CLI values of a flag which mean off (also as "" for some)
9262# the CLI file options which also take the file name as the next argument, as in the binary ('finH= FILE')
9263_CLI_FILE_KEYS = ("fdem", "dem", "finh", "fing", "finl", "fin", "hx", "finhx", "hz", "finhz", "lx", "finlx", "lz",
9264 "finlz", "finc", "outc", "outd", "drop", "steplog", "json")

9266
9267def _cli_arg_text(key: str, val: str, arg: str) -> str:
9268 """The argument as written, for the messages: 'key=val' (also for the form '--key VALUE')."""
9269 return arg if "=" in arg else f"{key}={val}"
9270
9271
9272_LLONG_MIN, _LLONG_MAX = -(1 << 63), (1 << 63) - 1
9273_INT_MIN, _INT_MAX = -(1 << 31), (1 << 31) - 1
9274
9275
9276def _cli_int(val: str, arg: str, ll: bool = False) -> int:
9277 """
9278 The integer value of a CLI argument arg (e.g., 'steps=1000'), as parse_ll_value() / int_arg() of the dist_m4ri
9279 binary: a decimal integer, an integer written as a floating-point number (e.g., steps=1e5 or 100000.0), or the
9280 signed decimal integer prefix with a warning to stderr (e.g., 'steps=1.5' -> 1, 'threads=4x' -> 4); ValueError
9281 naming the argument without a numeric prefix (e.g., steps=, steps=abc, steps=nan, steps=inf) or out of range.
9282 """
9283 import math
9284 import re
9285 s = str(val).lstrip()
9286 m = re.match(r"^[+-]?\d+", s)
9287 if m is None:
9288 raise ValueError(f"invalid '{arg}': expected an integer")
9289 x = int(m.group(0), 10)
9290 if not _LLONG_MIN <= x <= _LLONG_MAX:
9291 raise ValueError(f"invalid '{arg}': expected an integer")
9292 rest = s[m.end():]
9293 if rest:
9294 try:
9295 f = float(s) if not rest[-1:].isspace() else math.nan
9296 except ValueError:
9297 f = math.nan
9298 if math.isfinite(f) and f.is_integer() and abs(f) <= 9.0e18:
9299 x = int(f)
9300 else:
9301 sys.stderr.write(f"# WARNING: '{arg}' read as {x} (the rest of the value, '{rest}', is ignored)\n")
9302 lo, hi = (_LLONG_MIN, _LLONG_MAX) if ll else (_INT_MIN, _INT_MAX)
9303 if not lo <= x <= hi:
9304 raise ValueError(f"invalid '{arg}': the value is out of range")
9305 return x
9306
9307
9308def _cli_float(val: str, arg: str) -> float:
9309 """The finite number of a CLI argument arg (e.g., 'timeout=1.5'); ValueError naming the argument otherwise."""
9310 import math
9311 try:
9312 v = float(str(val).strip())
9313 except ValueError:
9314 v = math.nan
9315 if not math.isfinite(v): # (nan, inf: not a value; timeout=0 is no limit)
9316 raise ValueError(f"invalid '{arg}': expected a number")
9317 return v
9318
9319
9320def _cli_int_or_text(val: str) -> Union[int, str]:
9321 """The value of a disabled CLI option (noscan, cbeg, cend, irred, css): an integer, or the text as given (ignored
9322 with a warning in either case, see _warn_disabled_options() and _warn_cli_conflicts())."""
9323 try:
9324 return int(str(val).strip(), 10)
9325 except ValueError:
9326 return str(val)
9327
9328
9329def _cli_flag(val: str) -> bool:
9330 """The value of a CLI flag given as key=value: False for 0, false, no, off, or none (any case), True otherwise."""
9331 s = str(val).strip()
9332 return bool(int(s)) if s.isdigit() else s.lower() not in _CLI_FALSE
9333
9334
9335def _cli_is_number(tok: str) -> bool:
9336 """Whether a CLI token is a numeric value (e.g., '--kwin -1' or '--kwin -4x'), rather than a flag."""
9337 import math
9338 if len(tok) >= 2 and tok[0] in "+-" and (tok[1].isdigit() or (tok[1] == "." and tok[2:3].isdigit())):
9339 return True
9340 try:
9341 return math.isfinite(float(tok))
9342 except ValueError:
9343 return False

9852 elif key_lower in ("cws", "do_cws", "do-cws", "docws"):
9853 args["do_cws"] = _cli_flag(val)
9854 elif key_lower in ("nothrottle", "no_throttle", "no-throttle"):
9855 args["nothrottle"] = _cli_flag(val)
9856 elif key_lower in ("silent", "quiet", "q"):
9857 args["silent"] = _cli_flag(val)
9858 elif key_lower in ("no-cache", "no_cache", "nocache"):
9859 if _cli_flag(val):
9860 args["use_cache"] = False
9861 args["cache_file"] = None
9862 elif key_lower in ("chunk_size", "chunksize", "batch", "chunk"):
9863 args["chunk_size"] = _cli_int(val, num_arg)
9864 elif key_lower == "ksub":
9865 args["ksub"] = _cli_int(val, num_arg)
9866 elif key_lower in ("kwin", "win"):
9867 args["kwin"] = _cli_int(val, num_arg)
9868 elif key_lower in ("win_mode", "winmode"):
9869 args["win_mode"] = _cli_int(val, num_arg)
9870 elif key_lower in ("win_hyb", "winhyb"):
9871 args["win_hyb"] = _cli_int(val, num_arg)
9872 if args["win_hyb"] < 0:
9873 raise ValueError(f"invalid '{num_arg}': win_hyb should be 0 (256 columns for a DEM, 512 for "
9874 f"matrices) or positive")
9875 elif key_lower == "pairs":
9876 args["pairs"] = _cli_int(val, num_arg)
9877 if not -1 <= args["pairs"] <= 64:
9878 raise ValueError(f"invalid '{num_arg}': pairs should be -1 (auto), 0 (off), or 1 to 64 (random "
9879 f"pivot rows of the buckets)")
9880 elif key_lower in ("min_hits", "minhits", "max_hits", "maxhits"):
9881 args["min_hits"] = _cli_int(val, num_arg)
9882 elif key_lower in ("cov_cws", "covcws"):
9883 args["cov_cws"] = _cli_int(val, num_arg)
9884 elif key_lower == "refresh":
9885 args["refresh"] = _cli_int(val, num_arg)
9886 elif key_lower in ("simple", "simplified", "full"): # disabled since version 0.13.0 (ignored, a warning)
9887 args["full" if key_lower == "full" else "simple"] = (
9888 bool(int(val)) if val.isdigit()
9889 else (val.lower() not in ("0", "false", "no", "off"))
9890 )
9891 elif key_lower == "basis":
9892 if val.upper() not in ("X", "Z"):
9893 raise ValueError(
9894 f"Invalid basis '{val}'; must be 'X' or 'Z'."
9895 )
9896 args["basis"] = val.upper()
9897 elif key_lower == "rounds":
9898 args["rounds"] = _cli_int(val, num_arg)
9899 elif key_lower in ("p_noise", "p-noise", "pnoise"):
9900 args["p_noise"] = _cli_float(val, num_arg)
9901 if not 0.0 <= args["p_noise"] <= 0.5:
9902 raise ValueError(f"invalid '{num_arg}': the noise strength must be in [0, 0.5]")
9903 elif key_lower in ("force_noise", "force-noise", "forcenoise", "force"):
9904 args["force_noise"] = (
9905 bool(int(val)) if val.isdigit() else (val.lower() not in ("0", "false", "no", "off"))
9906 )
9907 elif key_lower in ("out-dir", "out_dir", "outdir"):
9908 args["out_dir"] = val
9909 elif key_lower in ("out-dem", "out_dem", "outdem"):
9910 if val.lower() in ("0", "false", "no", "off", "none"):
9911 args["out_dem"] = None
9912 elif val.lower() in ("1", "true", "yes", "auto", ""):
9913 args["out_dem"] = True
9914 else:
9915 args["out_dem"] = val
9916 elif key_lower in ("model-lb", "model_lb", "modellb"):
9917 args["model_lb"] = (
9918 bool(int(val)) if val.isdigit() else (val.lower() not in ("0", "false", "no", "off"))
9919 )
9920 elif key_lower in ("model-minority", "model_minority", "modelminority"):
9921 args["model_minority"] = (
9922 bool(int(val)) if val.isdigit() else (val.lower() not in ("0", "false", "no", "off"))
9923 )
9924 elif key_lower in ("out-model", "out_model", "outmodel"):
9925 args["out_model"] = val
9926 elif key_lower in ("out-stim", "out_stim", "outstim"):
9927 if val.lower() in ("0", "false", "no", "off", "none"):
9928 args["out_stim"] = None
9929 elif val.lower() in ("1", "true", "yes", "auto", ""):
9930 args["out_stim"] = True
9931 else:
9932 args["out_stim"] = val
9933 else:
9934 args["unrecognized"].append(arg)
9935
9936 i += 1
9937
9938 # Auto-infer classical mode when not explicitly set (matching src/util_io.c)
9939 if args["classical"] == -1:
9940 css_input = args["Hx"] is not None or args["Hz"] is not None # (Lx / Lz are only used with them)
9941 if (
9942 args["finG"] is not None or args["finL"] is not None
9943 or args["Hz"] is not None or (css_input and (args["Lz"] is not None or args["Lx"] is not None))
9944 or args["fdem"] is not None or args["fin"] is not None
9945 ):
9946 args["classical"] = 0
9947 elif args["finH"] is not None or args["Hx"] is not None:
9948 args["classical"] = 1
9949
9950 return args
9951
