9979
9980def print_cli_help(file: Optional[Any] = None) -> None:
9981 help_text = f"""dist_m4ri.py (version {__version__}): Multithreaded distance calculator Python CLI
9982Usage: dist_m4ri.py [key=val | --flag val ...]
9983
9984Input matrices & models:
9985 fdem=FILE Detector Error Model (.dem) or Stim circuit (.stim) file (also dem=FILE)
9986 finH=FILE Parity check matrix H (classical) or Hx (CSS quantum) (.mmx/.mtx)
9987 finG=FILE, finL=FILE Hz check matrix or Lx logical operator matrix (quantum CSS)
9988 fin=PREFIX Base prefix for CSS matrices (loads ${{fin}}X.mtx, ${{fin}}Z.mtx, e.g. try -> tryX.mtx)
9989 Hx=FILE, Hz=FILE CSS check matrices, both required (computes dX and dZ; also finHx=, finHz=)
9990 Lx=FILE, Lz=FILE CSS logical operators (optional, constructed if omitted; also finLx=, finLz=)
9991 pmin=PROB Minimum error probability threshold for DEM errors (default: 0.0)
9992 merge=0|1 Merge equal DEM columns (exact; codewords use the first one) (default: 1)
9993 drop=auto|0|css|FILE DEM detectors to drop if verified exact: auto=1 (default), 0 (none), css, or a file
9994 outD=FILE Write the DEM detectors dropped (0-based) to FILE
9995 --out-reduced [PFX] Save the reduced DEM and its maps to the DEM: PFX_red.dem and PFX_red.json
9996 classical=0|1 1: classical code (finH only), 0: quantum CSS (auto-detected)
9997 basis=X|Z Override primary memory basis ('X' or 'Z') for .stim circuits (with drop=css)
9998 --rounds [N] Set the REPEAT count of a .stim circuit (N=2 if omitted; error without .stim)
9999 --out-dir DIR Output directory for saved .dem/.stim files (default: input file dir)
10000 --out-dem [FILE] Save constructed DEM (default: <basename>_full.dem)
10001 --out-stim [FILE] Save processed/noisy Stim circuit (default: <basename>_full.stim)
10002 --p-noise P Strength of the noise added to a noiseless .stim circuit (default: 0.001; 0: none)
10003 --force-noise Replace the noise of a .stim circuit by that of --p-noise (with P=0: remove it)
10004 --model-lb Certified lower bound for a .stim circuit or .dem from its code-sized model
10005 --model-minority With --model-lb, also the rows of the minority-basis checks (default: off)
10006
10007Method and distance bounds:
10008 method=1|2|3 1=RW (upper bound), 2=CC (lower bound/exact), 3=Bracketing (default: 3; alias: m)
10009 dmin=N Certified lower bound, inclusive (CC starts from dmin) (default: 0)
10010 dmax=N Known upper bound, inclusive (CC up to w=dmax-1 only) (default: 0)
10011 dstop=N Stop once CC certifies dmin>=dstop (not an upper bound) (default: 0)
10012 dexp=N Expected distance estimate (alias: dest) (default: 0)
10013
10014Search limits and stopping criteria:
10015 steps=N Maximum RW steps / information sets (default: 100000; aliases: nsteps, num_steps)
10016 wmax=N Maximum cluster weight to search in CC (0=until bound/timeout; at most 99)
10017 wmin=N Stop immediately if cw with weight <= wmin is found (default: 1)
10018 min_hits=N Stop RW at <n> >= N hits per cw, or by the canonical classes of rw_opt 16 (default: 5; max_hits)
10019 timeout=SEC Execution timeout in seconds, 0 or inf for no timeout (default: 60.0; alias: time)
10020
10021Multithreading & execution:
10022 threads=N Max worker threads (default: all logical CPUs; throttled unless nothrottle=1; t, num_threads)
10023 solver=NAME 'dist_m4ri' (default), 'cert', 'tropidist', 'auto', 'codedistance' (also engine=, table_gb=N)
10024
10025Codeword collection & caching:
10026 --cws Collect minimum-weight codewords in the cache record (outC=FILE writes them; --do_cws)
10027 outC=FILE Save output codewords (for CSS, auto-suffixed _X.nz / _Z.nz)
10028 finC=FILE Input initial candidate codewords (.nz file)
10029 expand=0|1 DEM codewords: list all choices among equal columns (merge) (default: 0)
10030 cache=FILE, --no-cache Persistent JSON cache (default: tmp_dist_cache.json; alias: cache_file; nocache/0: off)
10031 --verbose / -v Explain bounds, steps, cache status, and miss probability estimates
10032 --silent / -q No warnings on stderr for ignored inputs (disabled options still warn; also --quiet)
10033
10034Extra parameters (see --morehelp for details):
10035 smax=N (0) Max syndrome weight for CC confinement profile (0 to disable)
10036 start=LIST (-1) Expert: CC from listed columns only, e.g. start=0,48 (also start_scan=1; see --morehelp)
10037 --trust-start Expert: accept start-list results as valid (copied to main cache record)
10038 noscan, cbeg, cend Disabled (warn, ignored): also css=, irred=0, steplog, slab_*, stamp, json, --simple, --full
10039 ortho=0|1 (1) Expert: 0 skips the check H G^T = 0 of G (valid only if it holds)
10040 sort_rows=0|1 Sort the rows of H by weight for CC (default: 1 for matrices, 0 for a DEM)
10041 cc_prune=0|1|2 (1) CC search: 0 first-row walk, 1 branch and bound, 2 also cover bounds
10042 nothrottle=1 (0) Disable automatic thread throttling (also --no-throttle)
10043 chunk_size=N (0) Max RW batch per claim (default: 0 for adaptive 25-500; aliases: batch, chunk)
10044 ksub=N (0) EXPERIMENTAL, do not use: RW subspace sketch dimension (0: full matrix)
10045 kwin=N (0) RW window size (0: hybrid, n>=500, DEM only if active rw_opt!=0 unless win_hyb>0; -1: off; win)
10046 win_mode=0|1 (0) RW window metric: 0=Tanner graph BFS, 1=index proximity
10047 win_hyb=N (0) Hybrid RW window size (0: 256 for a DEM; 512 for matrices with resolved rw_opt=0, uniform else)
10048 pairs=N (-1) RW pairs of non-pivot columns (p=2; -1: auto, 0: off)
10049 rw_opt=N (-1) RW triplet stages: -1 auto, 0 off (as 0.16.1), or a bitmask 1..63 (also --rw-opt N)
10050 cov_cws=N (100) Number of lowest-weight cws used for the min_hits statistic
10051 refresh=N RW basis refresh interval (0; 5000 with ksub>0; experimental ksub only)
10052 maxC=N (0) Maximum number of codewords to collect (0: unlimited)
10053 dW=N (-1, unset) Extra weight above the minimum weight found (binary 0; any dW>=0 collects cws, native in auto)
10054 seed=N (0) Random number generator seed
10055 debug=N (0) Debug bitmap, OR-combined (1: summary, 2: progress, 4: status, ...; alias: dbg)
10056
10057Help options:
10058 -h, -?, --help [TOPIC] Display this help message (with TOPIC: the same as --morehelp TOPIC)
10059 --morehelp [TOPIC] Display full help for all parameters (or only for TOPIC, e.g., maxC or windows)
10060 --version Display the versions of dist_m4ri.py and of the dist_m4ri binary"""
10061 print(help_text, file=file)
10062
10063
10064def _cli_morehelp_text() -> str:
10065 """The full help text of the CLI (--morehelp)."""
10066 return f"""dist_m4ri.py (version {__version__}): Multithreaded distance calculator Python CLI
10067Usage: dist_m4ri.py [key=val | --flag val ...]
10068
10069Required input (at least one matrix/model specification):
10070 fdem=FILE Detector Error Model (.dem) or Stim circuit (.stim) file (also dem=FILE).
10071 Automatically constructs parity check H and logical L matrices. An error
10072 channel which stim cannot write as independent errors (e.g., PAULI_CHANNEL_1
10073 without Y errors) is converted with approximate_disjoint_errors=True (only the
10074 probabilities change).
10075 finH=FILE Parity check matrix file in Matrix Market (.mmx / .mtx) format.
10076 For classical codes, this is check matrix H. For CSS codes, Hx.
10077 finG=FILE Generator / Hz matrix for quantum CSS codes in Matrix Market format.
10078 finL=FILE Logical operator matrix Lx for quantum CSS codes in Matrix Market format.
10079 Note: For a quantum CSS code, either finL (Lx) or finG (Hz) is required.
10080 fin=PREFIX Base prefix for CSS matrices (loads ${{fin}}X.mtx and ${{fin}}Z.mtx, e.g. try -> tryX.mtx).
10081 Hx=FILE, Hz=FILE CSS check matrices Hx and Hz, both required (alias: finHx=FILE; also
10082 finHz=FILE): computes both dX and dZ, and d = min(dX, dZ) (finH=Hx with
10083 finG=Hz gives dZ only).
10084 Lx=FILE, Lz=FILE Alternative syntax for specifying CSS logical operator matrices (alias:
10085 finLx=FILE; also finLz=FILE).
10086 ortho=0|1 Expert option (default: 1): 1, the dist_m4ri binary checks that the rows of H
10087 and G (finG, fin without finL, or Hx and Hz in each sector of a CSS code without
10088 Lx or Lz) are orthogonal, H G^T = 0, and stops with an error otherwise; 0 skips
10089 the check (a warning is printed), e.g., to screen many codes which are
10090 orthogonal by construction (the check takes O(nnz(G) times the column weight
10091 of H) operations). The result is valid only if H G^T = 0. The cache key does
10092 not depend on it. No effect without G (a warning).
10093 pmin=PROB Minimum error probability threshold for DEM parsing (default: 0.0).
10094 Error mechanisms with probability < pmin are filtered out. The column
10095 indices (start, finC, outC) count only the error mechanisms kept: with
10096 another pmin, the columns (and the codewords) change.
10097 merge=0|1 Merge the equal columns of the DEM (error mechanisms with the same detectors
10098 and observables) in the dist_m4ri binary (default: 1). Exact: dropping two
10099 equal columns of a codeword gives a lighter one, so the distance does not
10100 change (nor does the cache key). Column indices (finC, outC, start) are those
10101 of the DEM; the codewords found use the first one of each set of equal columns
10102 (use merge=0 to enumerate the codewords with each of them, or expand=1 to
10103 expand the list found).
10104 drop=auto|0|css|FILE The detectors which the binary drops from the DEM if this is verified to be
10105 exact (default: auto; drop=1 is the same as drop=auto; drop=0 keeps all
10106 detectors). Exact if every error touching them has a twin, an error with the
10107 same other detectors which touches none of them (or none if it has no other
10108 detector), with the same observables (or with L + A H for one matrix A):
10109 then the distance of the DEM is found from the smaller DEM without these
10110 detectors and the errors touching them, and the codewords found (outC) are
10111 codewords of the DEM which use only errors touching no dropped detector;
10112 finC codewords and CC start columns (see start) are mapped to the twins.
10113 drop=auto: the binary searches for the largest such set (with the same
10114 observables) in the DEM alone, e.g., the minority-basis detectors of a CSS
10115 circuit with the usual noise (see the README). drop=css: for a Stim circuit
10116 classified as CSS (including locally rotated CSS such as XZZX codes, by
10117 ancilla and data basis tracking), its minority-basis detectors (the basis
10118 other than the memory basis, see basis); otherwise (e.g., for a DEM),
10119 drop=auto is used, with a warning. drop=FILE: the detectors in FILE, for any
10120 DEM (a text file with the 0-based detector indices, k for Dk, separated by
10121 white space or commas; lines starting with '#' or '%' are comments; e.g.,
10122 written by outD). With css or FILE, if dropping the detectors is not exact, a
10123 note is printed and the full DEM is used. The values 0, 1, auto, and css take
10124 precedence over files with these names (write ./1 for a file named 1).
10125 outD=FILE Write the detectors dropped from the DEM by the binary to FILE (0-based, in
10126 the format of a drop file; only the comment line '# 0 of M detectors
10127 dropped ...' if none). With a cached result, the binary is run only for
10128 this (with dmin = dmax: no search).
10129 --out-reduced [PREFIX]
10130 Save the DEM without the detectors dropped (see drop and outD) to
10131 PREFIX_red.dem: the errors touching none of them (after the cutoff pmin, in
10132 the order of the flattened DEM), with the other detectors numbered
10133 consecutively. Its maps to the DEM go to PREFIX_red.json: "detectors" (the
10134 original index of each detector of the reduced DEM, i.e., those not in
10135 outD), "errors" (the original index of each error, as the columns of outC),
10136 "dropped", "num_detectors", "num_errors", "pmin", "source", "dem", "drop",
10137 and "__version__" (also out_reduced=PREFIX; default PREFIX: the basename of
10138 the input file, without _full or _simp; a PREFIX without a directory goes,
10139 like the default, to --out-dir or the directory of the input file: write
10140 ./PREFIX for the current directory). The reduced DEM has the same distance,
10141 and its codewords are mapped to codewords of the DEM by "errors".
10142 dem_rounds=N The rounds T of the DEM, passed to the binary as dem_rounds=N (default:
10143 automatic: for a Stim circuit its rounds, the largest number of measurements
10144 of one qubit, e.g., 1 with --rounds 0 for a circuit with one round before its
10145 REPEAT block; 0, unknown, for a .dem file): 1 adds the row slabs of rw_opt 4 to
10146 the automatic rw_opt of the binary (the boundary slabs are the two detector
10147 layers of the round); 2 or more: no automatic row slabs; 0: the binary
10148 decides (a DEM without round structure and with at most 640 detectors, see
10149 win_hyb). The distance and the cache do not depend on it.
10150 classical=0|1 Code type override:
10151 1: Classical linear code (finH only; ignored with a warning if finG, finL,
10152 fin, fdem, or Hz is given, or Lx or Lz with Hx; Lx / Lz without Hx and Hz
10153 are ignored with a warning).
10154 0: Quantum CSS code (requires logicals or Hz).
10155 Default: auto-detected (1 if only finH is given; 0 otherwise).
10156 css=N Disabled in the Python interface (CSS codes only; reserved in the binary for
10157 future non-CSS quantum code support): accepted for compatibility with the
10158 binary, and ignored with a warning to stderr.
10159 --simple / --full Disabled since version 0.13.0 (alias: --simplified; also simple=1, full=1):
10160 accepted for backward compatibility, but ignored with a warning to stderr. The
10161 DEM of a Stim circuit always has all detectors: the binary drops detectors if
10162 this is exact (see drop; e.g., the minority-basis detectors which --simple
10163 stripped), which is as fast and gives the distance of the full DEM (the
10164 stripped DEM only gives a lower bound when dropping them is not exact).
10165 basis=X|Z Explicitly set primary memory basis ('X' or 'Z') for .stim circuits
10166 (default: auto-detected from filename or initial/final resets/measurements);
10167 with drop=css, the detectors of the other basis are dropped if this is exact
10168 (otherwise only used for the --verbose report; ignored with a warning).
10169 --rounds [N] Construct DEM from a .stim circuit with N repetitions in its REPEAT block
10170 (default: 2 when --rounds is given without a number; 0 omits REPEAT blocks;
10171 also rounds=N). Issues a warning and continues with the original circuit if
10172 it has no REPEAT block; an error if the input is not a .stim circuit.
10173 --out-dir DIR Output directory for saving constructed DEM and/or processed Stim circuit
10174 files (also out_dir=DIR; default: directory of the input .stim/.dem file):
10175 the default names, and a FILE (or PREFIX) without a directory, of --out-dem,
10176 --out-stim, and --out-reduced go there (write ./FILE for the current
10177 directory).
10178 --out-dem [FILE] Save constructed (flattened) DEM to FILE (without a directory: in --out-dir,
10179 see there). If given without a filename (or out_dem=1), automatically saves
10180 as <basename>_full.dem.
10181 The codewords (outC) index its error lines: save the DEM in the same run (a DEM
10182 generated again from the circuit may differ, e.g., with another stim version).
10183 --out-stim [FILE] Save processed (noisy, rounds-adjusted) Stim circuit to FILE (without a
10184 directory: in --out-dir, see there). If given without a filename (or
10185 out_stim=1), automatically saves as <basename>_full.stim.
10186 --p-noise P Strength p of the uniform circuit-level noise added to a noiseless Stim circuit
10187 (also p_noise=P; default: 0.001; 0: no noise is added, and then a noiseless
10188 circuit gives no distance): DEPOLARIZE2(p) after two-qubit gates (CX, CZ,
10189 XCY, SWAP, ISWAP, SQRT_XX, CXSWAP, ..., also II), DEPOLARIZE1(p/10) after
10190 one-qubit gates (I, X, H, H_XY, S, SQRT_X, C_XYZ, ...), on the qubit of a
10191 classically controlled gate (e.g., CX rec[-1] 5), and on the qubits idle since
10192 the previous TICK, and X (Z) flips with probability p after Z-basis or Y-basis
10193 (X-basis) resets and before measurements (before and after MR, MRX, MRY); the
10194 multi-qubit measurements (MPP, MXX, MYY, MZZ) and Pauli product gates (SPP,
10195 SPP_DAG) get no noise. A circuit with noise (a noise channel, or a noisy
10196 measurement such as M(0.001)) is used as is, unless --force-noise. The
10197 distance does not depend on p (unless pmin > 0), only on which faults exist.
10198 --force-noise Replace the noise of a Stim circuit (also --force or force_noise=1): all of its
10199 noise is removed (noise channels, measurement flip probabilities, heralded
10200 noise; see stim's Circuit.without_noise()), and then the uniform noise of
10201 --p-noise is added (none with --p-noise 0, e.g., to save the noiseless circuit
10202 with --out-stim), e.g., to compare circuits with the same noise model.
10203 --model-lb Certified lower bound on the distance of a Stim memory circuit or DEM
10204 (fdem=FILE.stim or fdem=FILE.dem) from its code-sized model, instead of the
10205 distance of its DEM (also model_lb=1; see compute_model_lower_bound()): the
10206 detectors linked across rounds (in a circuit, by shared measurements other
10207 than the final data measurements; in a standalone DEM, by spatial detector
10208 coordinates, or else by dominant weight-2 observable-free error mechanisms)
10209 form chains, and each chain gives a row of the model, the sum of its detector
10210 rows (in a memory circuit, the chain of a check of the measured basis
10211 telescopes to the parity of the final data measurements on the check; the
10212 chains without a final data measurement, e.g., minority-basis checks, only
10213 with --model-minority), with the equal columns merged. Each codeword of the
10214 DEM gives a model codeword of no larger weight, so the model distance
10215 certified by CC is a lower bound on the DEM distance; it ignores the timing
10216 within the rounds (not tight in general, e.g., 5 for the bb_72 circuit of
10217 distance 6). The binary runs on the model with the measured-basis rows, then
10218 (with --model-minority) with all rows from that bound (RW first; method,
10219 threads, timeout, steps, dstop, wmax, seed, debug, nothrottle, pairs,
10220 sort_rows, cc_prune, and rw_opt apply to each run). The bound is stored as
10221 dmin in the cache record of the DEM, and the bounds of the DEM are printed.
10222 --model-minority With --model-lb, also the chains of the minority-basis checks are rows of the
10223 model (also model_minority=1; default: off). With depolarizing-type noise,
10224 they do not raise the bound (a lightest model codeword has a version without
10225 components of the other basis), but they may for other noise models.
10226 --out-model PREFIX With --model-lb, write the model to PREFIX_HR.mtx and PREFIX_LR.mtx (also
10227 out_model=PREFIX).
10228 (positional files) A file name without a key (the file must exist): a .dem or .stim file is used
10229 as fdem=FILE, and a .mtx or .mmx file as finH=FILE, or as finG=FILE if finH is
10230 already given (and neither finG nor finL); other files are ignored.
10231 (conflicting inputs) The input is selected in the order fdem, Hx/Hz (CSS code), and
10232 finH/finG/finL/fin (fin only supplies the missing finH and finG, while the
10233 binary ignores fin followed by finH, finG, or finL, and fin after them is an
10234 error); the ignored inputs (e.g., matrices with fdem, pmin, merge, expand,
10235 drop, or outD without fdem, basis, --p-noise, or --force-noise without a Stim
10236 circuit (--rounds without one is an error), basis without drop=css, fin with
10237 finH, classical=1 with finG, ortho=0 without G) give a warning (unless
10238 --silent).
10239
10240Calculation method:
10241 method=1|2|3 Calculation method (default: 3; alias: m=1|2|3):
10242 1: Random Window (RW) algorithm (upper bound on distance).
10243 Repeatedly samples random information sets to find low-weight
10244 codewords. Fast for discovering small errors.
10245 2: Connected Cluster (CC) algorithm (lower bound / exact distance).
10246 Exhaustive cluster search finding certified lower bound dmin or
10247 exact distance if run to completion.
10248 3: Bracketing mode (concurrent RW and CC).
10249 Dynamically allocates worker threads between CC (lower bound) and
10250 RW (upper bound) to converge on the exact distance rapidly, based on
10251 the measured CC and RW times, the bounds, and the remaining timeout.
10252
10253Distance bounds and guidance:
10254 dmin=N Known certified lower bound on distance (default: 0).
10255 CC search begins at weight w = max(1, dmin). In the output 'dmin dmax
10256 rw_steps', dmin - 1 is the largest weight w certified to have no codeword
10257 of weight <= w (0: none above 1; odd weights are skipped if all codewords
10258 have even weight; when exact, dmin = dmax = d, including d = 1). An input
10259 without logical codewords (k = 0) gives 0 0 0 with every engine, with one
10260 note on stderr (not with --silent), not cached (since version 0.17.2).
10261 dmax=N Known upper bound on distance (default: 0).
10262 CC ends once dmin = dmax (with outC, after the rounds w = dmax..dmax+dW);
10263 RW ignores candidate codewords of weight >= dmax unless collecting codewords
10264 or needed for min_hits. For a CSS code (Hx=, Hz=), dmax is a bound on
10265 d = min(dX, dZ), not on either sector: it is used as dstop for both sectors.
10266 dstop=N Stop target for the lower bound (default: 0 = off): the search (method=2
10267 or 3) ends once CC has certified dmin >= dstop, unless a lighter codeword is
10268 found. Unlike dmax, dstop is not an upper bound and is not reported as dmax
10269 (the bounds are 'dmin w steps' with dmin >= dstop, w: the lightest codeword
10270 found, or 0); a cached lower bound dmin >= dstop answers the request without
10271 a calculation. E.g., dstop=U wmin=U-1 decides whether d >= U.
10272 dexp=N Expected code distance estimate (alias: dest) (default: 0).
10273 Hint for method=3: as long as RW has found no codeword, CC rounds at
10274 w > dexp run only on threads which cannot run RW (CC pauses if RW can
10275 use all threads); CC resumes once RW finds a codeword or ends.
10276
10277Search limits and stopping criteria:
10278 steps=N Maximum number of RW steps / information sets across all threads
10279 (default: 100000; alias: nsteps=N; also num_steps=N).
10280 wmax=N Maximum cluster weight to analyze in CC (default: 0 = until a codeword is
10281 found, the bounds meet, dmin >= dstop, or the timeout; method=2 then needs
10282 timeout>0, dmax>0, or dstop>0; with outC and dW > 0, the CC rounds continue
10283 to the weight dmax + dW; up to the weight 99 at most, which is the largest
10284 wmax).
10285 wmin=N Minimum distance threshold (default: 1).
10286 If a codeword of weight w <= wmin is discovered, search halts immediately
10287 (not when collecting codewords with outC or maxC).
10288 timeout=SEC Execution timeout in seconds (default: 60.0; 0 or inf: no timeout; a
10289 trailing 's' is accepted, e.g., timeout=10s; alias: time=SEC).
10290 In method=3, it guides the CC vs RW thread balance, and a CC round predicted
10291 not to finish in time is not started while RW runs (in method=2, and with
10292 steps=0, it is started anyway: it may still find a codeword of weight dmin).
10293
10294Multithreading & throttling:
10295 threads=N Maximum number of worker threads to allocate (default: all logical CPUs
10296 available to the process, i.e., its CPU affinity mask, e.g., with taskset;
10297 alias: num_threads=N; also t=N).
10298 Subject to automatic thread throttling unless nothrottle=1 is specified:
10299 - Small codes, methods 1 and 3 (<= 4 threads for n < 60, or for m*n < 2e4
10300 with a small RW workload m*n*steps < 5e7; otherwise <= 16 threads for
10301 n < 150 or m*n < 1e5, if m*n*steps < 2e8; m: number of rows of H).
10302 Method 2 starts 4 threads, and the others once a CC round takes longer
10303 (predicted > 2 ms on the threads started, or running for 5 ms).
10304 - Large memory matrices (above 15 MB of dense RW working memory per thread:
10305 at most 32 RW threads, within a quarter of the physical memory).
10306 - Small RW step counts (RW threads clamped to <= (steps + 9) / 10).
10307 The last two limits apply to RW threads only: CC (method=2) is not
10308 limited, and in method=3 CC rounds can use all threads.
10309 CC rounds with few start columns per thread are split into work units
10310 which also fix the first 1-3 cluster extensions (balanced load).
10311 nothrottle=1 Disable automatic thread throttling (also --no-throttle).
10312 Forces allocation of the exact number of threads requested.
10313 chunk_size=N Maximum RW batch claimed at once by a thread (default: 0 = adaptive
10314 25-500). Near the end of the steps, batches shrink to at most
10315 ceil(remaining / (4 * RW threads)) steps. Alias: batch=N (also chunk=N).
10316 In method=3, adaptive batches take at most about 0.5 s of RW steps, and
10317 while RW steps remain to be claimed, an RW thread leaves its batch between
10318 two steps for a CC round which needs more threads (the rest of the batch
10319 runs after the round).
10320 ksub=N EXPERIMENTAL, should not be used (a warning is printed): subspace sketch
10321 dimension for RW (default: 0 = full matrix).
10322 Precomputes N = ker(H) once; each thread echelonizes a compact
10323 ksub x n sampled subspace in L1/L2 cache (e.g. ksub=32 or 64).
10324 Automatically falls back to ksub=0 if m < nu = dim(ker H) (a warning is
10325 printed with --verbose or debug&1). Each step reduces the span of ksub
10326 distinct rows of N, so that a few codewords are found much more often than
10327 others, and min_hits may end RW early.
10328 kwin=N Localized column permutation window size W around a random seed
10329 column j0, used in every RW step (alias: win=N). Default: 0 = automatic
10330 hybrid for n>=500: every other step uses an index window (win_mode=1) of
10331 win_hyb columns, and the other steps uniform random permutations (also
10332 for codewords which are not local in the column order); with a nonzero
10333 resolved rw_opt (the run plan), used only for a DEM (matrices use uniform
10334 permutations unless the resolved rw_opt is 0 or win_hyb > 0), and with the
10335 row slabs of rw_opt 4 (e.g., automatic for a single round), a slab instead.
10336 kwin=-1 (any negative value): no windows, uniform random permutations in
10337 every step.
10338 win_mode=0|1 Locality metric for kwin > 0: 0 = Tanner graph BFS neighbors
10339 (default), 1 = contiguous column index window.
10340 win_hyb=N Window size of the hybrid RW steps (kwin=0, n>=500; at most 3n/4).
10341 Default: 0 = 256 columns for a DEM, 512 for matrices with rw_opt=0 or
10342 resolved rw_opt=0x0 (when the resolved rw_opt is not 0, matrices use uniform
10343 permutations unless win_hyb > 0 or kwin > 0). The window columns come first
10344 in the elimination order; in a DEM, they are errors close in time, which
10345 touch few detectors: windows of 192-256 columns find circuit codewords 2-10
10346 times faster than 512, and windows of one round of columns much slower. With
10347 --verbose (or debug&1), the binary prints the rounds of a DEM (estimated
10348 from the time translation of its errors by D detectors, 2 <= D <= m/3, i.e.,
10349 at least three detector layers: D detectors and L columns per round; a
10350 single round, a folded schedule, whose rounds alternate between two forms,
10351 or detectors not in time order give no round structure, which the automatic
10352 row slabs of rw_opt 4 use, see dem_rounds) and the codewords found by the
10353 uniform steps, by the window steps, and by the row slabs (line '# RW step
10354 types': the codewords in hash, i.e., without outC, --cws, and maxC at most
10355 cov_cws of the minimum weight, the first found; 'both': found by the uniform
10356 and by the other steps).
10357 pairs=N RW pairs of non-pivot columns (p=2, as in Lee-Brickell and Stern): a RW
10358 step also finds the codewords with exactly two non-pivot columns,
10359 checking only the pairs of columns which agree on N random pivot rows
10360 (at most 64; 0 = off). Default: -1 = auto, about one non-pivot column per
10361 bucket, with fewer rows while a codeword of the weight of the upper bound
10362 would be kept with probability below 0.8, but enough rows to keep the
10363 pairs of a step within about the work of its elimination (e.g., at least
10364 6 for large circuit DEMs while the upper bound is far above the
10365 distance). The pairs find the minimum-weight codewords of circuit DEMs
10366 7-26 times faster, and lighter codewords of codes with a large distance.
10367 Not with ksub. With --verbose (or debug&1), the binary prints the pairs
10368 checked per step and the codewords found by pairs and by single columns.
10369 rw_opt=N Expert option (since version 0.17.0; also --rw-opt N): RW stages with the
10370 weight-3 degeneracies T3 (triplets of columns with zero syndromes of H and L)
10371 and the known generators (doc/rw_triplet_degeneracies.tex). Default: -1 =
10372 automatic (the stages below which apply to the input; none for classical
10373 codes); 0: all off (the RW of version 0.16.1, e.g., for comparisons); or the
10374 sum of the stages to use (1 to 63, decimal or 0x...):
10375 1: enumerate T3 (after merge and drop) and contract the candidates (2 -> 1,
10376 3 -> 0 columns): the single-column candidates up to the weight
10377 min(dmax+8, 64), the pairs up to min(dmax+1, 64) (+dW when collecting); in
10378 the pairs, skip the columns whose circuit (the column and its pivot
10379 columns) has a zero L syndrome and at most 3 columns (the Stern filter:
10380 loss-free for the distance, i.e., the minimum weight, with the
10381 contraction, hence only while dmax+8 <= 64, +dW when collecting; when
10382 collecting codewords with --cws, outC, or maxC, only with 32: 32 restores
10383 the codewords the filter removes through 2 <-> 2 exchanges, 1 -> 2 splits,
10384 and 1 <-> 1 swaps of identical columns, e.g., in finH/finL exported from a
10385 DEM without merging, or with merge=0); a zero column of H with a nonzero
10386 column of L gives d=1 at once
10387 (automatic: quantum codes, steps > 2);
10388 2: with G (finG, fin, or Hx/Hz without Lx/Lz), shorten the candidates by the
10389 rows of G (steepest descent, before the contraction of 1; the
10390 single-column candidates up to min(dmax+w_G-2, 64), with 1 up to
10391 min(dmax+max(8, w_G-2), 64)) and skip the columns whose circuits are rows
10392 of G in the pairs (only while that weight is at most 64; not when
10393 collecting; automatic: off);
10394 4: row-slab windows of a DEM in time order (kwin=0, not with sort_rows=1):
10395 every other step (the others use uniform random permutations), the
10396 columns inside the first or the last m/2 detectors, i.e., the two detector
10397 layers of a single round, a random independent set of the triplet graph
10398 first (automatic: a DEM with a single round, dem_rounds=1, e.g., from a
10399 Stim circuit with one round, or without round structure, see win_hyb, and
10400 with at most 640 detectors: the slabs find the codewords confined to one
10401 layer, e.g., weight 16 of the double-gross DEM with one round, which the
10402 other steps hardly find; not on deep circuit DEMs, where the index windows
10403 with 1 found more minimum-weight codewords per second; the slabs find the
10404 same codewords over and over, and min_hits does not count their hits);
10405 8: sparse-dual elimination: an m x m inverse instead of the m x n matrix (the
10406 same information sets, less memory per RW thread; quantum inputs with up to
10407 64 rows of L; automatic: m x n above 512 KiB, and n >= 20 m or m >= 1400;
10408 no '# RW FKG score');
10409 16: canonical classes: the codewords of the minimum weight found in the
10410 uniform RW steps are counted by their canonical form (2 <-> 2 exchanges
10411 across two triplets with a common column, or half-overlap exchanges with
10412 the even rows of G), each at most once per step, and min_hits stops RW by
10413 the Good-Turing / Chao2 rule (see min_hits; only with min_hits > 0, not
10414 with kwin > 0; automatic: quantum codes); the tables hold up to 2^24
10415 classes and codewords (up to about 640 MiB; then the rule of <n> is used);
10416 the codewords of a RW step are recorded at its end (lighter ones at once),
10417 each at most once (with an active 1 or 2 as well);
10418 32: when collecting codewords (--cws, outC, or maxC), add the codewords
10419 obtained from the codewords found by T3 before the export: 2 <-> 2
10420 exchanges and 1 -> 2 splits, up to the weight min_w+dW; and by 1 <-> 1
10421 swaps of the identical columns of H and L, also without T3 (see 1, irred,
10422 and maxC; automatic: quantum codes when collecting: --cws, outC, or maxC).
10423 When the resolved rw_opt is not 0 (see the run plan), matrices (finH, Hx/Hz)
10424 use uniform random permutations in all RW steps unless kwin > 0 or
10425 win_hyb > 0 (the hybrid windows are for DEMs, see kwin); an automatic rw_opt
10426 which resolves to 0 (rw_opt=0x0 in the run plan, e.g., for a classical code)
10427 keeps the hybrid windows of rw_opt=0. Only with full-matrix RW (ksub=0) and
10428 steps > 0 (automatic: steps > 2). The distance is valid with any rw_opt, and
10429 the cache key does not depend on it. With --verbose (or debug&1), the binary
10430 prints the stages used and their statistics (lines '# RW triplets',
10431 '# RW canonical', and '# RW FKG score': the mean Harris-FKG bound
10432 -sum ln(1 + |S_a|) on ln Pr(J) of the dense full-matrix steps with pairs, with
10433 any stage but not with 8 or on the slab steps, and -ln C(n, r)).
10434 min_hits=N QDistRnd-style RW stopping criterion (default: 5, 0 = off; alias: max_hits).
10435 Stops RW when the average number of hits <n> per codeword (over the
10436 codewords hit) reaches min_hits, both for the codewords of the minimum weight
10437 found and for a representative set of cov_cws lowest-weight codewords
10438 (heavier codewords are kept until enough lighter ones are found). A single
10439 codeword suffices. The hits counted: with a resolved rw_opt of 0 (rw_opt=0,
10440 or e.g. a classical code), all, as in version 0.16.1; otherwise (see the run
10441 plan) those of the uniform RW steps, of CC, of finC, and of the windows of
10442 kwin > 0 (then no step is uniform), but not those of the row slabs of rw_opt
10443 4 and of the hybrid index windows (kwin=0), which find the same codewords over
10444 and over (they are shown apart, see '# RW step types'). While no codeword
10445 of the minimum weight has a counted hit, the min_hits stop is inactive (the
10446 status line and the summary say so). A lighter codeword is missed with
10447 probability about exp(-<n>), assuming that lighter codewords are found at
10448 least as often. With debug&1 (or --verbose), a warning is printed at the end
10449 if the hit counts of codewords of the same weight are strongly non-uniform
10450 (then exp(-<n>) is optimistic), together with an information-set estimate
10451 (uniform random information sets) of the probability to miss a lighter
10452 codeword and of the RW steps needed for 1%.
10453 With --verbose, the active stopping rule and the baseline information-set
10454 estimate are shown for a result which is not certified. With min_hits=0, RW
10455 records only the codewords lighter than the upper bound (unless collecting
10456 codewords with outC, maxC, or --cws), so that the repeated hits are not
10457 counted.
10458 With the canonical classes of rw_opt (16, automatic for quantum codes with
10459 min_hits > 0 and kwin <= 0), RW stops instead once the canonical classes of
10460 the minimum weight found in the uniform steps (C of them, Q1 and Q2 found in
10461 exactly one and two steps, N step incidences in total) give
10462 N >= max(15, 3 min_hits), N/C >= min_hits, the Good-Turing unseen mass
10463 Q1/N <= min(0.02, 3 exp(-min_hits)), and the Chao2 unseen fraction
10464 C0/(C+C0) <= 0.05 with C0 = Q1(Q1-1)/(2(Q2+1)). Only the uniform steps
10465 count: while none of them has found a codeword of the minimum weight (e.g.,
10466 on deep circuit DEMs, where the window steps find them), the min_hits stop is
10467 inactive and RW runs until the steps or the timeout end (the status line and
10468 the summary say so; the window steps are shown for information only, see
10469 '# RW step types'). Without 16, <n> above.
10470 cov_cws=N Size of the representative set of lowest-weight codewords for min_hits
10471 (default: 100; 0 = only the minimum weight). Without outC and maxC, at
10472 most cov_cws minimum-weight codewords are tracked (all if cov_cws=0).
10473 With fewer minimum-weight codewords, a smaller cov_cws may stop RW
10474 earlier.
10475 refresh=N Periodic adaptive basis refresh interval in RW steps, only with the
10476 experimental ksub > 0 (default: 0; 5000 with ksub > 0).
10477 Re-echelonizes N and replaces one heavier basis row by a discovered
10478 minimum-weight codeword.
10479
10480Connected Cluster (CC) search options:
10481 smax=N Maximum syndrome weight for confinement profile (default: 0).
10482 When smax > 0, tracks minimum syndrome weights for each error weight.
10483 When smax=0, confinement is not computed. The binary disables it if
10484 dmin > 1 (including a lower bound from the cache), as the small cluster
10485 weights are then skipped.
10486 sort_rows=0|1 Sort the rows of H by increasing weight (stable) in the dist_m4ri binary
10487 (default: the binary's, 1 for matrices and 0 for a DEM). With cc_prune=0,
10488 CC extends a cluster by the columns of the first row of its syndrome (in
10489 row order), so that light rows first reduce the CC work for matrices with
10490 very different row weights (e.g., 1.7-4x with the hook columns of an
10491 extended CSS distance), while the detectors of a DEM are in time order,
10492 which is better (use sort_rows=0 for matrices exported from a DEM as well).
10493 With cc_prune=1 or 2, the order of the rows only breaks ties. The
10494 distance, RW, and the cache key do not depend on the order of the rows; CC
10495 enumerates the same codewords (outC), possibly in another order (with
10496 cc_prune=0, with other hit counts as well).
10497 cc_prune=0|1|2 The CC search of the dist_m4ri binary (with smax=0; default: the binary's,
10498 1; also --cc-prune N). 0: the walk of the versions before 0.15.0, which
10499 extends a cluster by the columns of the first unsatisfied row of its
10500 syndrome. 1: the branch and bound: it branches on the unsatisfied row
10501 with the fewest available columns, the columns of the earlier branches are
10502 forbidden in the later ones (each codeword is found once: one CC hit), and
10503 a branch is pruned by lower bounds on the number of columns needed (an
10504 unsatisfied row without available columns, or a packing of unsatisfied
10505 rows with disjoint sets of available columns). 2: adds the coverage and
10506 fractional cover bounds (fewer nodes, more work per node). All values
10507 find the same codewords and distances (doc/cc_completeness.tex); with the
10508 expert start list (and start_scan=0), cc_prune=1 and 2 forbid the columns
10509 listed before the start column. The cache key does not depend on it.
10510 start=LIST Expert option: comma-separated list of CC start columns (0-based), e.g.,
10511 start=0,48,96 (default: -1 = all columns; start=N is a one-element list).
10512 CC clusters are grown only from the listed columns, and they are NOT
10513 limited to larger column indices. Use, e.g., one column per block of a
10514 quasi-cyclic code. WARNING: dmin (and an exact result) is valid only if a
10515 code symmetry maps every minimum-weight codeword to one containing a listed
10516 column; dmax is always valid. For DEM input, columns index the error
10517 mechanisms in their order in the (flattened) DEM, after the pmin cutoff; with
10518 drop, a listed column touching a dropped detector is replaced by its twin (or
10519 removed if it has none, see drop).
10520 Results are cached under a separate key '<key>:start=a,b,c'; only dmax and
10521 codewords are merged into the main cache record. (Before version 0.10.0,
10522 start=N limited CC to clusters started at column N using only larger
10523 columns; this is now cbeg=N cend=N of the dist_m4ri binary.)
10524 start_scan=0|1 Expert option, with start (also --start-scan; default: 0): 1: a cluster grown
10525 from a listed column c only uses the columns > c, as in the scan of all
10526 columns. WARNING: dmin is then valid only if a code symmetry maps every
10527 minimum-weight codeword to one whose smallest column is listed, e.g., if
10528 the listed columns are the smallest columns of the orbits of a group of code
10529 automorphisms, one per orbit (start=0,l for the two blocks of a two-block
10530 group-algebra code of length 2l over an abelian group). The later start
10531 columns then need much less work, the least if each orbit is a range of
10532 consecutive columns. Cached under '<key>:start=a,b,c:scan'. Not for a DEM.
10533 --trust-start Expert option (also trust_start=1): accept the start-list results as valid,
10534 i.e., merge dmin and rw_steps into the main cache record as well, and copy an
10535 existing exact start-list record to the main record even if no calculation
10536 is needed. Only use it if the code symmetry assumption above holds.
10537 noscan, cbeg, cend Disabled in the Python interface: accepted for backward compatibility, but
10538 ignored with a warning to stderr. These expert options of the dist_m4ri
10539 binary do not give valid bounds on their own: noscan=1 runs CC only at
10540 weight w=wmax (method=2); cbeg/cend limit CC start columns to a range for
10541 split runs, where every column is eventually covered by one of the runs.
10542 Run the dist_m4ri binary directly to use them (see its --morehelp).
10543
10544Study options of the dist_m4ri binary (the statistics of the RW step types, e.g., the row slabs):
10545 steplog=FILE, slab_rows=N, slab_bnd=N, slab_var=N, slab_every=N
10546 Disabled in the Python interface: the study options of the dist_m4ri binary
10547 (steplog=FILE: a log of the RW steps and of the codewords found in them; the
10548 height, the boundary probability, the height variation, and the step period
10549 of the row slabs of rw_opt 4) are accepted, but ignored with a warning to
10550 stderr: a run of dist_m4ri.py may run the binary several times (e.g., two
10551 CSS sectors, or the stages of engine='auto'), or not at all (a cached
10552 result). Run the dist_m4ri binary directly to use them (see its --morehelp
10553 study).
10554
10555Machine-readable output options of the dist_m4ri binary (since version 0.17.4):
10556 stamp=0|1, json=0|1|FILE
10557 Disabled in the Python interface: the machine-readable output options of
10558 the dist_m4ri binary (stamp=1: elapsed search-time stamps [t=S.SSSs] on
10559 progress and stop lines; json=1|FILE: a single-line JSON summary, schema
10560 dm4ri-result/1) are accepted by the CLI, but ignored with a warning to
10561 stderr: a run of dist_m4ri.py may run the binary several times (e.g., two
10562 CSS sectors, or the stages of engine='auto'), or not at all (a cached
10563 result). Run the dist_m4ri binary directly (see its --morehelp output),
10564 or pass stamp=True / json_out=True|FILE to run_dist_m4ri() in Python.
10565
10566Codeword collection and export:
10567 --cws Collect non-trivial minimum-weight codewords (up to min_w + dW) into the
10568 cache record (also --do_cws, cws=0|1, do_cws=0|1). Does not print them to
10569 stdout; use outC=FILE to write them to a file. Uses the native binary with
10570 engine=auto (an error with engine=cert or codedistance).
10571 outC=FILE Export found codewords of weight up to min_w + dW (min_w: minimum weight
10572 found) to file in .nz format. In method=2/3, once the distance d is
10573 known, CC rounds w = d..d+dW enumerate all such irreducible codewords
10574 (see irred; unless the timeout is hit; for a DEM, up to the choice of
10575 equal columns: see merge).
10576 In CSS mode, automatically saves X-codewords to FILE_X.nz and
10577 Z-codewords to FILE_Z.nz. The codewords of the run are merged with the
10578 cached ones; with finC=FILE (the same file), those already in FILE are kept
10579 (including reducible ones recorded before version 0.14.8).
10580 finC=FILE Import initial candidate codewords from file in .nz format.
10581 In CSS mode (Hx=, Hz=), each sector reads its own file FILE_X.nz or FILE_Z.nz
10582 if at least one of them exists and is not empty (a sector without its file
10583 gets no input codewords); otherwise, FILE itself is given to both sectors
10584 (the binary skips the codewords which are not valid in a sector). If FILE
10585 is the same file as outC, a missing or empty file is ignored. The binary
10586 replaces a reducible codeword by an irreducible part (see irred). A column
10587 index below 1 is an error; codewords with a column beyond n, not orthogonal to
10588 H, or orthogonal to L are skipped (with a warning), and so are those heavier
10589 than wmax > 0 (with method=2 and wmax=0, heavier than 99). With drop (fdem),
10590 finC codewords are mapped to the twins.
10591 maxC=N Maximum number of codewords to collect (default: 0 = unlimited); with
10592 expand=1, bounds the size of the expanded list as well.
10593 dW=N Extra weight window above the minimum weight found to collect codewords
10594 (w <= min_w + dW; default: -1 = unset, i.e., 0 in the binary; any dW >= 0
10595 collects codewords and uses the native binary with engine=auto).
10596 irred=0|1 Disabled in the Python interface: irred=0, an expert option of the
10597 dist_m4ri binary, is ignored with a warning to stderr. Only irreducible
10598 codewords are recorded (irred=1, the default of the binary): a codeword
10599 which is the union of a codeword and a disjoint nonzero vector with zero
10600 syndrome (e.g., a trivial weight-3 vector of a circuit DEM, from weight
10601 d+3 on) is not. Minimum-weight codewords are always irreducible.
10602 expand=0|1 Python only, for a DEM: list each codeword found once for every choice
10603 among equal columns, which the binary merges (see merge; default: 0). The
10604 binary and the cache keep the merged list. With dW <= 1, the expanded list
10605 is that of merge=0 (with dW >= 2, merge=0 lists lighter codewords with two
10606 equal columns added as well). The list grows quickly with the weight: with
10607 maxC > 0, at most maxC codewords are written (a warning if some are dropped).
10608 (DEM codewords) The indices refer to the error lines of the DEM in the order of the flattened
10609 DEM, after the pmin cutoff. For a Stim circuit, save the DEM with --out-dem in
10610 the same run (a warning is printed otherwise): a DEM generated again from the
10611 circuit may differ (e.g., with another stim version).
10612
10613Distance caching (Python CLI):
10614 cache=FILE Path to persistent JSON cache file (default: tmp_dist_cache.json; alias:
10615 cache_file=FILE; 0 or none disables caching).
10616 --no-cache / nocache Disable reading and writing to the persistent JSON cache.
10617
10618General options:
10619 solver=NAME, engine=NAME
10620 Distance calculation engine (engine takes precedence over solver; ignored with
10621 a warning under --model-lb): 'dist_m4ri' (default; engine=native or off),
10622 'cert' ('qec_cert', 'qec-cert'), 'tropidist', 'auto', or 'codedistance'.
10623 'cert': runs qec_cert on distance-only requests (error if qec_cert or
10624 libqeccert.so is missing, or with codeword collection --cws or outC; outD,
10625 --out-reduced, finC, smax, dW, maxC, and start are ignored with a warning; with
10626 pmin > 0, certifies the DEM without errors of probability < pmin; method=1 runs
10627 its upper-bound mode 'ub'; '0 0 0' for an input without logical codewords,
10628 which qec_cert certifies as 'infeasible', as with every engine: see dmin).
10629 qec_cert gets wmin from a cached certified lower bound (dmin=N only tightens
10630 the returned bounds, not passed as wmin) and wmax from dmax-1, wmax, or
10631 dstop-1 (40 if none); only unconditional
10632 lower bounds (including those conditioned solely on that cached certified
10633 wmin) and upper bounds with a verified witness are cached.
10634 'tropidist': runs an external tropidist checkout ('python -m cdist', located
10635 via TROPIDIST_ROOT or cdist on PYTHONPATH) in a separate subprocess on
10636 distance-only requests (error if tropidist is not configured or with --cws /
10637 outC; outD, --out-reduced, finC, smax, dW, maxC, start, and method=1 are
10638 ignored with a warning; '0 0 0' when k = 0). For Stim circuits with pmin = 0,
10639 passes the .stim file directly so tropidist keeps its native circuit
10640 relaxations and noiseless Stim witness replay; for matrices (constructing L
10641 from H and G over GF(2) when G is given) and standalone DEMs (after pmin),
10642 passes --matrices H.mtx L.mtx and independently verifies every returned
10643 witness (H x = 0, L x != 0) before accepting or caching the upper bound
10644 (value_only DP bounds without a witness are not accepted as upper bounds).
10645 Search range kmin..kmax is clamped to 1..40, starting from a cached certified
10646 lower bound only; table_gb sets the lookup-table memory budget in GiB.
10647 'auto' (since version 0.17.0): two-stage portfolio for distance-only method=3
10648 runs on quantum codes, CSS sectors, DEMs, or Stim circuits (classical codes,
10649 method=1 or 2, codeword collection --cws/outC/dW>=0/maxC>0, finC, smax>0,
10650 start, outD, --out-reduced, and pmin>0 run the native dist_m4ri binary
10651 without importing qec_cert or spawning tropidist):
10652 - When qec_cert is available, a DEM or Stim circuit with > 25,000 raw error
10653 mechanisms (and timeout >= 3 s or 0) runs qec_cert first (exact DEM
10654 reductions before search); if qec_cert fails or ends early with an open
10655 bracket and > 1 s remains (or timeout=0), Stage C runs the native binary
10656 with the remaining time (no limit for timeout=0), seeded with the qec_cert
10657 bounds.
10658 - Otherwise, Stage A runs the native binary (method=3) for tau_1 = timeout if
10659 timeout <= 2 s, else min(max(2, timeout/10), 10) s, returning at once
10660 without importing qec_cert or spawning tropidist if exact, dmin >= dstop > 0,
10661 CC reached wmax > 0, timeout=0, or <= 1 s remains; Stage B then runs
10662 qec_cert (or tropidist when qec_cert is unavailable and tropidist is
10663 configured) with the remaining time, seeded with wmin = max(1, dmin_A) and
10664 wmax = dmax_A - 1 (Stage A's CC-certified dmin_A discharges
10665 lb_assumed_wmin <= dmin_A; qec_cert runs its randomized upper-bound stage
10666 use_ub=True when dmax_A <= 0 or dmax_A - max(1, dmin_A) >= 3, skipping it
10667 use_ub=False only for a narrow bracket 0 < dmax_A - max(1, dmin_A) < 3); if
10668 Stage B fails or ends early with an open bracket and > 1 s remains, Stage C
10669 runs the native binary with the remaining time from the tightened bounds.
10670 If neither qec_cert nor tropidist is available (warns once per process if
10671 qec_cert is installed without libqeccert.so), the native binary runs once
10672 with the whole timeout.
10673 With 'cert' and 'auto', a floor wmin > 1 (a certified lower bound) keeps the
10674 stabilizer dominance of the qec_cert search on for quantum codes and DEMs
10675 (force_dom=1 if this qec_cert has the option, since 0.17.4). Since 0.17.5, a
10676 qec_cert with the handoff parameters also gets dmax_init=<dmax> and, with
10677 'auto', the codeword of weight dmax_A found by Stage A (run with json=1),
10678 which qec_cert verifies (not for a Stim circuit); the floor stays wmin.
10679 'codedistance': runs the codedistance Python package (error if missing, or
10680 with --cws or outC; uses steps and seed, and ignores non-default dist_m4ri
10681 binary options with a warning). --verbose reports the engine='auto' stages.
10682 table_gb=N Lookup-table memory budget in GiB for engine='tropidist' (and engine='auto'
10683 when falling back to tropidist; also --table-gb N; 0: tropidist default,
10684 1 GiB or half RLIMIT_AS; ignored with a warning for other engines).
10685 --verbose / -v Enable verbose output with detailed explanations of bounds,
10686 timings, steps, and cache status (implies the debug bits 1, 2,
10687 65536, and 131072). For a RW upper bound which is not certified,
10688 reports the active stopping rule and miss-probability estimates
10689 (from <n> or canonical classes, and from uniform random information sets
10690 with n, rank(H), and the RW steps, with the steps and time for 1%).
10691 --silent / -q No warnings on stderr for the inputs which are ignored (e.g., matrices with
10692 fdem, the options of the binary with solver=codedistance, or the options
10693 not used with --model-lb; also the k = 0 note); the warnings for the
10694 disabled options (--simple, --full, noscan, cbeg, cend, irred=0, css=, the
10695 study options steplog and slab_*, and stamp, json) and on the validity of a
10696 result are still written (also --quiet, silent=0|1).
10697 In Python: set_silent().
10698 seed=N Random number generator seed (default: 0; the binary replaces seed<=0 by
10699 time(NULL) + 10*pid - 1000*seed).
10700 debug=N Debug bitmap (default: 0; alias: dbg), a decimal or hexadecimal (0x...)
10701 integer; multiple debug arguments are OR-combined. At debug=0, validity
10702 warnings, ignored/overridden parameter warnings, invalid finC warnings, and
10703 the smax > 0 confinement profile of the binary are still forwarded to stderr.
10704 Bits 1 to 32768 are passed to the dist_m4ri binary, which prints diagnostic
10705 output to stderr (see its --morehelp; lower bits are more informative):
10706 1: summary (input matrices, rounds of a DEM, RW windows, stop reason,
10707 codeword statistics, RW information sets, pairs, step types, and stages
10708 rw_opt),
10709 2: progress (run plan, finished CC rounds, new upper bounds, RW convergence),
10710 4: periodic status (after 1, 2, 4, ... s, then every 60 s: bounds, RW steps
10711 and rate, the min_hits statistic <n> or the canonical classes of rw_opt
10712 16, progress of the current CC round),
10713 8: thread allocation and timing, 16: code parameters (ranks, k),
10714 32: codeword supports, 64: arguments, 128: matrices,
10715 256: codeword dump, 2048: no size cutoff.
10716 Bits 65536 and above are used by the Python wrapper only:
10717 65536: dist_m4ri command lines and run times,
10718 131072: cache messages,
10719 262144: Stim circuit to DEM conversion details,
10720 524288: keep (and list) the temporary files.
10721
10722Option groups (--help GROUP prints all entries of GROUP):
10723 windows kwin, win_mode, win_hyb, rw_opt
10724 stopping, stop steps, wmin, timeout, min_hits, cov_cws
10725 bounds dmin, dmax, dstop, dexp, wmax
10726 dem fdem, pmin, merge, drop, outD, --out-reduced, expand, dem_rounds
10727 stim fdem, basis, --rounds, --out-dir, --out-dem, --out-stim, --p-noise,
10728 --force-noise, --model-lb, --model-minority, --out-model
10729 matrices, matrix finH, finG, finL, fin, Hx, Lx, classical, ortho
10730 codewords --cws, outC, finC, maxC, dW, irred, expand
10731 threading threads, nothrottle, chunk_size
10732 cache cache, --no-cache, --trust-start
10733 expert start, start_scan, --trust-start, noscan
10734 experimental ksub, refresh
10735 study steplog, slab_rows, slab_bnd, slab_var, slab_every
10736 output stamp, json
10737
10738Help options:
10739 -h, -?, --help [TOPIC]
10740 Display summary help message (fits 80 rows); with TOPIC, the same as
10741 --morehelp TOPIC (also --help=TOPIC).
10742 --morehelp [TOPIC] Display this full help message with all parameters, or only the entries of
10743 TOPIC, e.g., --morehelp maxC (also --morehelp=TOPIC; several topics separated
10744 by commas, e.g., maxC,dW; the names are case-insensitive, without '-' or '_'
10745 (and '=VALUE' in --help=TOPIC and --morehelp=TOPIC: a separate argument with
10746 '=' is not a TOPIC), and include aliases such as dest or batch; an unknown
10747 name gives the closest names on stderr, and the exit code 1). A group name
10748 (see Option groups, also as singular or plural, e.g., window) gives all
10749 entries of the group, and a parameter of a group also the other entries of
10750 its group (see also).
10751 --version Display the versions of dist_m4ri.py and of the dist_m4ri binary.
10752
10753Exit codes:
10754 exit codes 0: success; 1: an invalid value of an argument (also an unknown help topic);
10755 2 (since version 0.17.2; a traceback before): a package or library which is
10756 missing or not usable (e.g., qec_cert without libqeccert.so, tropidist without
10757 TROPIDIST_ROOT, stim), the binary not found or failed (its error message), or
10758 a file which cannot be read or written; 255: an unrecognized parameter, or no
10759 input. Errors are written to stderr on one line: 'Error: ...'.
10760"""
10761
10762
10763def _help_entries(text: str) -> List[Tuple[str, List[str], Dict[str, str]]]:
10764 """
10765 The entries of a help text (see _cli_morehelp_text()): (section header, the lines of the entry, its names). An
10766 entry starts with a line indented by 2 spaces (the names, then the description), and continues with the lines
10767 indented by more; a section header is a line without indentation ending with ':'. The names (a dict: normalized
10768 name -> name as written) are those in the first column (e.g., 'Hx=FILE, Hz=FILE' -> Hx, Hz; '--no-cache /
10769 nocache'), without the values (FILE, [N], ...; but all words of a note such as '(DEM codewords)'), and the aliases
10770 in the description ('alias: dest', 'Alias: win=N', 'also --no-throttle', 'also rounds=N'); normalized: lowercase,
10771 without '-' and '_'.
10772 """
10773 import re
10774 entries: List[Tuple[str, List[str], Dict[str, str]]] = []
10775 section = ""
10776 for line in text.splitlines():
10777 if line and not line[0].isspace() and line.rstrip().endswith(":"):
10778 section = line.rstrip()
10779 continue
10780 m = re.match(r"^ (\S.*?)(?:\s{2,}|$)", line)
10781 if m: # a new entry
10782 names: Dict[str, str] = {}
10783 for tok in re.split(r"[,/\s]+", m.group(1)):
10784 tok = tok.strip("()[]").split("=", 1)[0]
10785 # (not a value, e.g., FILE or N; all words of a note, e.g., '(DEM codewords)')
10786 if tok.strip("-") and (m.group(1).startswith("(") or not tok.isupper()):
10787 names.setdefault(_help_name_key(tok), tok)
10788 entries.append((section, [line], names))
10789 elif line.startswith(" ") and entries:
10790 entries[-1][1].append(line)
10791 for _, lines, names in entries:
10792 desc = " ".join(s.strip() for s in lines)
10793 for a in re.findall(r"(?i)\balias(?:es)?:\s*(-{0,2}[\w-]+)", desc) + re.findall(r"\balso (--?[\w-]+)", desc) + \
10794 re.findall(r"\balso ([\w-]+)=", desc):
10795 names.setdefault(_help_name_key(a), a)
10796 return entries
10797
10798
10799def _help_name_key(name: str) -> str:
10800 """A name of a help entry normalized for matching (see _help_entries()): lowercase, without '-' and '_'."""
10801 return name.lower().replace("-", "").replace("_", "")
10802
10803
10804def _help_group_members(entry: Tuple[str, List[str], Dict[str, str]]) -> Optional[Set[str]]:
10805 """
10806 The normalized names of the members of a group (an entry of the section 'Option groups' of the full help: the
10807 names listed after its first column), or None for another entry.
10808 """
10809 import re
10810 section, lines, _ = entry
10811 if not section.startswith("Option groups"):
10812 return None
10813 m = re.match(r"^ \S.*?(?:\s{2,}|$)", lines[0])
10814 text = " ".join([lines[0][m.end():] if m else ""] + [s.strip() for s in lines[1:]])
10815 return {_help_name_key(t) for t in re.split(r"[,\s]+", text) if t.strip("-")}
10816
10817
10818def _help_group_key_match(gkey: str, key: str) -> bool:
10819 """Whether the topic key matches the name gkey of a group, also as singular or plural (e.g., window, windows)."""
10820 return key in (gkey, gkey + "s") or (gkey.endswith("s") and key == gkey[:-1])
10821
10822
10823def print_cli_morehelp(file: Optional[Any] = None, topic: Optional[str] = None) -> int:
10824 """
10825 Prints the full help of the CLI (--morehelp), or with `topic` (one or more names separated by commas, see
10826 _help_entries()) only the entries of these parameters, in the order of the full help under their section headers.
10827 A topic may also be a group of the section 'Option groups' (also as singular or plural, e.g., window): then all
10828 its members are printed; and an entry of a group also gives the other members of its groups and these groups
10829 (one level: 'see also'). Returns 0, or 1 if some topic has no entry (then the closest names are suggested on
10830 stderr).
10831 """
10832 import difflib
10833 text = _cli_morehelp_text()
10834 keys = [(t, _help_name_key(t.split("=", 1)[0])) for t in (s.strip() for s in (topic or "").split(","))]
10835 keys = [(t, k) for t, k in keys if k]
10836 if not keys:
10837 print(text, file=file)
10838 return 0
10839 entries = _help_entries(text)
10840 members = [_help_group_members(e) for e in entries]
10841 status = 0
10842 asked: Set[int] = set()
10843 for t, key in keys:
10844 found = [i for i, e in enumerate(entries)
10845 if (key in e[2] if members[i] is None else any(_help_group_key_match(g, key) for g in e[2]))]
10846 if not found:
10847 names = {k: v for e in entries for k, v in e[2].items()}
10848 close = [names[k] for k in difflib.get_close_matches(key, list(names), n=5, cutoff=0.6)]
10849 hint = f"; did you mean {', '.join(close)}?" if close else ""
10850 sys.stderr.write(f"dist_m4ri.py: no help entry for '{t}'{hint} (--morehelp lists all parameters)\n")
10851 status = 1
10852 asked.update(found)
10853 chosen: Set[int] = set(asked)
10854 for g, mem in enumerate(members): # the groups asked for or with a member asked for: the group and its members
10855 if mem is None:
10856 continue
10857 in_group = [i for i, e in enumerate(entries) if members[i] is None and mem & set(e[2])]
10858 if g in asked or asked & set(in_group):
10859 chosen.add(g)
10860 chosen.update(in_group)
10861 out: List[str] = []
10862 section = None
10863 for i in sorted(chosen): # in the order of the full help, under their section headers
10864 sec, lines, _ = entries[i]
10865 if sec != section:
10866 if out:
10867 out.append("")
10868 out.append(sec)
10869 section = sec
10870 out.extend(lines)
10871 if out:
10872 print("\n".join(out), file=file)
10873 return status
10874
10875
10876def _warn_cli_conflicts(args: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:
10877 """
10878 Writes warnings to stderr for the CLI inputs which are ignored. The input is selected in the order fdem (a DEM or
10879 a Stim circuit), Hx / Hz (a CSS code), and finH / finG / finL / fin (one sector of a quantum code, or a classical
10880 code); fin=PREFIX supplies only the missing finH (PREFIX + 'X.mtx') and finG (PREFIX + 'Z.mtx', unless finL). The
10881 disabled options --simple and --full always give a warning (see _warn_disabled_simple_full()), and so does the
10882 expert option irred of the dist_m4ri binary, unless irred=1 (the codewords recorded are always irreducible), and so
10883 do the study options of the binary (steplog, slab_rows, slab_bnd, slab_var, slab_every; see _STUDY_OPTIONS). The
10884 expert option ortho=0 gives a warning here for a DEM or a classical code (for a quantum code, see _warn_ortho()).
10885 """
10886 def given(*keys: str) -> List[str]:
10887 return [k for k in keys if args.get(k) is not None]
10888
10889 _warn_disabled_simple_full(args.get("simple"), args.get("full"), cli=True) # (not passed on)
10890 if args.get("irred") is not None and args["irred"] != 1: # (not passed on: the binary's default irred=1)
10891 _warn_disabled(f"irred={args['irred']} is disabled in the Python interface (ignored: only irreducible "
10892 f"codewords are recorded); use the dist_m4ri binary directly")
10893 for key in _STUDY_OPTIONS: # (not passed on: the study options of the binary, see _STUDY_OPTIONS)
10894 if args.get(key) is not None:
10895 _warn_disabled(f"{key}={args[key]} is disabled in the Python interface (a study option of the dist_m4ri "
10896 f"binary; ignored); use the dist_m4ri binary directly")
10897 for key in _BIN_OUTPUT_OPTIONS: # (not passed on: binary output options, see _BIN_OUTPUT_OPTIONS)
10898 if args.get(key) is not None:
10899 _warn_disabled(f"{key}={args[key]} is disabled in the Python interface (a machine-readable output option "
10900 f"of the dist_m4ri binary; ignored); use the dist_m4ri binary directly")
10901 stim_opts = [opt for opt, on in (("basis=", args.get("basis") is not None),
10902 ("--out-stim", args.get("out_stim") is not None),
10903 ("--p-noise", args.get("p_noise") is not None),
10904 ("--force-noise", bool(args.get("force_noise")))) if on]
10905 warns = []
10906 warned: Set[str] = set() # (the options with a warning: one warning per option, since version 0.17.2)
10907 if args.get("fdem"):
10908 ign = given("finH", "finG", "finL", "fin", "Hx", "Hz", "Lx", "Lz")
10909 if ign:
10910 warns.append(f"fdem={args['fdem']} given: ignoring {', '.join(k + '=' for k in ign)}")
10911 if stim_opts and not str(args["fdem"]).endswith(".stim"):
10912 warns.append(f"{', '.join(stim_opts)}: only used for a Stim circuit (.stim); ignored")
10913 warned.update(stim_opts)
10914 elif (args.get("basis") is not None and str(args.get("drop")).lower() != "css"
10915 and not args.get("verbose")): # (with --verbose, the basis of the classification is reported)
10916 warns.append("basis=: only used with drop=css (the minority-basis detectors of a CSS circuit); ignored")
10917 if args.get("expand") and not (args.get("outC") or args.get("do_cws")):
10918 warns.append("expand=: only used with outC= or --cws; ignored")
10919 warned.add("expand=")
10920 else:
10921 dem_opts = stim_opts + [opt for opt, on in (("--out-dir", args.get("out_dir") is not None),
10922 ("--out-dem", args.get("out_dem") is not None)) if on]
10923 if (args.get("pmin") or 0.0) > 0.0:
10924 dem_opts.append("pmin=")
10925 if args.get("merge") is not None:
10926 dem_opts.append("merge=")
10927 if args.get("expand") is not None:
10928 dem_opts.append("expand=")
10929 if args.get("drop") is not None:
10930 dem_opts.append("drop=")
10931 if args.get("outD") is not None:
10932 dem_opts.append("outD=")
10933 if args.get("out_reduced") is not None:
10934 dem_opts.append("--out-reduced")
10935 if args.get("dem_rounds") is not None:
10936 dem_opts.append("dem_rounds=")
10937 if dem_opts:
10938 warns.append(f"{', '.join(dem_opts)}: only used with fdem= (a DEM or Stim circuit); ignored")
10939 if args.get("Hx") is not None or args.get("Hz") is not None:
10940 ign = given("finH", "finG", "finL", "fin")
10941 if ign:
10942 warns.append(f"Hx=/Hz= given (CSS code): ignoring {', '.join(k + '=' for k in ign)}")
10943 else:
10944 ign = given("Lx", "Lz")
10945 if ign:
10946 warns.append(f"{', '.join(k + '=' for k in ign)}: only used for a CSS code (Hx= and Hz=); ignored")
10947 ign = given("finH", "finG", "finL")
10948 if args.get("fin") is not None and ign:
10949 warns.append(f"fin={args['fin']} together with {', '.join(k + '=' for k in ign)}: the explicit file "
10950 "names take precedence")
10951 css_input = bool(given("Hx", "Hz")) # (Lx and Lz are only used with them)
10952 if args.get("classical") == 1 and (given("finG", "finL", "fin", "fdem", "Hz") or (css_input and given("Lx", "Lz"))):
10953 warns.append("classical=1 ignored: the input is a quantum code or a DEM")
10954 if args.get("ortho") is False: # (a quantum code: compute_quantum_distance() and compute_css_distance() warn)
10955 quantum = bool(given("Hx", "Hz", "finG", "finL", "fin")) or args.get("classical") == 0
10956 if args.get("fdem") or not quantum:
10957 warns.append("ortho=0: only used for a quantum code with G (finG=, fin=, or Hx= and Hz=); ignored")
10958 if args.get("css") is not None:
10959 _warn_disabled(f"css={args['css']} is disabled in the Python interface (CSS codes only; ignored)")
10960 for f in args.get("ignored_files") or []:
10961 warns.append(f"{f}: a positional file which is not used (not a .dem, .stim, .mtx, or .mmx file, or a third "
10962 f"matrix file); ignored")
10963 if args.get("model_lb"): # the code-sized model of a Stim circuit (compute_model_lower_bound())
10964 ign = [opt for opt, on in (("outC=", args.get("outC") is not None), ("finC=", args.get("finC") is not None),
10965 ("--cws", bool(args.get("do_cws")) and args.get("outC") is None),
10966 ("drop=", args.get("drop") is not None),
10967 ("outD=", args.get("outD") is not None),
10968 ("--out-reduced", args.get("out_reduced") is not None),
10969 ("--out-dir", args.get("out_dir") is not None),
10970 ("--out-dem", args.get("out_dem") is not None),
10971 ("--out-stim", args.get("out_stim") is not None),
10972 ("start=", args.get("start") is not None), ("dmin=", bool(args.get("dmin"))),
10973 ("dmax=", bool(args.get("dmax"))), ("dexp=", bool(args.get("dexp"))),

11003def main(argv: Optional[List[str]] = None) -> int:
11004 """
11005 The CLI (see print_cli_help()). With --silent, set_silent() is on during the run, and with --no-cache the distance
11006 cache is disabled (see disable_distance_cache()); both are restored at its end (the cache since version 0.17.2).
11007
11008 Returns:
11009 The exit code: 0 on success, 1 for an invalid argument value (and the help of an unknown parameter), 2 if a
11010 package or library is missing (e.g., qec_cert), the binary is not found or fails, or a file cannot be read or
11011 written (since version 0.17.2; before, a traceback), and 255 for an unrecognized parameter or without an input.
11012 """
11013 report, use_cache = _report_ignored, _use_distance_cache
11014 try:
11015 return _main(argv)
11016 finally:
11017 set_silent(not report)
11018 if use_cache:
11019 enable_distance_cache()
11020 else:
11021 disable_distance_cache()
11022
